…that with which he is at one is the Way; those whom he transforms are the people; and those gradually imbued with his beneficence are all under Heaven and the generations to come. Heaven and the sage cannot be viewed as distinct; hence we call him Heaven. Why need we seek this in accomplishments of a morning or evening, or search for it in the incidental details of material forms and implements?
Taking Guang’s lament over the Tang as my starting point, I have examined the rites and music of that dynasty. From the establishment of its dynastic legacy in the Zhenguan era, there were inward grounds for moral shame, and the rites and music of the inner household fell into disorder. During the Xianqing era, many affairs of government were decided within the palace, and the rites and music of the court were abandoned. One succession later came the abuses of obliquely sealed appointments and ink-written edicts; another succession brought the provocation that summoned rebellion from Yuyang; and another two successions brought the calamity of eunuchs monopolizing government. Surveying the rulers of the Li house of Tang, we find what is meant by establishing a dynastic legacy improperly and having benighted successors: the prevailing tendency would bring down even its very root. This was human action, not Heaven. How could it deserve to be called rites and music?
It is thus no wonder that Sima Guang, with profound concern and far-reaching thought, expounded centrality, rectitude, harmony, and peace, seeking to awaken what is heavenly in the rulers of his own and later ages. Master You said, “The gentleman attends to the root.” Master Zeng said, “This is called knowing the root.” In my humble view, the same may be said of Guang’s words on rites and music. Thus ends this discourse.
Memorial
A memorial composed in the role of a chief councillor of the Song, thanking the emperor for bestowing his poems “Viewing the Crops in Ruisheng Garden” and “Viewing the Wheat South of the City.” Ninth year of the Xiangfu era [1016].
By Liu Juliang.
Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: “Elegant yet observant of proper standards; its unassuming simplicity is delightful.”

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官訓導穆批駢儷中委曲詳盡殆傑作也宜
冠本房
考試官敎諭鄭批沖腴典則四六之擅場者
臣某等言某年月日欽蒙
聖恩特賜瑞聖園觀稼城南觀麥詩者伏以靈
苗瑞實呈異穎於星田
聖藻仙葩捧
宸辭於龍檢啓函拜
賜拭目增榮臣等誠懽誠忭稽首頓首竊惟
===
===
周朝以農事肇國故豳風以七月陳詩多
稼偉曾孫之詠興紀丘園來牟藹后稷之
傳情垂隴畝惟克艱而後罔艱思無逸乃
能有逸迨夫王跡既熄慨矣刪後無詩大
風沛筑念靡及於桑麻夜帳楚歌涕徒悲
於姬侍芝房花萼惟騁雕纖雞塞玉笙虛
工流麗文不在茲時將有待茲蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
禹稼蕃滋
punctuated:
考試官訓導穆批：駢儷中委曲詳盡，殆傑作也，宜冠本房。
考試官敎諭鄭批：沖腴典則，四六之擅場者。
臣某等言：某年月日，欽蒙聖恩，特賜瑞聖園觀稼、城南觀麥詩者。伏以靈苗瑞實，呈異穎於星田；聖藻仙葩，捧宸辭於龍檢。啓函拜賜，拭目增榮。臣等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首。竊惟周朝以農事肇國，故豳風以七月陳詩。多稼偉曾孫之詠，興紀丘園；來牟藹后稷之傳，情垂隴畝。惟克艱而後罔艱，思無逸乃能有逸。迨夫王跡既熄，慨矣刪後無詩。大風沛筑，念靡及於桑麻；夜帳楚歌，涕徒悲於姬侍。芝房花萼，惟騁雕纖；雞塞玉笙，虛工流麗。文不在茲，時將有待。茲蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，禹稼蕃滋，
translation_en:
Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor, comments: Within its parallel phrasing, this is nuanced and comprehensive—surely an outstanding work. It deserves first place in this examining section.
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: Serene yet rich, classically grounded and well regulated: a masterly performance in four-and-six prose.
Your servants, so-and-so and the others, submit: On such-and-such a day, month, and year, we reverently received Your Majesty’s gracious special gift of the poems “Viewing the Crops in Ruisheng Garden” and “Viewing the Wheat South of the City.” We humbly reflect: numinous seedlings and auspicious grain display extraordinary ears in the celestial fields; sage compositions, immortal blossoms—we hold aloft Your imperial words in their dragon-adorned binding. Opening the case, we bow to receive the gift; clearing our eyes to read, we feel our honor increase. We, Your servants, are truly delighted and truly joyful; we bow our heads to the ground and kowtow.
We humbly consider that the Zhou dynasty founded its state upon agriculture; thus the Airs of Bin set forth their verse in “The Seventh Month.” Abundant crops lend grandeur to the song of the royal descendant, its poetic inspiration recording hills and gardens; wheat and barley flourish in the traditions of Hou Ji, their sentiments extending to the furrowed fields. Only by undertaking difficulty can one afterward be free of difficulty; only by remembering to shun ease can one attain ease. When the traces of the true kings had faded, alas, after the editing of the Odes there was no more poetry. The “Great Wind,” with the zhu zither at Pei [?], gave no thought to mulberry or hemp; the songs of Chu in the nighttime tent drew tears merely in grief for a consort. “Fungal Chamber” and “Flower Calyx” merely pursued ornate delicacy; “Chicken Frontier” and “Jade Mouth Organ” [?] vainly perfected flowing elegance. True literary achievement did not reside in these: its time was yet to come.
Now, however, we have humbly encountered 〇〇〇〇 [four circles in the text]: the crops of Yu grow luxuriantly …

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
堯文炳蔚
青宫浴德灼見小人之依
丹詔騰輝獨高大雅之作
妙造化之機軸斵元氣之斧斤
滿心而溢弗出冥搜肆筆以成允為
天縱
湯銘舜典匪直清燕以摛辭孔思周情且乗
逸遊而麗藻
雕輦翠旃時臨內圃
===
珠旗玉軚載駕城南秋實春華欣欣然喜經
御覽銀編金縷洋洋乎揮灑
瓊章一穗兩岐不數張君之詠十畝千石方輕
汜氏之書允矣掩蘭菊於漢篇卓哉越茨
梁於周雅仰符出洛俯陋橫汾
絲綸之寶射奎璧而爭光
菽粟之篇迥琳琅而振響臣等啣
命自
天感恩無地飽百祿之素餐荷十行之
punctuated: 堯文炳蔚，青宫浴德，灼見小人之依；丹詔騰輝，獨高大雅之作。妙造化之機軸，斵元氣之斧斤。滿心而溢弗出，冥搜肆筆以成，允為天縱。湯銘舜典，匪直清燕以摛辭；孔思周情，且乗逸遊而麗藻。雕輦翠旃，時臨內圃；珠旗玉軚，載駕城南。秋實春華，欣欣然喜經御覽；銀編金縷，洋洋乎揮灑瓊章。一穗兩岐，不數張君之詠；十畝千石，方輕汜氏之書。允矣掩蘭菊於漢篇，卓哉越茨梁於周雅。仰符出洛，俯陋橫汾。絲綸之寶，射奎璧而爭光；菽粟之篇，迥琳琅而振響。臣等啣命自天，感恩無地，飽百祿之素餐，荷十行之
translation_en:
…The writings of Yao shine in splendid profusion. Having steeped yourself in virtue in the Palace of the Heir Apparent, you clearly perceived what sustains the common people. Your vermilion edict radiates brilliance; your composition alone rises to the heights of the Greater Odes. You wondrously wield the loom of creation and the axe that shapes primordial vital energy. Filling the heart, it overflows yet does not emerge [?]; through profound searching and freely flowing brushwork, the composition takes form—truly a Heaven-bestowed gift.

Like Tang’s inscription and the Canon of Shun, it is more than an embellishment of language during tranquil leisure; embodying Confucius’s thought and the sentiments of Zhou, it also gives elegant expression to leisurely excursions. Your carved carriage and kingfisher-green banners sometimes approach the inner gardens; with pearl-adorned flags and a jade carriage fitting [?], you ride out south of the city. Autumn fruits and spring blossoms joyfully delight in receiving your imperial gaze; silver-bound volumes and golden threads lavishly display your jade-like compositions.

An ear of grain with two branches: Master Zhang’s verse need no longer be reckoned. A thousand shi of grain from ten mu: the book of Fan now seems slight. Truly, your work eclipses the orchids and chrysanthemums in the Han composition; loftily, it surpasses the thatch and weirs of the Zhou Odes. Above, it accords with the auspicious writing that emerged from the Luo River; below, it makes the song of crossing the Fen River seem paltry. Your precious imperial words vie in radiance with the Kui and Bi constellations; your verses on beans and grain ring out like resonant fine jade [?]. We, your servants, have received our commission from Heaven and can find no means adequate to express our gratitude. Sated with manifold emoluments despite rendering no worthy service, we gratefully receive the ten lines of…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
賜札幸獲窺於
黼黻慚無補於涓埃方將什襲以珍藏至欲
銘心而鏤骨伏願
一人有慶恒先稼穡之艱難
萬壽無疆敢後岡陵之祝頌臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
===
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
馬應羲
同考試官教諭沈批五荅雄贍是策尤偉昔葛文康
謂記問之博當如陶隱居耻一事不知子豈其人歟健羨健羨
考試官訓導穆批其氣充其辭偉佳士也可敬可
服
punctuated:
賜札，幸獲窺於黼黻，慚無補於涓埃。方將什襲以珍藏，至欲銘心而鏤骨。伏願一人有慶，恒先稼穡之艱難；萬壽無疆，敢後岡陵之祝頌？臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁場
策
第一問
馬應羲
同考試官教諭沈批：五荅雄贍，是策尤偉。昔葛文康謂記問之博，當如陶隱居，耻一事不知。子豈其人歟？健羨，健羨！
考試官訓導穆批：其氣充，其辭偉，佳士也！可敬，可服！
translation_en:
…the graciously bestowed letter. Fortunate to glimpse Your Majesty’s literary splendor, we are ashamed that our contribution amounts not even to a droplet or a speck of dust. We shall wrap it in ten layers and treasure it; indeed, we would engrave it upon our hearts and carve it into our bones. We humbly wish that the One Man may enjoy blessings, ever giving first consideration to the hardships of sowing and reaping. May Your Majesty live ten thousand years without end: how could we lag behind in offering wishes for longevity firm as hills and mountains? We, your servants, gaze toward Heaven and look up to the Sage, overcome with fervent emotion and trembling awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our thanks and make them known to Your Majesty.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Ma Yingxi
Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: All five answers are vigorous and richly furnished; this policy essay is especially magnificent. Ge Wenkang once said that, in breadth of remembered learning, one should emulate Tao the Recluse, who considered it shameful not to know even a single matter. Might you be such a man? How I envy you! How I envy you!
Comment by Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor: His vital force is abundant, his diction magnificent. An excellent scholar! Worthy of respect and admiration!

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭鄭批敷腴中度雋氣不羣殆漢唐之
英也高薦何忝
古今能文者多矣必闔闢造化然後足以
爲聖人之藻彩帝王善文者衆矣必經緯
天地然後盡聖人之偉觀粤稽諸古黃竹
白雲垂芳帝籍玉書金簡爲章於天放勳
之文煥有虞舜之歌惟幾殷盤周誥炳若
丹青充棟汗牛不一而足雖崆峒之碑漫
滅石鼓之文脫漏人猶競傳而寶之豈非
===
想陶唐之遺風羨宣王之大雅歟嗣是炎
劉以降趙宋以前誼辟英君代有作者沛
筑形歌唐殿載詠脩辭亦壯矣然未甞思
治念不及民識者少之脩嫮艷冶宫體雕
纖構思若豔矣然溺志嬪御慚德閨闈讀
者憾焉外此非無文也率皆疾風勁草溢
美臣隣賞花釣魚流連光景求其邁殷湯
之晨露掩重華之薫風者寂寥汗青不多
見也洪惟我
punctuated:
考試官教諭鄭批：敷腴中度，雋氣不羣，殆漢唐之英也。高薦何忝？

古今能文者多矣，必闔闢造化，然後足以爲聖人之藻彩。帝王善文者衆矣，必經緯天地，然後盡聖人之偉觀。粤稽諸古，黃竹白雲垂芳帝籍，玉書金簡爲章於天。放勳之文煥，有虞舜之歌惟幾。殷盤周誥，炳若丹青，充棟汗牛，不一而足。雖崆峒之碑漫滅，石鼓之文脫漏，人猶競傳而寶之，豈非想陶唐之遺風，羨宣王之大雅歟？嗣是炎劉以降，趙宋以前，誼辟英君，代有作者。沛筑形歌，唐殿載詠，脩辭亦壯矣，然未甞思治，念不及民，識者少之。脩嫮艷冶，宫體雕纖，構思若豔矣，然溺志嬪御，慚德閨闈，讀者憾焉。外此非無文也，率皆疾風勁草，溢美臣隣；賞花釣魚，流連光景。求其邁殷湯之晨露，掩重華之薫風者，寂寥汗青，不多見也。洪惟我
translation_en:
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “Full and rich, yet within proper bounds; its outstanding spirit sets it apart. Here, surely, is a talent worthy of the Han and Tang. What could be unmerited in recommending him highly?”

Many, ancient and modern, have been skilled in writing. Yet only by encompassing the opening and closing of creation can their writing adequately serve as the sage’s literary adornment. Many emperors and kings have excelled in writing. Yet only by ordering heaven and earth can their writing fully display the sage’s grandeur. Looking back into antiquity, Yellow Bamboo and White Clouds left their fragrance in the imperial records; jade writings and gold tablets formed patterns in heaven. Fangxun’s literary accomplishment shone brilliantly, and the songs of Shun of Youyu concerned the subtle beginnings of affairs. The Shang’s Pan Geng and the Zhou proclamations gleamed like vermilion and blue pigments. Such writings filled buildings and made the oxen hauling them sweat: no single enumeration could exhaust them. Although the inscription at Kongtong has worn away and characters in the Stone Drum inscriptions are missing, people still vie to transmit and treasure them. Is this not because they yearn for the surviving influence of Taotang and admire the great elegance of King Xuan?

Thereafter, from the Liu house of Han down to the time before the Zhao house of Song, worthy sovereigns and illustrious rulers produced writings in every age. The zither at Pei found expression in song, and the Tang palace resounded with verse. Their diction was indeed magnificent; yet they never gave thought to good government, nor did their concern extend to the people, so discerning critics held them in low esteem. Elaborate beauty and seductive ornament, the intricate delicacy of palace-style verse—their conceptions seemed dazzling. Yet their aspirations were submerged in attachment to consorts and attendants, and their conduct within the inner chambers brought shame upon their virtue, leaving readers disappointed. Beyond these, writings were certainly not lacking. Most, however, merely praised ministers extravagantly as ‘sturdy grass in a strong wind,’ or lingered over scenery while enjoying flowers and fishing. If one seeks works surpassing the Morning Dew of Tang of Shang or eclipsing the Fragrant Wind of Chonghua, the historical record is sparse: few are to be found. Reverently considering our …

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝德侔天地道冠黃虞值奎壁宿聚〔文運〕
之開紹帝王垂絕之統萬幾之暇作為文
章挾雲漢之黼黻濯江漢之濤瀾易簡之
訓範圍兩儀昭回之光賁飾萬物猗歟盛
哉愚嘗拜觀
國初儒英之仰讚
御製文集之珍傳而窺其萬一矣請略陳之
登極之詔所以嚴華夷之防
大祀之文所以謹郊禋之禮
===
皇陵之碑述創業之艱難兗公之敕崇聖賢之
苗裔答
御殿之表而宰臣之體貌以隆草靖江之詔而
宮僚之責任斯重平蜀之製則昭旂常之
日月鐵券之文則錄佐
命之功庸誥湯和誥沐英尚元勳也誥李祺誥
黃琛貴戚里也勸農桑免租稅則后稷稼
穡之教也諭安南詔高麗則周王薄伐之
仁也誦循環之論而天道昭讀閱江之記
punctuated: 太祖高皇帝德侔天地，道冠黃虞，值奎壁宿聚〔文運〕之開，紹帝王垂絕之統。萬幾之暇，作為文章，挾雲漢之黼黻，濯江漢之濤瀾。易簡之訓，範圍兩儀；昭回之光，賁飾萬物。猗歟盛哉！愚嘗拜觀國初儒英之仰讚、御製文集之珍傳，而窺其萬一矣。請略陳之：登極之詔，所以嚴華夷之防；大祀之文，所以謹郊禋之禮；皇陵之碑，述創業之艱難；兗公之敕，崇聖賢之苗裔。答御殿之表，而宰臣之體貌以隆；草靖江之詔，而宮僚之責任斯重。平蜀之製，則昭旂常之日月；鐵券之文，則錄佐命之功庸。誥湯和，誥沐英，尚元勳也；誥李祺，誥黃琛，貴戚里也。勸農桑，免租稅，則后稷稼穡之教也；諭安南，詔高麗，則周王薄伐之仁也。誦循環之論而天道昭，讀閱江之記
translation_en:
… Emperor Taizu Gao, whose virtue equaled Heaven and Earth and whose Way surpassed those of Huangdi and Shun, came upon the opening of an age when the Kui and Bi constellations gathered together [?]〔the fortunes of literary culture〕, and continued the succession of emperors and kings when it was on the verge of extinction. Amid the countless affairs of government, he found leisure to compose writings. These bore the embroidered splendor of the Milky Way and were washed in the surging waters of the Yangzi and Han. His teachings of ease and simplicity encompassed Heaven and Earth; their radiant light adorned all things. Ah, how magnificent! I have reverently read the admiring praises of the outstanding scholars of the dynasty’s founding years and the treasured, transmitted collection of imperially composed writings, and have thereby glimpsed one ten-thousandth of their excellence. Allow me to set this out briefly.

His accession edict enforced the distinction between the Chinese and the outer peoples; his text for the great sacrifice ensured care in the rites of suburban sacrifice to Heaven. His inscription for the imperial mausoleum recounted the hardships of founding the dynasty; his edict to the Duke of Yan honored the descendants of sages and worthies. By answering the memorial concerning his taking his place in the imperial hall, he enhanced the honor accorded his chief ministers; by drafting the edict concerning Jingjiang, he gave greater weight to the responsibilities of the princely palace officials. His composition on the pacification of Shu displayed achievements as brilliant as the sun and moon upon the commemorative banners; the text of his iron patent recorded the meritorious service of those who assisted in establishing his rule. His proclamations to Tang He and Mu Ying honored the founding meritorious servants; those to Li Qi and Huang Chen ennobled the imperial relatives. In encouraging agriculture and sericulture and remitting taxes, he followed Hou Ji’s teaching of husbandry; in admonishing Annan and issuing an edict to Gaoli, he displayed the benevolence of the Zhou king’s limited punitive campaigns. Recite his Discourse on Cyclical Return, and the Way of Heaven becomes clear; read his Record of the River-Viewing Tower …

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而輿圖正水旱之說成而堯湯之心慰矣
伯夷之頌駁而韓柳之見卑矣秋宇澄清
之製姚姒之英藻也沛邑之歌寧不當北
面哉黃河良馬之文姬周之傑作也橫汾
之詠寧不拜下風哉
列聖相承天葩輝映迨今
皇上法
祖崇文頒繼統之詔而
大禮明降分祀之制而
===
===
大祭謹
敬一有箴髣髴唐虞精一之學也洪範有序
依稀夏禹九疇之演也
欽天有記聖王嚴恭之懿矩也緝熈之美不再
見耶四箴有註孔門傳授之心法也敬止
之風曾是加耶
睿製奎章崢嶸
秘府播之寰宇人誦家傳雖嵩衡岱華不足
以為高黃鍾大呂不足以為清大哉
punctuated:
而輿圖正。水旱之說成，而堯湯之心慰矣；伯夷之頌駁，而韓柳之見卑矣。《秋宇澄清》之製，姚姒之英藻也；沛邑之歌，寧不當北面哉？黃河、良馬之文，姬周之傑作也；橫汾之詠，寧不拜下風哉？
列聖相承，天葩輝映。迨今皇上法祖崇文，頒繼統之詔而大禮明，降分祀之制而大祭謹。敬一有箴，髣髴唐虞精一之學也；洪範有序，依稀夏禹九疇之演也。欽天有記，聖王嚴恭之懿矩也，緝熈之美不再見耶？四箴有註，孔門傳授之心法也，敬止之風曾是加耶？
睿製奎章，崢嶸秘府，播之寰宇，人誦家傳。雖嵩衡岱華不足以為高，黃鍾大呂不足以為清。大哉！
translation_en:
…and the map of the realm is set right. When the explanation of floods and droughts was completed, the concerns of Yao and Tang were assuaged; when the eulogy of Bo Yi was refuted, the views of Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan were shown to be inferior. The composition Autumn Skies, Clear and Pure displays the splendid literary gifts of Shun and Yu. Should not the song of Pei bow northward before it as a subject? The writings on the Yellow River and the fine horse are masterpieces worthy of the Zhou rulers of the Ji clan. Should not the poem on crossing the Fen River acknowledge their superiority?
The successive sage emperors carried on the tradition, their heavenly blossoms of writing illuminating one another. Now His Majesty follows his ancestors and honors letters. By promulgating the edict on succeeding to the imperial line, he clarified the Great Rites; by issuing the decree on separate sacrifices, he ensured meticulous observance of the great sacrifices. His Admonition on Revering Unity recalls the learning of Yao and Shun concerning refinement and single-mindedness. His preface to the Great Plan recalls Yu of Xia’s exposition of the Nine Categories. His Record of Revering Heaven provides an admirable model of a sage king’s solemn reverence: is not the excellence of continuing and broadening luminous virtue seen once again? His commentary on the Four Admonitions conveys the teaching of the mind transmitted within the school of Confucius: could the tradition of abiding in reverence surpass this?
His sagely compositions, writings radiant as the literary constellation Kui, tower in the palace repositories and circulate throughout the world, recited by individuals and handed down in households. Even the mountains Song, Heng, Dai, and Hua cannot match their loftiness; even the Huangzhong and Dalü pitch standards cannot match their purity of tone. Great indeed …

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
王言眞有以追
皇祖之遐軌攀
列聖之逸駕矣於戲
堯言炳煥而如見
聖謨灝噩而孔彰愚也惟晝誦而味夜思而求
耳若廼鋪張對
天之洪休揚厲無前之偉績則自有文學供奉
之賢在草茅何足以語此幸執事進而敎
之
===
第二問
段有成
同考試官敎諭戴 批 五葉涉筆敷陳直言不費探索
而斷選處深識講筵要領殆老成之見也一薦何忝
考試官訓導穆 批 結末數言足覘忠悃高選允宜
考試官敎諭鄭 批 講筵顛末歷述瞻明是胷中有
書笥者
覽說命之書而後見講讀之所始披帝學
之篇而後知講筵之甚重何哉商周盛時
punctuated:
王言，眞有以追皇祖之遐軌，攀列聖之逸駕矣。於戲！堯言炳煥而如見，聖謨灝噩而孔彰。愚也惟晝誦而味，夜思而求耳。若廼鋪張對天之洪休，揚厲無前之偉績，則自有文學供奉之賢在，草茅何足以語此？幸執事進而敎之。

第二問
段有成

同考試官敎諭戴批：五葉涉筆敷陳，直言不費探索，而斷選處深識講筵要領，殆老成之見也。一薦何忝？
考試官訓導穆批：結末數言，足覘忠悃，高選允宜。
考試官敎諭鄭批：講筵顛末，歷述瞻明，是胷中有書笥者。

覽《說命》之書，而後見講讀之所始；披《帝學》之篇，而後知講筵之甚重。何哉？商周盛時，
translation_en:
…the royal words truly enable Your Majesty to follow the lofty course of the imperial ancestor and draw alongside the swift carriages of the successive sage sovereigns. Ah! The words of Yao shine brilliantly, as though before our eyes; the sage counsels, vast and majestic, are most clearly manifest. In my ignorance, I can only recite them by day to savor their meaning and ponder them by night to seek understanding. As for fully setting forth the immense blessings received from Heaven and extolling achievements without precedent, there are worthy men of letters serving at court for that purpose. How could a man of the countryside presume to speak of these things? I hope that you, honored examiner, will favor me with further instruction.

Second Policy Question
Duan Youcheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Dai, Instructor: Across five leaves, he develops his account in straightforward language that requires no laborious probing. At the point of judgment and selection [?], he shows a profound understanding of the essentials of the imperial lectures—surely the insight of a mature scholar. How could recommending him bring any discredit?

Comment by Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor: The few concluding remarks suffice to reveal his loyal sincerity. Selection for a high place is entirely fitting.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: He recounts the imperial lectures from beginning to end, comprehensively and clearly [?]. Here is a man with a whole library stored in his breast.

Only after reading the chapter “The Charge to Yue” (Yue ming) does one perceive the origins of lecturing and reading before the emperor; only after opening Imperial Learning (Di xue) does one understand the great importance of the imperial lectures. Why is this so? In the flourishing days of the Shang and Zhou…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
哲王世有師氏之職同與膳夫掖廷外朝
統於冢宰師保疑丞之外保氏史官之餘
靡人非賢靡地非學於戲至矣降而漢唐
古意寖失出入禁庭講論經學者似榮矣
然望之名儒出補外郡石顯憸巧播弄秘
庭白虎石渠之講讀果能不變其初耶横
經帝幄紬繹陳編者似善矣然梨園之樂
汨亂聰明寧王之笛轉移心術集賢書院
之講學果能無改其舊耶甚者尚書樸學
===
厭而不好博士倚席廢而弗講駸乎無以
議爲也迨夫宋室奎璧騰輝人文滋盛英
君誼辟銳意講筵勸學有所講讀有官以
水喻政得之小旻烹鮮喻治得之匪風善
詩學也薄征緩刑荒政論之脩德承天視
祲議之探禮學也上承下施蓋取諸鼎亂
極生治蓋取諸萃易學明也讀說命之篇
而三句特誦講五子之歌而六句再陳書
學深也論魯封疆講鄭鑄刑容非邃於春
punctuated: 哲王世有師氏之職，同與膳夫、掖廷、外朝統於冢宰。師保疑丞之外，保氏史官之餘，靡人非賢，靡地非學。於戲，至矣！降而漢唐，古意寖失。出入禁庭、講論經學者似榮矣，然望之名儒，出補外郡；石顯憸巧，播弄秘庭。白虎、石渠之講讀，果能不變其初耶？横經帝幄、紬繹陳編者似善矣，然梨園之樂汨亂聰明，寧王之笛轉移心術。集賢書院之講學，果能無改其舊耶？甚者，《尚書》樸學，厭而不好；博士倚席，廢而弗講，駸乎無以議爲也。迨夫宋室，奎璧騰輝，人文滋盛。英君誼辟銳意講筵，勸學有所，講讀有官。以水喻政，得之《小旻》；烹鮮喻治，得之《匪風》，善詩學也。薄征緩刑，《荒政》論之；脩德承天，《視祲》議之，探禮學也。上承下施，蓋取諸《鼎》；亂極生治，蓋取諸《萃》，易學明也。讀《說命》之篇，而三句特誦；講《五子之歌》，而六句再陳，書學深也。論魯封疆，講鄭鑄刑，容非邃於春
translation_en:
…In the age of wise kings there was the office of Preceptor, which, together with the Provisioner, the palace service, and the outer court, came under the Grand Steward. Beyond the preceptors, guardians, advisers, and assistants, and besides the guardians and historiographers, there was no person who was not worthy and no place that was not devoted to learning. Ah, how consummate this was!

By the Han and Tang dynasties, the ancient spirit was gradually lost. Those who entered and left the forbidden court to expound classical learning seemed honored. Yet Wangzhi, a renowned Confucian scholar, was sent out to fill a provincial post, while the deceitful and crafty Shi Xian manipulated affairs within the palace. Could the lectures and readings at the White Tiger Hall and Stone Canal Pavilion truly have preserved their original purpose? Those who spread out the Classics before the imperial seat and drew out the meanings of ancient texts seemed to be doing well. Yet the music of the Pear Garden clouded the ruler’s discernment, and the Prince of Ning’s flute diverted his mind. Could the lectures at the Academy of Scholarly Worthies truly have continued unchanged? Worse still, plain scholarship on the Book of Documents was disliked and rejected; the Erudites’ lecture mats were set aside, and lectures ceased. Matters deteriorated beyond discussion [?].

When the Song dynasty arose, the literary stars Kui and Bi shone brilliantly, and literary culture flourished increasingly. Outstanding rulers and righteous sovereigns devoted themselves earnestly to court lectures. There were places for encouraging learning and officials charged with lecturing and reading. They drew from “Lesser Heaven” (Xiao Min) the use of water as an analogy for government, and from “Not the Wind” (Fei Feng) the use of cooking small fish as an analogy for governing: this was proficiency in the study of the Book of Odes. They discussed light taxation and lenient punishments through “Measures for Famine Relief” (Huang Zheng), and the cultivation of virtue in obedience to Heaven through “Observer of Portents” (Shi Jin): this was an exploration of ritual learning. Receiving from above and bestowing below was a principle drawn from the hexagram “The Cauldron” (Ding); order arising when disorder reaches its extreme was drawn from “Gathering” (Cui): this showed clarity in the study of the Book of Changes. When reading “The Charge to Yue” (Shuo Ming), three sentences were singled out for recitation; when lecturing on “The Songs of the Five Sons,” six sentences were presented again: this showed depth in the study of the Book of Documents. They discussed the boundaries of Lu and expounded Zheng’s casting of its penal laws in metal. Could this fail to show profound understanding of the Spring…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
秋者歟中庸脩身大學入德容非優於記
禮者歟噫趙宋講筵有光帝學固可稱矣
然比隆商周賢聖繼作者則槩乎未之見
也恭惟我
皇祖甫入建康禮賢創舘首徵儒碩訪治談經
列聖相承講筵增重夷攷其時自微言以及大
政皆謀議之所先自公卿以及將吏皆咨
訪之所及宫僚之議參之兩府藩屏之建
謀之侍臣桂彥良帝王心法之言則蒙
===
帝師之褒宋𤅀旨帝王傳心之論致動
天顏之喜祭酒吳顒次第進講則訓以中正之
道待制王禕進講大學則諭以德本之言
聞解縉正心之講而
睿覽至再喜士奇堯典之陳而稱善又之講乾
之九四以儲貳為言則學士王達之見敏
也纂周易直指而備述本義則學士楊士
奇之論詳也留
神乙夜數御講筵春坊講章內閣改正尚書
punctuated:
秋者歟？中庸脩身，大學入德，容非優於記禮者歟？噫！趙宋講筵有光帝學，固可稱矣。然比隆商周，賢聖繼作者，則槩乎未之見也。
恭惟我皇祖甫入建康，禮賢創舘，首徵儒碩，訪治談經。列聖相承，講筵增重。夷攷其時，自微言以及大政，皆謀議之所先；自公卿以及將吏，皆咨訪之所及。宫僚之議，參之兩府；藩屏之建，謀之侍臣。桂彥良帝王心法之言，則蒙帝師之褒；宋𤅀旨帝王傳心之論，致動天顏之喜。祭酒吳顒次第進講，則訓以中正之道；待制王禕進講大學，則諭以德本之言。聞解縉正心之講，而睿覽至再；喜士奇堯典之陳，而稱善又之。講乾之九四，以儲貳為言，則學士王達之見敏也；纂周易直指，而備述本義，則學士楊士奇之論詳也。留神乙夜，數御講筵。春坊講章，內閣改正。尚書
translation_en:
…the Spring and Autumn Annals? In cultivating oneself through the Doctrine of the Mean and entering into virtue through the Great Learning, could they have failed to excel in the Record of Rites? Ah! The lecture mat of the Zhao Song dynasty lent lustre to imperial learning and certainly deserves praise. Yet anything comparable to the flourishing of Shang and Zhou, when worthy and sagely rulers succeeded one another, was, broadly speaking, nowhere to be seen.
We reverently consider how our imperial ancestor, upon first entering Jiankang, honoured worthy men and established a hall, first summoning eminent Confucian scholars to consult them on government and discuss the classics. Successive sage emperors carried this forward, giving ever greater weight to the imperial lectures. Examining those times, we find that everything from subtle teachings to major affairs of government received priority in deliberation, and everyone from dukes and ministers to military commanders and officers was consulted. Proposals concerning palace personnel were referred to the two councils; the establishment of princely bulwarks was discussed with attendant ministers. Gui Yanliang’s remarks on the methods of the mind practised by emperors and kings earned him praise as a teacher of the emperor. Song [𤅀旨, name garbled?] discussed the transmission of the mind among emperors and kings, bringing joy to the imperial countenance. When Wu Yong, Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, presented his lectures in sequence, the emperor instructed him in the Way of centrality and correctness. When Wang Yi, an Expectant Official, lectured on the Great Learning, the emperor admonished him with words about virtue as the root. On hearing Xie Jin’s lecture on rectifying the mind, the emperor read it twice; delighted by Shiqi’s exposition of the Canon of Yao, he praised it again [?]. Academician Wang Da showed keen insight when, lecturing on the fourth nine of the hexagram Qian, he spoke in terms of the heir apparent. Academician Yang Shiqi’s discussion was comprehensive when he compiled Direct Explanation of the Changes of Zhou and fully expounded its original meaning [also the title of Zhu Xi’s commentary]. The emperor devoted his attention to study during the second watch of the night and frequently attended the imperial lectures. Lecture texts from the Secretariat of the Heir Apparent were revised by the Grand Secretariat. The Book of Documents…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
毛詩則解縉胡廣專閱焉經術何銳情也
周易春秋則幼孜士奇更覽焉古訓何探
賾也是誠以講學為治本以聖賢為家法
矣迨我
皇上察倫明物法
祖右文經筵日講而不間夫寒暑隨處用力而
靡二於宫庭隆體貌於細旃究心原於古
訓垂
敬一之旨衍四箴之義示學宫也正孔子先
===
師之號抑廣孝配享之非昭禮樂也雖商
宗之監成憲成王之酌祖道不是過矣一
何盛哉執事倘與薦焉則進陽爻退陰位
如昭素之辨乾龍闢君子闔小人若馮元
之推泰象尚當於
丹陛下陳之
第三問
楊茂時
同考試官訓導許批五策明實可錄而是篇尤為警策
punctuated:
毛詩，則解縉、胡廣專閱焉，經術何銳情也！周易、春秋，則幼孜、士奇更覽焉，古訓何探賾也！是誠以講學為治本，以聖賢為家法矣。迨我皇上察倫明物，法祖右文，經筵日講而不間夫寒暑，隨處用力而靡二於宫庭，隆體貌於細旃，究心原於古訓，垂敬一之旨，衍四箴之義，示學宫也；正孔子先師之號，抑廣孝配享之非，昭禮樂也。雖商宗之監成憲，成王之酌祖道，不是過矣。一何盛哉！執事倘與薦焉，則進陽爻、退陰位，如昭素之辨乾龍；闢君子、闔小人，若馮元之推泰象，尚當於丹陛下陳之。
第三問
楊茂時
同考試官訓導許批：五策明實可錄，而是篇尤為警策。
translation_en:
…As for the Mao Book of Odes, Xie Jin and Hu Guang were assigned to review it: how keen was the devotion to classical learning! As for the Book of Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals, Youzi and Shiqi reviewed them in turn: how deeply were the ancient teachings explored! This was truly to make the exposition and study of learning the foundation of government, and the sages and worthies the models of the imperial house.
Coming to our present Emperor, he examines human relationships and clarifies the principles of things, follows his ancestors, and honors cultured learning. The Classics Colloquium and daily lectures continue without interruption through cold and heat; he applies himself wherever he is, with undivided commitment within the palace. He accords lofty ceremonial respect to the lecturers upon their fine felt mats and probes the foundations of the mind through ancient teachings. He has issued his injunction on reverent concentration and elaborated the meaning of the Four Admonitions to instruct the schools. He has rectified Confucius’s title as First Teacher and rejected the impropriety of Guangxiao’s sharing in the sacrifices, thereby making rites and music manifest. Even the Shang ancestral king’s observance of established statutes and King Cheng’s consideration of his ancestors’ way did not surpass this. How splendid indeed!
If you, sir, should include me among those recommended, I shall yet present before the vermilion steps an exposition on advancing the yang lines and withdrawing the yin positions, like Zhaosu’s discrimination of the dragons in the Qian hexagram; and on admitting gentlemen and excluding petty men, like Feng Yuan’s elucidation of the imagery of the Tai hexagram.
Third Policy Question
Yang Maoshi
Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor: “The five policy essays are clear and substantive, and merit selection; this piece is especially incisive…”

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
策手也何惜高薦
考試官訓導穆批藻彩溢出而典則𢎞中度是善場
厲者取之
考試官教諭鄭批周悉之見忠厚之言允宜錄出
以範來學
詠行葦之詩則知壽耇之當崇佩中庸之
旨則知臣工之宜體此三代之家法萬世
之懿矩也況開創之主其佐命之臣冒矢
石而不辭處風波而自任艱難備嘗茂著
===
勞烈功成之後謂宜貌敬心孚終始一致
而崇德報功可也奈何商周不作識者憾
焉犬馬土芥致歎軻書騎項溺冠貽譏青
史誅秦蹙項淮陰之績偉矣而卒招狗烹
之恨填國撫民酇侯之功高矣而未免械
繫之羞麟閣不名大臣之至禮也未幾而
有赤族之慘凌烟賦詩宰衡之至愛也無
何而形仆碑之咎迺若中令元勳鼎鐺有
耳魏公宿德倚重長城溥筦疾瘳而爵賞
punctuated:
策手也，何惜高薦？
考試官訓導穆批：藻彩溢出，而典則𢎞中度，是善場厲者，取之。
考試官教諭鄭批：周悉之見，忠厚之言，允宜錄出，以範來學。
詠《行葦》之詩，則知壽耇之當崇；佩《中庸》之旨，則知臣工之宜體。此三代之家法，萬世之懿矩也。況開創之主，其佐命之臣，冒矢石而不辭，處風波而自任，艱難備嘗，茂著勞烈。功成之後，謂宜貌敬心孚，終始一致，而崇德報功可也。奈何商周不作，識者憾焉！犬馬土芥，致歎軻書；騎項溺冠，貽譏青史。誅秦蹙項，淮陰之績偉矣，而卒招狗烹之恨；填國撫民，酇侯之功高矣，而未免械繫之羞。麟閣不名，大臣之至禮也，未幾而有赤族之慘；凌烟賦詩，宰衡之至愛也，無何而形仆碑之咎。迺若中令元勳，鼎鐺有耳；魏公宿德，倚重長城。溥筦疾瘳，而爵賞
translation_en:
…a master of policy essays! Why hesitate to recommend him highly?
Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor, comments: Literary brilliance shines forth, while the classical standards are broadly embodied and due measure observed. This is an accomplished contender in the examination arena [?]; select him.
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: Comprehensive insights and words of loyalty and generosity: this certainly deserves to be recorded as a model for future students.
Reciting the poem “Thick Grow the Reeds” teaches us that the aged should be honored; taking to heart the meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean teaches us that officials should be treated with consideration. These were the ancestral rules of the Three Dynasties and admirable standards for all ages. How much more does this apply to founding rulers! The ministers who assisted their rise braved arrows and stones without demur, shouldered responsibility amid turmoil, experienced every hardship, and distinguished themselves through service and achievement. Once their work was accomplished, surely they deserved outward respect and inward trust, maintained consistently from beginning to end, so that virtue was honored and service rewarded. Alas, the ways of Shang and Zhou were not revived, to the regret of discerning men!
Treating ministers as dogs and horses, or as dirt and weeds, occasioned lament in the book of Meng Ke; riding upon a man’s neck and urinating into a cap left grounds for censure in the histories. In overthrowing Qin and bringing Xiang Yu to bay, the achievements of the Marquis of Huaiyin were great, yet he ultimately suffered the bitterness of the hunting dog boiled once its work was done. In securing the state and reassuring its people, the merits of the Marquis of Zan were lofty, yet he did not escape the humiliation of being put in fetters.
To omit a minister’s personal name from the Qilin Pavilion was the utmost courtesy toward a great minister; yet before long came the calamity of the extermination of his clan. Composing a poem at Lingyan Pavilion expressed the utmost affection for a chief minister; yet soon afterward came the reprehensible act of toppling his commemorative stele.
Then there was the Director of the Secretariat, a founding minister of outstanding merit, and the saying, “Even cauldrons and cooking pots have ears”; and the Duke of Wei, a man of long-established virtue, relied upon as a Great Wall. When Pu Guan [?] recovered from illness, titles and rewards were bestowed…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
醫工夷簡抱病而剪鬚親賜其體貌之尊
崇禮意之優渥固未能同符商周聖武之
君其視漢唐刻薄之主則彼善於此矣仰
惟
皇祖龍飛淮甸鹿逐胡元以忠孝為家法以禮
義為國維元勳碩德既崇爵於土龍既禱
之餘
縟典盛儀復追報於喬木見思之日中山不
禄則欷歔而流涕開平櫬至則痛哭而拊
===
膺武靖之功竒矣不以甥舅之貴戚而或
掩良禎之績茂矣不以兄弟之并用而見
疑稱吾子房而不名重劉基也
賜百歲之衣而慰藉禮宋濂也俞忠烈病革則
曰平章知予問疾乎天性骨肉之恩不是
加也郭靖海起避則曰第坐不汝關焉家
人父子之愛不是過也覽竹帛之舊績而
六王之元祀以崇龍蛇一章不媿汙於茲
耶勒鼎彝之前勳而列侯之爵以厚弓藏
punctuated:
醫工；夷簡抱病，而剪鬚親賜。其體貌之尊崇，禮意之優渥，固未能同符商周聖武之君；其視漢唐刻薄之主，則彼善於此矣。
仰惟皇祖龍飛淮甸，鹿逐胡元，以忠孝為家法，以禮義為國維。元勳碩德，既崇爵於土龍既禱之餘；縟典盛儀，復追報於喬木見思之日。中山不禄，則欷歔而流涕；開平櫬至，則痛哭而拊膺。武靖之功竒矣，不以甥舅之貴戚而或掩；良禎之績茂矣，不以兄弟之并用而見疑。稱吾子房而不名，重劉基也；賜百歲之衣而慰藉，禮宋濂也。俞忠烈病革，則曰：「平章知予問疾乎？」天性骨肉之恩，不是加也。郭靖海起避，則曰：「第坐，不汝關焉。」家人父子之愛，不是過也。覽竹帛之舊績，而六王之元祀以崇，龍蛇一章不媿汙於茲耶？勒鼎彝之前勳，而列侯之爵以厚，弓藏
translation_en:
…the physician; when Yijian fell ill, the emperor cut off some of his own beard and personally bestowed it upon him. Such esteem for their standing and such generous ceremonial regard could certainly not match that of the sage and martial rulers of Shang and Zhou. Yet compared with the harsh rulers of Han and Tang, these were better.
We reverently reflect that our imperial ancestor rose like a dragon from the Huai region and contested dominion with the non-Han Yuan. He made loyalty and filial piety the guiding principles of his house, and ritual propriety and righteousness the foundations of his state. He honored men of founding merit and eminent virtue with exalted ranks after prayers to the earthen dragon had been offered [?]; and, when the sight of their lofty trees prompted remembrance, he again repaid their service posthumously with elaborate rites and splendid ceremonies. When Zhongshan died, he sobbed and shed tears; when Kaiping’s coffin arrived, he wept bitterly and beat his breast. Wujing’s achievements were extraordinary: their brilliance was never obscured by his privileged kinship as the emperor’s nephew. Liang and Zhen’s accomplishments were outstanding: they incurred no suspicion because both brothers held office together. Calling Liu Ji “my Zifang” rather than using his personal name expressed his esteem for him. Bestowing a robe for a hundred years of life upon Song Lian, with words of consolation, expressed his respect for him. When Yu Zhonglie was critically ill, he said, “Does the Manager of Governmental Affairs know that I have inquired after his illness?” Even the natural affection between blood relatives could add nothing to this. When Guo, Lord Jinghai, rose to withdraw, he said, “Just remain seated; this does not concern you.” Even the affection between father and son within a household could not surpass this. Reviewing the past achievements recorded on bamboo and silk, he exalted the principal sacrifices to the six princes. Would not the ‘Dragon and Snake’ song be ashamed to sully such a record [?]? Inscribing their former merits on ceremonial bronze vessels, he enriched the ranks of the marquises; the bow put away…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
數語不報容於是耶若迺韓成之委身紀
信之誑楚也孫炎之罵賊巡遠之流亞也
忠節諸臣不一而足血食廟貌冊府增光
於戲厚矣矧金書鐵券
天藻輝煌帶礪河山爵及苗裔所謂洽魚水於
一堂慶雲龍於千載我
皇祖以之矣愚也食粟而憶稷踐土而思禹於
我
皇祖君臣丕天之功自知不能摹乾坤繪日月
===
而揄揚其萬一矣謹摭拾以爲明問復
第四問
黨宗正
考試官訓導穆批評隲歷代史才如指諸掌而結
末斷案歸美兩得之强學待問者也讀之終篇不覺斂衽
考試官教諭鄭批博極羣書邃於史學主司得子
可以自慶矣
事紀於儒臣之筆者可以史名事定於聖
人之筆者當以經論自有載籍以來芸編
punctuated:
數語不報容於是耶？若迺韓成之委身，紀信之誑楚也；孫炎之罵賊，巡遠之流亞也。忠節諸臣，不一而足；血食廟貌，冊府增光。於戲，厚矣！矧金書鐵券，天藻輝煌，帶礪河山，爵及苗裔。所謂洽魚水於一堂，慶雲龍於千載，我皇祖以之矣。愚也食粟而憶稷，踐土而思禹，於我皇祖君臣丕天之功，自知不能摹乾坤、繪日月，而揄揚其萬一矣。謹摭拾以爲明問復。

第四問
黨宗正
考試官訓導穆批：評隲歷代史才，如指諸掌，而結末斷案、歸美兩得之，强學待問者也。讀之終篇，不覺斂衽。
考試官教諭鄭批：博極羣書，邃於史學，主司得子，可以自慶矣。

事紀於儒臣之筆者，可以史名；事定於聖人之筆者，當以經論。自有載籍以來，芸編
translation_en:
…could those few words find any place here [?]? As for Han Cheng’s sacrifice of himself, it was like Ji Xin’s deception of Chu; Sun Yan’s denunciation of the rebels placed him in the company of Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan. The loyal and steadfast ministers were too numerous to enumerate. They receive blood sacrifices in their temples, and their deeds add lustre to the imperial records. Ah, how generous were these honors! Moreover, the gold-inscribed iron certificates shone with the brilliance of imperial writing; their promises endured until the rivers became narrow as belts and the mountains small as whetstones, and noble rank extended to their descendants. What is called the harmony of fish and water within a single hall, and the felicitous meeting of cloud and dragon across a thousand years—our Imperial Progenitor achieved it!

In my humble ignorance, when I eat grain I remember Ji, and when I tread the earth I think of Yu. As for the Heaven-vast achievements of our Imperial Progenitor and his ministers, I know that I cannot portray Heaven and Earth or depict the sun and moon so as to praise even one ten-thousandth of them. I have respectfully gathered these few details in reply to your discerning question.

Fourth Question
Dang Zongzheng

Comment by Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor: His assessments of historical talent through successive ages are as clear as pointing to his own palm. In his conclusion, he succeeds both in delivering a verdict and in rendering praise where it is due. He is one who studies diligently and stands ready to answer questions. On reading the whole piece, I could not help straightening my robes in respect.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: His reading ranges through the whole multitude of books, and his knowledge of historical scholarship is profound. An examination official who finds such a candidate may congratulate himself.

Events recorded by the pens of Confucian ministers may be called history; events given definitive judgment by the pen of a sage should be treated as a Classic. Ever since written records first existed, rue-scented volumes…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
蠹簡浩穰滿家史法相沿代有作者溫純
如左氏簡潔如子長雄健如孟堅是誠史
家之魯殿靈光而巋然者也然其才氣之
所充規模之所就要之所謂多聞習事而
猶未能離乎史也迺若朱子綱目之作發
宣尼之蘊成一家之言雖未敢擬經中之
史亦可謂史中之經矣此我
憲皇所以特命儒英法之而有續通鑑綱目之
書也請陳其槩而執事擇焉可乎蓋嘗攷
===
之書者古史也帝王之軌範政治之權輿
所從出也聖人從而定焉芟繁亂而剪浮
辭自唐虞而訖成周大經大法曉然而易
遵坦然而易行由是觀之則書非孔子莫
能定矣請米而作佳傳者豈能為其廝養
耶春秋者魯史記之名也君臣父子之大
經禮樂征伐之事所由紀也聖人從而脩
焉抑諸侯而尊王室即十二公之行事見
於二百四十二年之間而後善人勸焉淫
punctuated: 蠹簡浩穰滿家，史法相沿，代有作者。溫純如左氏，簡潔如子長，雄健如孟堅，是誠史家之魯殿靈光而巋然者也。然其才氣之所充，規模之所就，要之所謂多聞習事，而猶未能離乎史也。迺若朱子《綱目》之作，發宣尼之蘊，成一家之言，雖未敢擬經中之史，亦可謂史中之經矣。此我憲皇所以特命儒英法之，而有《續通鑑綱目》之書也。請陳其槩，而執事擇焉，可乎？蓋嘗攷之，《書》者，古史也，帝王之軌範、政治之權輿所從出也。聖人從而定焉，芟繁亂而剪浮辭，自唐虞而訖成周，大經大法，曉然而易遵，坦然而易行。由是觀之，則《書》非孔子莫能定矣。請米而作佳傳者，豈能為其廝養耶？《春秋》者，魯史記之名也，君臣父子之大經、禮樂征伐之事所由紀也。聖人從而脩焉，抑諸侯而尊王室，即十二公之行事，見於二百四十二年之間，而後善人勸焉，淫
translation_en:
…worm-eaten bamboo slips fill households in vast abundance. The methods of historical writing have been handed down, and every age has had its authors. Refined and mellow like Zuo, concise like Zichang, vigorous like Mengjian: these are truly the towering survivors among historians, like the Lingguang Hall of Lu. Yet, for all the fullness of their talent and spirit and the scope of their achievements, they amount ultimately to what is called extensive learning and familiarity with affairs; they have still not gone beyond history.

As for Master Zhu’s Outline and Details, it brought to light the profound meaning of Xuanni [Confucius] and established a distinctive interpretation. Although one would not presume to compare it with the histories among the Classics, it may indeed be called a Classic among histories. This is why our Emperor Xian specially commanded outstanding Confucian scholars to take it as their model, producing the Continuation of the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror. May I set forth its general principles for you, honored examiners, to judge?

I have examined the matter. The Book of Documents is ancient history: it is the source of the standards for emperors and kings and of the beginnings of governance. The Sage then established its definitive text, pruning what was excessive and confused and cutting empty language. From Tang and Yu down to the established Zhou dynasty, its great norms and laws are clear and easy to follow, straightforward and easy to practice. Viewed thus, no one but Confucius could have established the Book of Documents. Could someone who requested rice in exchange for writing a favorable biography even serve as his menial attendant?

The Spring and Autumn Annals was the name of the historical records of Lu. It recorded the great norms governing ruler and minister, father and son, and matters of ritual, music, punitive expeditions, and warfare. The Sage then revised it, restraining the feudal lords and exalting the royal house. Through the deeds of the twelve dukes, presented over a span of 242 years, good people were encouraged, and the depraved…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
人懼焉執此論之則春秋非孔子莫能脩
矣受金而諛盛德者豈能望其藩籬耶於
戲尚書春秋不可及矣弗獲已而思其次
其惟諸史乎諸史之良遷固其尤也辯而
不華質而不俚遷之得也議者謂其崇勢
利而羞貧賤特合抱之寸朽也可盡訾歟
贍而不穢詳而有體固之長也議者謂其
輕仁義而賤死節特連城之微瑕也可盡
譏歟吁自史才言之遷固又非諸史可同
日語矣昔之評者曰遷固之史可與左丘
明鴈行可使范曄北面可使陳壽作衙官
晉史而下可以奴僕命之何也評者之意
蓋以左氏之傳其文緩其旨遠炳然有三
代之風而班馬二史之雄深雅健似亦少
減故曰可與左丘明鴈行焉范曄之述東
漢標格卑陋文彩不足以動人嘗自擬其
博贍不及班固則於遷可知矣故曰可使
范曄北面焉若夫陳壽之志三國義例舛
punctuated: 人懼焉。執此論之，則春秋非孔子莫能脩矣。受金而諛盛德者，豈能望其藩籬耶？於戲！尚書、春秋不可及矣。弗獲已而思其次，其惟諸史乎？諸史之良，遷、固其尤也。辯而不華，質而不俚，遷之得也。議者謂其崇勢利而羞貧賤，特合抱之寸朽也，可盡訾歟？贍而不穢，詳而有體，固之長也。議者謂其輕仁義而賤死節，特連城之微瑕也，可盡譏歟？吁！自史才言之，遷、固又非諸史可同日語矣。昔之評者曰：「遷、固之史，可與左丘明鴈行，可使范曄北面，可使陳壽作衙官，晉史而下，可以奴僕命之。」何也？評者之意，蓋以左氏之傳，其文緩，其旨遠，炳然有三代之風，而班、馬二史之雄深雅健，似亦少減，故曰可與左丘明鴈行焉。范曄之述東漢，標格卑陋，文彩不足以動人，嘗自擬其博贍不及班固，則於遷可知矣，故曰可使范曄北面焉。若夫陳壽之志三國，義例舛
translation_en:
…the wicked are made afraid. Judging by this, none but Confucius could have revised the Spring and Autumn Annals. Could those who accept gold to offer flattering praise of glorious virtue even hope to approach its outer fence? Alas! The Book of Documents and the Spring and Autumn Annals are beyond reach. If we must seek what comes next, would it not be the various histories? Among the finest historians, Sima Qian and Ban Gu are outstanding. Eloquent without being ornate, plain without being vulgar: these are Qian’s achievements. Critics say that he exalts power and profit and regards poverty and low status as shameful. Yet this is merely an inch of rot in a tree whose trunk takes two arms to encircle. Can one condemn him wholesale for it? Copious without being cluttered, detailed yet well ordered: these are Gu’s strengths. Critics say that he makes light of benevolence and righteousness and disparages dying for one’s principles. Yet this is merely a tiny flaw in a jade worth a string of cities. Can one disparage him wholesale for it? Ah! In historical talent, Qian and Gu cannot even be spoken of in the same breath as the other historians.

A critic of former times said: “The histories of Qian and Gu may rank alongside Zuo Qiuming; they may have Fan Ye face north before them as a pupil, and Chen Shou serve as their subordinate officer. The histories of the Jin and those below them may be assigned the status of slaves and servants.” Why is this? The critic presumably meant that the Commentary of Zuo is measured in expression and far-reaching in purport, manifestly possessing the spirit of the Three Dynasties. Even the grandeur, depth, elegance, and vigor of the two histories by Ban Gu and Sima Qian seem slightly inferior to it. Hence the statement that they may rank alongside Zuo Qiuming. Fan Ye’s account of the Eastern Han is low and crude in style, and its literary brilliance is insufficient to move readers. He himself once judged that his breadth and richness fell short of Ban Gu’s; how he compares with Qian can therefore be inferred. Hence the statement that Fan Ye may be made to face north before them as a pupil. As for Chen Shou’s Records of the Three Kingdoms, its organizing principles and conventions are inconsistent…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
駁校其書而譏之者十有八九矣寧不爲
遷固之衙官耶外此若二晉所紀南北所
載朱紫不分鬼異詼諧則淫巫瞽史之流
矣寧非遷固之奴隸耶於戲遷固二子固
史之良也求其發聖人之微言邁二子之
製作吾於考亭綱目見之矣觀其自序云
表歲以首年而因年以著統大書以提要
而分註以備言歲周於上而天道明矣統
正於下而人道定矣大綱槩舉而鑒戒昭
===
矣衆物畢張而幾微著矣真自尚書春秋
以來未有也是固不可及矣然而威烈而
上未萃成編藝祖以還又自爲籍是猶未
免執卷有浩繁之歎臨文乏啓沃之資也
職此之故是以我
憲宗皇帝誕命儒臣以宋元二史之舊倣綱目
之法而成書也其書由建隆之開基至海
南之訖籙凡其中命令紀綱之詳國體安
危之係大書特書據往牒也敢爲臆說乎
punctuated:
駁，校其書而譏之者十有八九矣，寧不爲遷固之衙官耶？外此，若二晉所紀、南北所載，朱紫不分，鬼異詼諧，則淫巫瞽史之流矣，寧非遷固之奴隸耶？於戲！遷固二子固史之良也。求其發聖人之微言、邁二子之製作，吾於考亭綱目見之矣。觀其自序云：「表歲以首年，而因年以著統；大書以提要，而分註以備言。歲周於上，而天道明矣；統正於下，而人道定矣；大綱槩舉，而鑒戒昭矣；衆物畢張，而幾微著矣。」真自《尚書》《春秋》以來未有也，是固不可及矣。然而威烈而上未萃成編，藝祖以還又自爲籍，是猶未免執卷有浩繁之歎、臨文乏啓沃之資也。
職此之故，是以我憲宗皇帝誕命儒臣，以宋元二史之舊，倣綱目之法而成書也。其書由建隆之開基至海南之訖籙，凡其中命令紀綱之詳、國體安危之係，大書特書，據往牒也，敢爲臆說乎？
translation_en:
…contradictory. Of those who have examined his book, eight or nine in ten have criticized it. Could he fail to rank as a subordinate officer to Sima Qian and Ban Gu? Beyond this, the records of the two Jin dynasties and the histories of the Northern and Southern dynasties fail to distinguish vermilion from purple—that is, the true from the false—and abound in supernatural oddities and jocular tales. Their authors belong among heterodox shamans and blind annalists. Are they not the slaves of Sima Qian and Ban Gu? Ah! These two men were indeed fine historians. Yet if we seek a work that elucidates the subtle words of the sages and surpasses their compositions, I have found it in the Outline and Details of History (Gangmu) by the master of Kaoting, Zhu Xi. Consider what his own preface says: “The years are marked out by placing the year designation first, and the years are used to display the legitimate succession. Large characters present the essentials, while subsidiary annotations provide the full account. The sequence of years is complete above, making the Way of Heaven clear; the legitimate succession is set right below, establishing the human order. The main outlines are broadly presented, making lessons and warnings manifest; the manifold particulars are fully displayed, revealing the subtlest incipient developments.” Truly, nothing like this had existed since the Book of Documents and the Spring and Autumn Annals. It is indeed beyond compare. Nevertheless, events before King Weilie have not been gathered into a compilation, while those from the founding emperor of the Song onward form a separate work. Thus, readers still cannot avoid lamenting the vast bulk of the volumes, while the text lacks sufficient resources for enlightening and nourishing the ruler’s mind.
For this reason, our Emperor Xianzong solemnly commanded his Confucian ministers to draw upon the existing histories of the Song and Yuan and compile a book following the method of the Outline and Details. This book extends from the foundation laid in the Jianlong reign period to the ending of the imperial mandate at Hainan [?]. All the particulars of commands and institutions, and all matters bearing upon the security or peril of the state, are prominently and expressly recorded on the authority of earlier records. Would they dare offer conjectures?

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
正例變例本成規也敢爲高論乎彼契丹
之出鮮卑女眞之起渤海亦爲采摭而附
見焉毋放失也敢闊略乎迺若胡元主華
世運極否似無足齒矣第勢成混一傳世
頗久雖則大書其年猶存外夷之意也諸
凡書法燁然華袞之褒凜然市朝之誅矣
末則紀
天兵之征討戡亂雄之割據
王師所加勢如破竹不旋踵而再闢乾坤肇脩
===
人紀眞萬代之快覩矣所謂三年鬼方之
伐六月玁狁之師豈足以俎豆於此哉於
戲訓裁斷自於
淵衷謨烈光昭乎信史與尚書春秋並觀可
也史云乎哉愚不敏謹述舊聞以對執事
以爲何如
第五問
梁佐
考試官訓導穆批〔深悉御將之略善談兵者也可〕
punctuated:
正例、變例，本成規也，敢爲高論乎？彼契丹之出鮮卑、女眞之起渤海，亦爲采摭而附見焉，毋放失也，敢闊略乎？迺若胡元主華，世運極否，似無足齒矣。第勢成混一，傳世頗久，雖則大書其年，猶存外夷之意也。諸凡書法，燁然華袞之褒，凜然市朝之誅矣。末則紀天兵之征討，戡亂雄之割據。王師所加，勢如破竹，不旋踵而再闢乾坤，肇脩人紀，眞萬代之快覩矣！所謂三年鬼方之伐、六月玁狁之師，豈足以俎豆於此哉？於戲！訓裁斷自於淵衷，謨烈光昭乎信史，與《尚書》《春秋》並觀可也，史云乎哉？愚不敏，謹述舊聞以對，執事以爲何如？
第五問
梁佐
考試官訓導穆批〔深悉御將之略善談兵者也可〕
translation_en:
…Its regular and exceptional conventions follow established rules: would we dare advance lofty theories of our own? Accounts of the Khitan emerging from the Xianbei and the Jurchen arising from Bohai were likewise gathered and appended, so that nothing would be lost: would we dare treat them cursorily? As for the foreign Yuan ruling China, the fortunes of the age had reached their lowest ebb, and it might seem that they scarcely deserved mention. Yet they achieved unification and transmitted their rule for a considerable time. Although their years are therefore prominently recorded, the intention of treating them as foreign barbarians is still preserved. Throughout, the conventions of historical writing confer praise as resplendent as an embroidered ceremonial robe, and impose condemnation as awe-inspiring as execution in the marketplace.

Finally, the work records the campaigns of the heavenly armies and their suppression of the territories held by rebellious strongmen. Wherever the royal army advanced, its momentum was like splitting bamboo. In scarcely the time needed to turn one's heel, Heaven and Earth were opened anew and human relationships restored. Truly, this was a heartening spectacle for ten thousand generations! How could the celebrated three-year campaign against the Guifang or the sixth-month expedition against the Xianyun merit ceremonial honor beside this? Alas! The instructions and editorial judgments [?] issued from the depths of the imperial mind; the imperial plans and achievements shine brilliantly in this trustworthy history. It may rightly be viewed alongside the Book of Documents and the Spring and Autumn Annals. Could one call it merely a history? Dull-witted as I am, I have respectfully recounted what I previously heard in reply. What do you, honored examiners, think of it?

Fifth question
Liang Zuo
Examiner Mu, an Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔He thoroughly understands the strategies for controlling generals and is skilled in discussing military affairs. Acceptable.〕

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
則祀漢配天也特掌上耳光武之賢孰能
爲之大歟吁高光之雄尚矣藝祖之略亦
有可稱郭進之在西山軍校越訴則執之
以賜進此感之以誠也曹彬之請使相官
恐太隆則寧賜之以錢此勉之以權也伐
西蜀之將至脱裘帽以衣而不惜謂非結
之以恩耶征江南之將至出匣劒以警而
無貸謂非懼之以法耶嗟夫漢之高光宋
之藝祖誠孫綽所謂馭龍馭虎者矣噫兹
===
特昔人謂之暗合孫吳者爾惟我
聖祖奮迹淮甸汛掃胡塵精神義氣感召招徠
一時猛將如雲謀臣如雨殆將擢頗牧於
禁中走穰侯於堂下矣何其盛哉嘗敢攷
之其與劉基論兵則曰克敵在兵而制兵
在將兵無節制則將不任將非其人則兵
必敗至謂因敵制勝豈必泥古闔闢奇正
在通其變容非不泥其迹而獨用其神乎
諭徐達伐張士誠則曰自大亂以來豪傑
punctuated:
則祀漢配天也，特掌上耳。光武之賢，孰能爲之大歟？吁！高光之雄尚矣，藝祖之略亦有可稱。郭進之在西山，軍校越訴，則執之以賜進，此感之以誠也。曹彬之請使相，官恐太隆，則寧賜之以錢，此勉之以權也。伐西蜀之將至，脱裘帽以衣而不惜，謂非結之以恩耶？征江南之將至，出匣劒以警而無貸，謂非懼之以法耶？嗟夫！漢之高光、宋之藝祖，誠孫綽所謂馭龍馭虎者矣。噫！兹特昔人謂之暗合孫吳者爾。
惟我聖祖奮迹淮甸，汛掃胡塵，精神義氣，感召招徠，一時猛將如雲，謀臣如雨，殆將擢頗牧於禁中，走穰侯於堂下矣。何其盛哉！嘗敢攷之，其與劉基論兵，則曰：「克敵在兵，而制兵在將。兵無節制，則將不任；將非其人，則兵必敗。」至謂：「因敵制勝，豈必泥古？闔闢奇正，在通其變。」容非不泥其迹而獨用其神乎？諭徐達伐張士誠，則曰：「自大亂以來，豪傑
translation_en:
…then offering sacrifice to Han and associating it with Heaven was merely a matter in the palm of his hand [?]. Who could surpass Guangwu in worthiness? Ah! The heroic prowess of Gaozu and Guangwu has long been esteemed; the strategies of the Song dynastic founder also deserve praise. When Guo Jin was at Xishan, a military officer bypassed him to lodge a complaint; the emperor had the officer seized and handed over to Guo Jin. This was moving him through sincerity. When Cao Bin requested appointment as military commissioner with a concurrent chancellor title, the emperor feared that the office would be too exalted and preferred to reward him with money. This was encouraging him through judicious discretion. When a commander charged with attacking Western Shu arrived, the emperor took off his own fur robe and hat to clothe him, without begrudging them. Was this not binding him through favor? When a commander charged with conquering Jiangnan arrived, the emperor drew a sword from its case to warn him that there would be no leniency. Was this not instilling fear through law? Ah! Gaozu and Guangwu of Han and the dynastic founder of Song were truly what Sun Chuo called men who could harness dragons and tigers. Yet these were merely men whom earlier writers described as unwittingly conforming to the teachings of Sun Wu and Wu Qi.
Our Sagely Founder arose in the Huai region and swept away the dust of the northern invaders. His spirit and righteous resolve inspired men to rally to him: fierce generals gathered like clouds, and strategists like rain. It was almost as though he could raise up men like Lian Po and Li Mu within the palace and have the Marquis of Rang hastening to serve below his hall. How magnificent! I have ventured to examine this. Discussing warfare with Liu Ji, he said: “Defeating the enemy depends on the troops, but controlling the troops depends on the general. If the troops lack discipline, the general is unequal to his charge; if the wrong man is general, the troops will certainly be defeated.” He went so far as to say: “Victory is achieved by adapting to the enemy. Why must one cling to antiquity? Closing and opening, unconventional and conventional operations—all depend on mastering their transformations.” Surely this was to employ the animating spirit of ancient methods without clinging to their outward forms? In instructing Xu Da to attack Zhang Shicheng, he said: “Since the great upheaval began, heroes …

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
並起江南亂雄西有陳友諒東有張士誠
聚淵寇攘數侵疆塲今姑蘇諸郡未下命
卿等討之又謂克敵者必以成功為效樹
德者必以廣恩為務是誠仁義之師神武
而不殺者也取中原之命則勤懇於部伍
分數之嚴虛實通變之法其决勝萬全之
師範歟捷蘭州之諭則諄切於恃功驕恣
之戒高危滿溢之憂其明哲保身之藥石
歟佩遣使諭將之勅而凛乎四失之責眞
===
對病之良劑也讀與李翀論武之言而確
然四善之兼眞却敵之良圖也於戲
聖謨昭乎日月
睿筭炳乎丹青方今南征之將果能書紳而儆
目莊誦而銘心又於定興指授之略西平
策應之方凡擊蛇首尾之勢逐鹿掎角之
謀悉講求其故而不泥其迹焉將見如虎
豹之在山若風雷之肅物乘月奏笳而胡
騎遠遁雪夜進旅而元濟成擒矣何也昔
punctuated: 並起，江南亂雄，西有陳友諒，東有張士誠，聚淵寇攘，數侵疆塲。今姑蘇諸郡未下，命卿等討之。」又謂：「克敵者必以成功為效，樹德者必以廣恩為務。」是誠仁義之師，神武而不殺者也。取中原之命，則勤懇於部伍分數之嚴、虛實通變之法，其决勝萬全之師範歟？捷蘭州之諭，則諄切於恃功驕恣之戒、高危滿溢之憂，其明哲保身之藥石歟？佩遣使諭將之勅，而凛乎四失之責，眞對病之良劑也。讀與李翀論武之言，而確然四善之兼，眞却敵之良圖也。於戲！聖謨昭乎日月，睿筭炳乎丹青。方今南征之將，果能書紳而儆目，莊誦而銘心，又於定興指授之略、西平策應之方，凡擊蛇首尾之勢、逐鹿掎角之謀，悉講求其故，而不泥其迹焉，將見如虎豹之在山，若風雷之肅物，乘月奏笳而胡騎遠遁，雪夜進旅而元濟成擒矣。何也？昔
translation_en:
…arose together. Among the formidable rebels in Jiangnan were Chen Youliang in the west and Zhang Shicheng in the east. They gathered in their strongholds and plundered [?], repeatedly invading our frontiers. Now Gusu and the other prefectures have not yet submitted; I command you to campaign against them.” He also said: “Those who defeat the enemy must measure their effectiveness by success; those who establish virtue must make extending benevolence their task.” This was truly an army of benevolence and righteousness, possessing divine martial prowess yet refraining from killing.

His command to take the Central Plain earnestly stressed strict organization into units and subdivisions, and methods of adapting to weakness and strength and responding to change. Was this not a model for securing victory with complete assurance? His instruction on the victory at Lanzhou insistently warned against arrogance and license born of reliance on military merit, and against the dangers of lofty position and excessive success. Was this not salutary medicine for preserving oneself through wisdom and discernment? Reverently receiving the edict sent through an envoy to instruct the generals, one trembles at its rebuke of the four failings: truly an excellent remedy suited to the disease. Reading his words on military affairs with Li Chong, one firmly grasps the need to combine the four virtues: truly an excellent plan for repelling the enemy.

Ah! His sagely plans shine like the sun and moon; his imperial calculations gleam in the painted record. If the generals now campaigning in the south can indeed write these words upon their sashes to keep them before their eyes, solemnly recite them and engrave them upon their hearts, and also investigate the reasoning behind Dingxing’s strategic instructions and Xiping’s methods of coordinated support—all the dispositions by which a snake’s head and tail aid one another when struck, and all the plans for pursuing the deer by holding its legs and seizing its antlers—without rigidly adhering to their outward forms, then we shall see them like tigers and leopards in the mountains, like wind and thunder striking awe into all things. As their reed pipes sound beneath the moon, the Hu cavalry will flee far away; as their troops advance on a snowy night, Yuanji will be taken captive. Why is this so? In former times…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
雲南鄉試錄後序
嘉靖丁酉秋八月旺不穀以
應聘至濫竽文柄以職事當
序末簡稽之前史滇省爲古
西南夷尚矣自漢迄唐臣叛
靡一迨胡元統天始入職方
若幸也第以服左衽而言侏
===
儒者猶夫昔也匪滇爲然斯
時也腥氣迷天汚流漲地雖
河洛文獻之邦中土衣冠之
裔胥而爲夷者十室八九自
今攷之若許魯齋之闡明道
學郝伯常之博綜經史亦士
之魯殿靈光而巋然者顧廼
punctuated:
雲南鄉試錄後序

嘉靖丁酉秋八月，旺不穀以應聘至，濫竽文柄，以職事當序末簡。稽之前史，滇省爲古西南夷，尚矣。自漢迄唐，臣叛靡一。迨胡元統天，始入職方，若幸也。第以服左衽而言侏儒者，猶夫昔也。匪滇爲然，斯時也，腥氣迷天，汚流漲地，雖河洛文獻之邦、中土衣冠之裔，胥而爲夷者十室八九。自今攷之，若許魯齋之闡明道學、郝伯常之博綜經史，亦士之魯殿靈光而巋然者，顧廼
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yunnan Provincial Examination

In autumn, in the eighth month of the dingyou year of Jiajing [1537], I, the unworthy Wang [?], arrived in response to an invitation. Though inadequately qualified, I assumed responsibility for judging literary compositions, and my duties required me to write a postface for the concluding pages. Examining earlier histories, I find that Yunnan’s identification with the ancient southwestern barbarians reaches far back. From the Han through the Tang, its people shifted continually between submission and rebellion. Only when the barbarian Yuan ruled all under Heaven was it incorporated into the imperial domain—seemingly a fortunate development. Yet its people still fastened their robes to the left and spoke an unintelligible tongue [?], just as before. Nor was Yunnan alone in this. At that time, a rank stench obscured the heavens and filthy waters flooded the earth. Even in the lands of the Yellow and Luo rivers, renowned for their cultural traditions, and among the descendants of the cultured families of the central lands, eight or nine households out of ten had together become barbarians. Looking back from the present, men such as Xu Luzhai, who elucidated the Learning of the Way, and Hao Bochang, whose learning comprehensively embraced the classics and histories, stood lofty among scholars like the Lingguang Palace of Lu, a lone surviving monument. Yet they…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
俛首而拜犬豕甘心而飽胡
祿他尚何責耶間有若劉因
者居元近甸密邇朔庭而於
胡鼎不肯一染指焉可謂巨
浸懷襄而砥柱中流者矣然
降奴奔妾之言見於渡江之
賦識者恨之得非夷俗入人
===
之深雖賢者有不免歟是亦
天地之大變矣恭惟我
皇祖驅胡沙漠廓清海宇開
天一詔傳檄中原讀之使人毛髮
森灑凜然夷夏之分定律議
禮俾中國復文明之會洗左
衽之俗焉旋乾轉坤卓越千
punctuated:
俛首而拜犬豕，甘心而飽胡祿，他尚何責耶？間有若劉因者，居元近甸，密邇朔庭，而於胡鼎不肯一染指焉，可謂巨浸懷襄而砥柱中流者矣。然降奴奔妾之言見於渡江之賦，識者恨之，得非夷俗入人之深，雖賢者有不免歟？是亦天地之大變矣。
恭惟我皇祖驅胡沙漠，廓清海宇，開天一詔，傳檄中原，讀之使人毛髮森灑，凜然夷夏之分。定律議禮，俾中國復文明之會，洗左衽之俗焉。旋乾轉坤，卓越千
translation_en:
…bowed their heads in homage to dogs and swine and willingly fed to satiety on barbarian stipends. What, then, could one demand of the others? Occasionally there was someone like Liu Yin, who lived in the environs of the Yuan capital, close to the northern court, yet refused so much as to dip a finger into the barbarians’ cauldron. He may indeed be called a pillar of rock standing midstream amid an overwhelming flood. Yet the words “surrendered slaves” and “runaway concubines” appear in his Rhapsody on Crossing the River, to the regret of discerning readers. Could it be that barbarian customs had penetrated people so deeply that even the worthy could not escape them? This, too, was a great upheaval of Heaven and Earth.
Reverently we reflect that our imperial ancestor drove the barbarians into the sandy wastes and swept clean all within the seas. With a single edict inaugurating a new order, he circulated his proclamation throughout the Central Plain. Reading it makes one’s hair stand on end, so awe-inspiring is its distinction between barbarians and Chinese. He established laws and deliberated on rites, enabling China once more to become a gathering place of civilization and cleansing it of the custom of fastening garments on the left. He turned Heaven and Earth about, surpassing a thousand…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
古
皇祖之績蔑以加已
列聖相承化民俗俗經生學究一
變至道其弓旌之所迎科目
之所舉率皆當時豪俊而翊
賛
皇猷丕闡化理雖唐虞之際於斯
===
爲盛焉是以滇雲之域號稱
僻壤而士生其間往往涵泳
聖涯歌頌熈皡擢科登仕代
不乏人頃歲言者以茲土雖
遠夷荒域而
天地涵育之久人文炳蔚崇而舘
閣要而臺省胥皆沐
punctuated: 古，皇祖之績蔑以加已。列聖相承，化民俗，俗經生學究一變至道。其弓旌之所迎、科目之所舉，率皆當時豪俊，而翊賛皇猷，丕闡化理，雖唐虞之際，於斯爲盛焉。是以滇雲之域，號稱僻壤，而士生其間，往往涵泳聖涯，歌頌熈皡，擢科登仕，代不乏人。頃歲，言者以茲土雖遠夷荒域，而天地涵育之久，人文炳蔚，崇而舘閣，要而臺省，胥皆沐
translation_en:
…antiquity: nothing could surpass the achievements of the Imperial Ancestor. Successive sage emperors inherited his work and transformed popular customs; ordinary students of the classics and scholars [?], through a single transformation, attained the Way. Those welcomed with bows and banners of recruitment and those selected through the examinations were generally the outstanding talents of their age. They assisted the imperial plans and greatly advanced transformative governance. Even compared with the age of Tang and Yu—the sage rulers Yao and Shun—this age was more flourishing.

Thus, although the region of Dianyun, or Yunnan, is reputed to be remote, scholars born there have often immersed themselves in the realm of the sages and sung praises of radiant harmony. In every generation there have been men who succeeded in the examinations and entered official service. In recent years, those submitting proposals argued that, although this land lies far away in the uncultivated territory of non-Chinese peoples, Heaven and Earth have long nurtured it, and its literary culture shines brilliantly. Whether in the lofty Hanlin Academy and imperial libraries or in the pivotal censorial and central administrative offices, all have received…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
殊恩叨清選與中州縉紳項背相
望有鄒魯之遺焉請增解額
為遐壤勸疏奏
皇上特賜俞允其變夷之功作人
之盛可仰窺其萬一矣是舉
也就試者殆千人鎖院如
制三試之則見攡辭脫頴談王論
===
道主六經而奴百氏啖梁肉
而茹苦荼華藻雅贍若照乗
木難媚澤奪目所謂盈前珠
璣而揀汰為難者也豈不盛
歟諸士子之登茲選者眞千
載一時之逢亦既幸且榮矣
尚其仰體豐芑之遺而以古
punctuated: 殊恩，叨清選，與中州縉紳項背相望，有鄒魯之遺焉。請增解額，為遐壤勸。疏奏，皇上特賜俞允。其變夷之功、作人之盛，可仰窺其萬一矣。是舉也，就試者殆千人。鎖院如制，三試之，則見攡辭脫頴，談王論道，主六經而奴百氏，啖梁肉而茹苦荼，華藻雅贍，若照乗木難，媚澤奪目。所謂盈前珠璣而揀汰為難者也，豈不盛歟？諸士子之登茲選者，眞千載一時之逢，亦既幸且榮矣。尚其仰體豐芑之遺，而以古
translation_en:
…exceptional imperial favor and have been granted prestigious appointments. They follow one another in succession alongside the scholar-officials of the central provinces, preserving something of the legacy of Zou and Lu. A request was made to increase the quota of provincial graduates, to encourage this distant region. When the memorial was submitted, His Majesty graciously gave his special assent. From this we may reverently glimpse a ten-thousandth part of his achievement in transforming the frontier peoples and his magnificent cultivation of talent.

For this examination, nearly a thousand candidates presented themselves. The examination compound was locked in accordance with the regulations. Through the three sessions, we saw compositions displaying outstanding talent, discussing kingly government and the Way, taking the Six Classics as masters and the hundred schools as servants, eating fine grain and meat while also consuming bitter greens [?]. Their literary embellishment was elegant and abundant, like carriage-illuminating pearls and munan gems, whose lovely luster dazzles the eyes. This was truly what is meant by pearls and jewels filling the space before one, making selection and rejection difficult. Was it not a splendid occasion?

Those scholars who have attained selection here have truly encountered an opportunity that comes but once in a thousand years: they are both fortunate and honored. May they reverently embody the inherited ideal of nurturing talent expressed in “Luxuriant Millet,” and take the ancient…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
豪傑自期焉可也昔李唐之
盛閩廣之選未聞有舉進士
者旣而於閩得歐陽詹於廣
得張九齡文章相業光昭汗
簡至今其地號詩書之府其
士挹歐張之風不衰諸君子
生長之地亦旣相若矣行將
===
試禮闈策
大庭服官序有日矣其亦爭自磨
濯而動念於斯否乎若夫志
伊學顏為國華彩而上不負
天子焉則又主司者之深願也寧
不為科目之光哉
江西廣信府弋陽縣儒學訓
punctuated:
豪傑自期焉可也。昔李唐之盛，閩廣之選，未聞有舉進士者。旣而於閩得歐陽詹，於廣得張九齡，文章相業，光昭汗簡。至今其地號詩書之府，其士挹歐張之風不衰。諸君子生長之地，亦旣相若矣。行將試禮闈，策大庭，服官序有日矣。其亦爭自磨濯而動念於斯否乎？若夫志伊學顏，為國華彩，而上不負天子焉，則又主司者之深願也。寧不為科目之光哉！
江西廣信府弋陽縣儒學訓
translation_en:
…it is fitting that you aspire to be outstanding men. In the flourishing days of the Tang house of Li, among those selected from Min and Guang, none had been heard of who attained the jinshi degree. Subsequently, Min produced Ouyang Zhan and Guang produced Zhang Jiuling. Their literary achievements and accomplishments in the chief councillorship shone brightly in the historical records. To this day, those regions are called repositories of the Poetry and Documents, and their scholars continue unabated to draw inspiration from Ouyang and Zhang. The places where you gentlemen were born and raised are much like those regions. Soon you will sit the Metropolitan Examination and answer policy questions at the imperial court; the day when you take your places in official service is approaching. Will you not vie with one another in refining and purifying yourselves, keeping these examples in mind? As for aspiring to emulate Yi Yin and learning from Yan Hui, bringing lustre to the state and proving worthy of the Son of Heaven above—this is also the profound hope of those presiding over the examination. Would this not bring glory to the examination system!
Assistant Instructor of the Confucian School of Yiyang County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text: 導穆旺謹序
punctuated: 導穆旺謹序。
translation_en: …Instructor Mu Wang respectfully composed this preface.

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
雲南鄉試錄序
嘉靖丁酉歲秋八月廼天下
賓興期先寔貴州士合試於
滇至是用言者
請貴州特設科論士雲南則增解
額總若干名而掄材擢秀仍
舊貫焉疏下禮部議上其事
===
制曰可於戲可以仰見
國家豐芑之遺
神化漸被之遠
聖天子作人之盛矣廷相也不佞
竊惟周書論辭貴乎體要尼
父陳訓惡乎異端古人為文
率皆明道德經世務若太羹
punctuated:
雲南鄉試錄序

嘉靖丁酉歲秋八月，廼天下賓興期。先寔貴州士合試於滇，至是用言者請，貴州特設科論士，雲南則增解額總若干名，而掄材擢秀仍舊貫焉。疏下禮部，議上其事，制曰：「可。」於戲！可以仰見國家豐芑之遺、神化漸被之遠、聖天子作人之盛矣。

廷相也不佞，竊惟《周書》論辭，貴乎體要；尼父陳訓，惡乎異端。古人為文，率皆明道德、經世務，若太羹
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yunnan Provincial Examination

In the eighth month, in autumn of the dingyou year of Jiajing [1537], it was time throughout the realm to honor and select worthy men through the examinations. Previously, candidates from Guizhou had taken the examination jointly with those of Yunnan. Now, following a proposal submitted to the throne, Guizhou was granted a separate examination to assess its candidates, while Yunnan’s quota of provincial graduates was increased to a certain total number. Its established procedures for selecting talent and promoting outstanding men remained in place. The memorial was referred to the Ministry of Rites, which deliberated and submitted its recommendations. The Emperor’s decree reads: “Approved.” Ah! Here we may reverently perceive the state’s inherited tradition of nurturing talent, the far-reaching spread of its wondrous civilizing influence, and the flourishing of our sagely Son of Heaven’s cultivation of worthy men.

I, Tingxiang, though lacking ability, venture to reflect that the Documents of Zhou, in discussing language, prizes substance and essentials; Father Ni [Confucius], in setting forth his teachings, rejects heterodox doctrines. The writings of the ancients generally all served to elucidate the Way and virtue and to order the affairs of the world, resembling the plain broth of the great sacrifice…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
玄酒然如典謨之明白易知
是已初無險僻艱深之狀竒
澁茁軋而不可讀也嘗莊誦
高皇帝聖語曰諸葛孔明出師表
不事雕刻而誠意溢出至今
使人誦之忠義感激又曰近
世文士不究道德之本不達
===
當世之務辭雖艱深意實淺
近卽使過相如楊雄何裨實
用大哉
王言真醇淵懿濟濟多士藹然嚮
風
聖子神孫益隆紹述百六十年來
海內髦俊抱墳策而頌太平
punctuated:
玄酒然，如典謨之明白易知是已。初無險僻艱深之狀，竒澁茁軋而不可讀也。嘗莊誦高皇帝聖語曰：「諸葛孔明出師表，不事雕刻而誠意溢出，至今使人誦之，忠義感激。」又曰：「近世文士不究道德之本，不達當世之務，辭雖艱深，意實淺近。卽使過相如、楊雄，何裨實用？」大哉，王言！真醇淵懿，濟濟多士，藹然嚮風。
聖子神孫，益隆紹述。百六十年來，海內髦俊抱墳策而頌太平
translation_en:
…and plain sacrificial water: such is the clarity and accessibility of the Canons and Counsels in the Book of Documents. Originally, such writing had none of the strained obscurity and difficulty, the strangeness, roughness, and awkwardness [?] that make a text unreadable. I have reverently recited these sage words of Emperor Gao: “Zhuge Kongming’s Memorial on Dispatching the Army employs no elaborate ornamentation, yet sincerity overflows from it. Even today, reciting it stirs people to loyalty and righteousness.” He also said: “Literary men of recent times do not investigate the foundations of the Way and virtue, nor do they comprehend the affairs of their age. Though their language is difficult and obscure, their meaning is actually shallow. Even if they surpassed Xiangru and Yang Xiong, what benefit would they bring to practical affairs?” How great are these imperial words! True and pure, profound and admirable, they draw the assembled multitude of scholars gladly to their example.
His sage sons and divine grandsons have further exalted the work of continuing his legacy. For 160 years, the outstanding talents throughout the realm have embraced the ancient writings and celebrated the Great Peace…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
者咸布帛菽粟之雅而一時
名卿碩輔代工熈載以復惇
大成裕之治者胥此焉出誠
科目之榮也猗歟休哉迨我
皇上敬天法
祖崇雅黜浮敬一之箴洪範之序
煥乎堯文而太朴未斵所以
===
風天下之士習者乆矣頃年
復用禮官議申禁鈎棘浮藻
之文俾典衡者式焉
天詔渙頒校黌易轍雲南雖古六
詔邊陲而士生其間搦管濡
毫亦皆知脫雕麗而就質素
剪華彩而務雅馴不佞於供
punctuated:
者，咸布帛菽粟之雅，而一時名卿碩輔代工熈載，以復惇大成裕之治者，胥此焉出，誠科目之榮也。猗歟休哉！
迨我皇上敬天法祖，崇雅黜浮，敬一之箴、洪範之序，煥乎堯文，而太朴未斵，所以風天下之士習者乆矣。頃年，復用禮官議，申禁鈎棘浮藻之文，俾典衡者式焉。天詔渙頒，校黌易轍。雲南雖古六詔邊陲，而士生其間，搦管濡毫，亦皆知脫雕麗而就質素，剪華彩而務雅馴。不佞於供
translation_en:
…all possessed the plain elegance of cloth, silk, beans, and grain. The eminent ministers and great counselors of successive times, who carried out Heaven’s work and brought its undertakings to fruition, thereby restoring a generous and ample order of government, all emerged through this route. Truly, this brings honor to the examination system. Ah, how splendid!
Our present Emperor reveres Heaven and takes his ancestors as models, exalting elegance and rejecting superficiality. His Admonition on Reverent Single-mindedness and Preface to the Great Plan shine with the cultural brilliance of Yao, yet preserve primordial simplicity unhewn. Long have they guided the literary habits of scholars throughout the realm. In recent years, he again adopted the proposals of the ritual officials, reiterating the prohibition against thorny, convoluted writing and empty ornament, so that those charged with judging examination essays might follow this standard. The imperial edict was widely promulgated, and the schools changed their course. Although Yunnan is a frontier region, the land of the ancient Six Zhao, the scholars born there, when they take up their brushes and moisten their tips, all know to cast off ornate beauty and embrace plain substance, to trim away colorful embellishment and pursue elegance and propriety. As for my unworthy self, while carrying out…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
事之頃得而縱觀之於易義
之文見庖犧之故焉於書義
之文見陶唐之渾焉於詩禮
春秋義之文見天理民彛之
常焉其誥表策判之文胥稱
是雖熟而爲
宗廟之粢盛裁而爲
===
朝廷衮黼也亦宜矣於戲盛哉
間有競巧趨新靡麗騰口摇
筆而散珠動墨而横錦務爲
炳炳烺烺以投主司之肯首
是殆經賊文妖無補於治者
則黜之不少貸焉於戲諸君
子生長遐方遭逢
punctuated:
事之頃，得而縱觀之。於易義之文，見庖犧之故焉；於書義之文，見陶唐之渾焉；於詩、禮、春秋義之文，見天理民彛之常焉。其誥、表、策、判之文，胥稱是。雖熟而爲宗廟之粢盛，裁而爲朝廷衮黼也，亦宜矣。於戲，盛哉！
間有競巧趨新，靡麗騰口，摇筆而散珠，動墨而横錦，務爲炳炳烺烺，以投主司之肯首，是殆經賊文妖、無補於治者，則黜之，不少貸焉。於戲！諸君子生長遐方，遭逢
translation_en:
…while carrying out my duties, I had the opportunity to survey these writings at length. In the essays on the meaning of the Book of Changes, I discerned the ancient legacy of Pao Xi; in those on the Book of Documents, the unspoiled wholeness of Tao Tang (Yao); and in those on the Books of Odes and Rites and the Spring and Autumn Annals, the enduring principles of Heaven and the constant norms of human relations. Their proclamations, memorials, policy essays, and legal judgments were all of a corresponding standard. Even if these writings were cooked to become sacrificial grain for the ancestral temple, or cut to become the court’s ceremonial robes with their embroidered patterns, they would indeed be fitting. Ah, how splendid!
Among them, however, were some who competed in cleverness and pursued novelty, pouring forth florid language, scattering pearls with a flourish of the brush and spreading brocade with a movement of ink. They strove for dazzling brilliance to win a nod of approval from the examiners. These were surely despoilers of the Classics and perverters of literary composition, contributing nothing to good governance. Such writings I rejected without the slightest indulgence. Ah, gentlemen! Born and raised in a distant region, you have encountered…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
盛際亦既以其辭之醇且朴者
得雋固榮矣尚相與鞭策淬
礪排闥古聖賢純懿之域而
優入焉則主司者之望也毋
徒以地之遠而自鄙夷斯善
矣何也孟子曰舜生於諸馮
東夷之人也文王生於岐周
===
西夷之人也彼丈夫也我丈
夫也有為者亦若是諸君子
顧力行何如耳毋自諉曰辭
達而已矣海濱之子奚足以
語此則幸也是役也合提學
副使陳煥所簡經生之英而
拔其尤擇其文爾雅渾厚者
punctuated:
盛際，亦既以其辭之醇且朴者得雋，固榮矣。尚相與鞭策淬礪，排闥古聖賢純懿之域而優入焉，則主司者之望也。毋徒以地之遠而自鄙夷，斯善矣。何也？孟子曰：「舜生於諸馮，東夷之人也；文王生於岐周，西夷之人也。」「彼丈夫也，我丈夫也，有為者亦若是。」諸君子顧力行何如耳。毋自諉曰：「辭達而已矣，海濱之子奚足以語此？」則幸也。
是役也，合提學副使陳煥所簡經生之英而拔其尤，擇其文爾雅渾厚者
translation_en:
…in this flourishing age, you have already succeeded through the purity and simplicity of your writing—an honor indeed. Yet I hope you will spur one another onward and temper yourselves, push open the gates to the realm of the ancient sages’ and worthies’ pure excellence, and enter it with ease. This is what those presiding over the examination expect of you. It would be good if you did not belittle yourselves merely because your homeland is distant. Why? Mencius said: “Shun was born in Zhufeng; he was a man of the eastern Yi. King Wen was born in Qizhou; he was a man of the western Yi.” “He was a man, and I too am a man. Those who strive to accomplish something can likewise become such as he.” For you gentlemen, it depends only on how earnestly you put this into practice. I would be gratified if you did not excuse yourselves by saying: “Words need only convey their meaning. How could sons of the seacoast be worthy to discuss such matters?”
For this examination, we assembled the outstanding students of the Classics selected by Chen Huan, the Education Intendant and Vice Commissioner, and chose the very best among them, selecting those essays that were elegant, substantial, and dignified…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
登諸冊名為雲南鄉試錄肇
今制也廷相與訓導穆旺濫竽考
試官敎諭沈仁戴希顥訓導
許士德為同考試官分經供
事維謹皆四方之良也迺若
工部右侍郎潘鑑奉
命督木崇重賢科征南將軍黔國
公沐朝輔新握兵符雅尚文
事巡撫雲南右僉都御史汪
文盛經略邊鄙加志儒林監
臨則巡按雲南監察御史陰
汝登提調則雲南左布政使
王俊民右叅政葉珩監試則
雲南按察副使程旦僉事戴
punctuated:
登諸冊，名為《雲南鄉試錄》，肇今制也。廷相與訓導穆旺濫竽考試官，敎諭沈仁、戴希顥，訓導許士德為同考試官，分經供事維謹，皆四方之良也。
迺若工部右侍郎潘鑑奉命督木，崇重賢科；征南將軍黔國公沐朝輔新握兵符，雅尚文事；巡撫雲南右僉都御史汪文盛經略邊鄙，加志儒林。監臨則巡按雲南監察御史陰汝登；提調則雲南左布政使王俊民、右叅政葉珩；監試則雲南按察副使程旦、僉事戴
translation_en:
…entered them in a volume entitled Record of the Yunnan Provincial Examination, inaugurating the present practice. I, Tingxiang, together with Assistant Instructor Mu Wang, unworthily served as Examiners. Instructors Shen Ren and Dai Xihao and Assistant Instructor Xu Shide served as Associate Examiners. Assigned responsibility for the respective Classics, they performed their duties with care; all were worthy men drawn from various regions.
Pan Jian, Right Vice Minister of Works, who had received imperial orders to supervise timber procurement, held the examination for selecting worthy men in high esteem. Mu Chaofu, General Who Subdues the South and Duke of Qian, had newly assumed military command and had a longstanding regard for literary pursuits. Wang Wensheng, Grand Coordinator of Yunnan and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, managed the frontier regions and devoted particular attention to the community of scholars. The Supervising Official was Yin Rudeng, Regional Inspector of Yunnan and Investigating Censor. The Proctors were Wang Junmin, Yunnan’s Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Ye Heng, its Right Administration Vice Commissioner. Examination supervision was entrusted to Cheng Dan, Yunnan’s Provincial Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Dai…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
邦正綜理防範則右布政使
李顯左參政黃祺右參政車
純按察副使朱方鄭登高任
維賢僉事郭田胡仲誥都指
揮僉事馮立樊泰右參政胡
德僉事余承業則先期入
賀胥贊厥成收掌試卷則知府
===
梅月姜恩其餘如謄錄對讀
如供給受卷名號靡一例得
以執事書時
王師將問罪交南兵事倥偬而文
闈完整雖乏金碧之輝殊無
湫隘之陋議者以為有司得
貞固之榦云
punctuated:
邦正。綜理防範則右布政使李顯、左參政黃祺、右參政車純、按察副使朱方、鄭登高、任維賢、僉事郭田、胡仲誥、都指揮僉事馮立、樊泰。右參政胡德、僉事余承業則先期入賀，胥贊厥成。收掌試卷則知府梅月、姜恩。其餘如謄錄、對讀，如供給、受卷、名號，靡一例得以執事書。
時王師將問罪交南，兵事倥偬，而文闈完整，雖乏金碧之輝，殊無湫隘之陋。議者以為有司得貞固之榦云。
translation_en:
…Bangzheng. General management and security were handled by Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Xian; Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Huang Qi; Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Che Chun; Provincial Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zhu Fang, Zheng Denggao, and Ren Weixian; Provincial Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Guo Tian and Hu Zhonggao; and Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Feng Li and Fan Tai. Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Hu De and Provincial Surveillance Assistant Commissioner Yu Chengye had gone to court beforehand to offer congratulations; all contributed to bringing the undertaking to completion. Prefects Mei Yue and Jiang En were responsible for collecting and keeping the examination papers. The remaining personnel—for transcription, proofreading by reading aloud, supplies, receipt of papers, and names and identification numbers—could not all be recorded uniformly as examination functionaries [?].
At that time, the imperial army was about to call Jiaonan to account. Military affairs were pressing, yet the examination compound was fully in order. Though it lacked the splendor of gold and jade-green decoration, it was entirely free of the defects of dampness and cramped quarters. Observers considered that the responsible authorities had shown firm and steadfast administrative ability.

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
河南汝寧府上蔡縣儒學教
諭鄭廷相謹序
punctuated: 河南汝寧府上蔡縣儒學教諭鄭廷相謹序。
translation_en: Preface respectfully composed by Zheng Tingxiang, Instructor of the Confucian School of Shangcai County, Runing Prefecture, Henan.

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試
監臨官
巡按雲南監察御史陰汝登〔民獻四川内江縣人癸酉貢士〕
提調官
雲南等處承宣布政使司左布政使王俊民〔用章湖廣石首縣人甲戌進士〕
雲南等處承宣布政使司右參政葉珩〔鳴玉福建莆田縣人丁丑進士〕
監試官
雲南等處提刑按察司副使程旦〔孟明直隸歙縣人癸未進士〕
雲南等處提刑按察司僉事戴邦正〔貞卿直隸上海縣人丙戌進士〕
===
考試官
河南汝寧府上蔡縣儒學教諭鄭廷相〔調父湖廣黄岡縣人壬午貢士〕
江西廣信府弋陽縣儒學訓導穆旺〔相甫福建閩縣人辛卯貢士〕
同考試官
河南南陽府桐栢縣儒學教諭沈仁〔子恕福建漳浦縣人辛卯貢士〕
江西廣信府鉛山縣儒學教諭戴希顥〔秀夫廣西柳州衛籍湖廣寧鄉縣人己卯貢士〕
直隸蘇州府吳江縣儒學訓導許士德〔容甫廣東南海縣人乙酉貢士〕
印卷官
雲南等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷張壅〔崇德湖廣石首縣人監生〕
punctuated:
嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試

監臨官：巡按雲南監察御史陰汝登〔民獻，四川内江縣人，癸酉貢士〕。

提調官：雲南等處承宣布政使司左布政使王俊民〔用章，湖廣石首縣人，甲戌進士〕。雲南等處承宣布政使司右參政葉珩〔鳴玉，福建莆田縣人，丁丑進士〕。

監試官：雲南等處提刑按察司副使程旦〔孟明，直隸歙縣人，癸未進士〕。雲南等處提刑按察司僉事戴邦正〔貞卿，直隸上海縣人，丙戌進士〕。

考試官：河南汝寧府上蔡縣儒學教諭鄭廷相〔調父，湖廣黄岡縣人，壬午貢士〕。江西廣信府弋陽縣儒學訓導穆旺〔相甫，福建閩縣人，辛卯貢士〕。

同考試官：河南南陽府桐栢縣儒學教諭沈仁〔子恕，福建漳浦縣人，辛卯貢士〕。江西廣信府鉛山縣儒學教諭戴希顥〔秀夫，廣西柳州衛籍，湖廣寧鄉縣人，己卯貢士〕。直隸蘇州府吳江縣儒學訓導許士德〔容甫，廣東南海縣人，乙酉貢士〕。

印卷官：雲南等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷張壅〔崇德，湖廣石首縣人，監生〕。
translation_en:
Yunnan Provincial Examination of the Sixteenth Year of Jiajing (1537)

Supervising Official
Yin Rudeng, Regional Inspecting Censor for Yunnan, had the courtesy name Minxian and was from Neijiang County, Sichuan. He was a tribute student (gongshi) of the guiyou year.

Proctors
Wang Junmin, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Yunnan, had the courtesy name Yongzhang and was from Shishou County, Huguang. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the jiaxu year.
Ye Heng, Right Administration Vice Commissioner of Yunnan, had the courtesy name Mingyu and was from Putian County, Fujian. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the dingchou year.

Examination Monitoring Officials
Cheng Dan, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Yunnan, had the courtesy name Mengming and was from She County, Zhili. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the guiwei year.
Dai Bangzheng, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner of Yunnan, had the courtesy name Zhenqing and was from Shanghai County, Zhili. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the bingxu year.

Examiners
Zheng Tingxiang, Instructor in the Confucian School of Shangcai County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Diaofu and was from Huanggang County, Huguang. He was a tribute student (gongshi) of the renwu year.
Mu Wang, Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Yiyang County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Xiangfu and was from Min County, Fujian. He was a tribute student (gongshi) of the xinmao year.

Associate Examiners
Shen Ren, Instructor in the Confucian School of Tongbai County, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Zishu and was from Zhangpu County, Fujian. He was a tribute student (gongshi) of the xinmao year.
Dai Xihao, Instructor in the Confucian School of Yanshan County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Xiufu. He was registered with Liuzhou Guard in Guangxi and was originally from Ningxiang County, Huguang; he was a tribute student (gongshi) of the jimao year.
Xu Shide, Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Rongfu and was from Nanhai County, Guangdong. He was a tribute student (gongshi) of the yiyou year.

Examination Paper Printing Officials
Zhang Yong, Registrar in the Registry of the Yunnan Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Chongde and was from Shishou County, Huguang. He was a student of the Imperial University (jiansheng).

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
雲南等處提刑按察司經歷司知事胡大嵩〔邦秀湖廣瀏陽縣人監生〕
收掌試卷官
雲南府知府梅月〔子恒貴州普定衞籍陝西三原縣人丙戌進士〕
臨安府知府姜恩〔君錫四川廣安州人癸未進士〕
受卷官
曲靖軍民府知府姚正〔在養福建莆田縣人辛巳進士〕
大理府同知范言〔孔嘉浙江秀水縣人丙戌進士〕
曲靖軍民府同知吳讓〔撝謙湖廣澧州人庚午貢士〕
臨安府阿迷州知州苟儒〔宗道四川綿州人巳卯貢士〕
===
彌封官
楚雄府同知顏階〔崇升福建龍溪縣人癸酉貢士〕
永昌軍民府同知徐士華〔希舜貴州烏撒衞籍直隸崑山縣人庚午貢士〕
雲南府晉寧州知州鮑冕〔惟瞻直隸歙縣人戊子貢士〕
