雲南府嵩明州知州劉陞〔進之南京豹韜左衞籍湖廣通山縣人監生〕
永昌軍民府騰越州知州程輅〔宗殷貴州普定衞籍直隸歙縣人庚午貢士〕
謄錄官
武定軍民府和曲州知州何士鰲〔安周廣西蒼梧縣籍湖廣長沙縣人丁卯貢士〕
鶴慶軍民府順州知州王璋〔德卿四川瀘州人庚午貢士〕
punctuated:
雲南等處提刑按察司經歷司知事胡大嵩〔邦秀，湖廣瀏陽縣人，監生〕。

收掌試卷官：
雲南府知府梅月〔子恒，貴州普定衞籍，陝西三原縣人，丙戌進士〕。臨安府知府姜恩〔君錫，四川廣安州人，癸未進士〕。

受卷官：
曲靖軍民府知府姚正〔在養，福建莆田縣人，辛巳進士〕。大理府同知范言〔孔嘉，浙江秀水縣人，丙戌進士〕。曲靖軍民府同知吳讓〔撝謙，湖廣澧州人，庚午貢士〕。臨安府阿迷州知州苟儒〔宗道，四川綿州人，巳卯貢士〕。

彌封官：
楚雄府同知顏階〔崇升，福建龍溪縣人，癸酉貢士〕。永昌軍民府同知徐士華〔希舜，貴州烏撒衞籍，直隸崑山縣人，庚午貢士〕。雲南府晉寧州知州鮑冕〔惟瞻，直隸歙縣人，戊子貢士〕。雲南府嵩明州知州劉陞〔進之，南京豹韜左衞籍，湖廣通山縣人，監生〕。永昌軍民府騰越州知州程輅〔宗殷，貴州普定衞籍，直隸歙縣人，庚午貢士〕。

謄錄官：
武定軍民府和曲州知州何士鰲〔安周，廣西蒼梧縣籍，湖廣長沙縣人，丁卯貢士〕。鶴慶軍民府順州知州王璋〔德卿，四川瀘州人，庚午貢士〕。
translation_en:
Hu Dasong, Clerk in the Registry of the Yunnan Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Bangxiu. He was from Liuyang County, Huguang, and was an Imperial University student.

Officials in Charge of Safekeeping Examination Papers:
Mei Yue, Prefect of Yunnan Prefecture, had the courtesy name Ziheng. Registered in Puding Guard, Guizhou, and originally from Sanyuan County, Shaanxi, he was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the bingxu year.
Jiang En, Prefect of Lin’an Prefecture, had the courtesy name Junxi. He was from Guang’an Subprefecture, Sichuan, and was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

Officials Receiving Examination Papers:
Yao Zheng, Prefect of Qujing Military and Civil Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zaiyang. He was from Putian County, Fujian, and was a metropolitan graduate of the xinsi year.
Fan Yan, Vice Prefect of Dali Prefecture, had the courtesy name Kongjia. He was from Xiushui County, Zhejiang, and was a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.
Wu Rang, Vice Prefect of Qujing Military and Civil Prefecture, had the courtesy name Huiqian. He was from Li Subprefecture, Huguang, and was a provincial graduate (here termed gongshi) of the gengwu year.
Gou Ru, Magistrate of Ami Subprefecture in Lin’an Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zongdao. He was from Mian Subprefecture, Sichuan, and was a provincial graduate of the year transcribed as simao [?].

Officials Sealing Candidates’ Identifying Information:
Yan Jie, Vice Prefect of Chuxiong Prefecture, had the courtesy name Chongsheng. He was from Longxi County, Fujian, and was a provincial graduate of the guiyou year.
Xu Shihua, Vice Prefect of Yongchang Military and Civil Prefecture, had the courtesy name Xishun. Registered in Wusa Guard, Guizhou, and originally from Kunshan County in the directly administered metropolitan region, he was a provincial graduate of the gengwu year.
Bao Mian, Magistrate of Jinning Subprefecture in Yunnan Prefecture, had the courtesy name Weizhan. He was from She County in the directly administered metropolitan region and was a provincial graduate of the wuzi year.
Liu Sheng, Magistrate of Songming Subprefecture in Yunnan Prefecture, had the courtesy name Jinzhi. Registered in the Nanjing Baotao Left Guard and originally from Tongshan County, Huguang, he was an Imperial University student.
Cheng Lu, Magistrate of Tengyue Subprefecture in Yongchang Military and Civil Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zongyin. Registered in Puding Guard, Guizhou, and originally from She County in the directly administered metropolitan region, he was a provincial graduate of the gengwu year.

Officials Supervising Transcription:
He Shi’ao, Magistrate of Hequ Subprefecture in Wuding Military and Civil Prefecture, had the courtesy name Anzhou. Registered in Cangwu County, Guangxi, and originally from Changsha County, Huguang, he was a provincial graduate of the dingmao year.
Wang Zhang, Magistrate of Shun Subprefecture in Heqing Military and Civil Prefecture, had the courtesy name Deqing. He was from Lu Subprefecture, Sichuan, and was a provincial graduate of the gengwu year.

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
楚雄府鎮南州知州王畬〔以治江西安福縣人丙子貢士〕
雲南府晉寧州歸化縣知縣張澤〔汝厚湖廣黃岡縣人乙酉貢士〕
騰衝衛經歷司經歷吳尚經〔宗正湖廣通城縣人監生〕
對讀官
大理府賓川州知州唐佐〔一夔廣西靈川縣人丙子貢士〕
大理府太和縣知縣景鸞〔應期貴州普定衛人壬午貢士〕
楚雄府定邊縣知縣董欑〔汝壽湖廣麻城人房縣籍監生〕
麗江軍民府經歷司經歷汪世卿〔承選直隸歙縣人監生〕
楚雄府經歷司經歷宋含美〔時暢直隸趙州人監生〕
===
巡綽官
雲南中衛指揮使蘇綱〔國維山東濟南府人〕
廣南衛指揮同知陳麒〔仁夫湖廣通城縣人〕
雲南左衛指揮僉事馬昇〔騰霄直隸和州人〕
雲南右衛指揮僉事紀璋〔國器直隸如皐縣人〕
雲南右衛指揮僉事張威〔可畏湖廣鈞州人〕
雲南中衛指揮僉事方雄〔世英直隸宣城縣人〕
搜檢官
雲南右衛指揮使楊翱〔鵬舉江西豐城縣人〕
punctuated:
楚雄府鎮南州知州王畬〔以治，江西安福縣人，丙子貢士〕。雲南府晉寧州歸化縣知縣張澤〔汝厚，湖廣黃岡縣人，乙酉貢士〕。騰衝衛經歷司經歷吳尚經〔宗正，湖廣通城縣人，監生〕。

對讀官：大理府賓川州知州唐佐〔一夔，廣西靈川縣人，丙子貢士〕。大理府太和縣知縣景鸞〔應期，貴州普定衛人，壬午貢士〕。楚雄府定邊縣知縣董欑〔汝壽，湖廣麻城人，房縣籍，監生〕。麗江軍民府經歷司經歷汪世卿〔承選，直隸歙縣人，監生〕。楚雄府經歷司經歷宋含美〔時暢，直隸趙州人，監生〕。

巡綽官：雲南中衛指揮使蘇綱〔國維，山東濟南府人〕。廣南衛指揮同知陳麒〔仁夫，湖廣通城縣人〕。雲南左衛指揮僉事馬昇〔騰霄，直隸和州人〕。雲南右衛指揮僉事紀璋〔國器，直隸如皐縣人〕。雲南右衛指揮僉事張威〔可畏，湖廣鈞州人〕。雲南中衛指揮僉事方雄〔世英，直隸宣城縣人〕。

搜檢官：雲南右衛指揮使楊翱〔鵬舉，江西豐城縣人〕。
translation_en:
Wang Yu, magistrate of Zhennan Subprefecture in Chuxiong Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yizhi and was from Anfu County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute student of the bingzi year.
Zhang Ze, magistrate of Guihua County in Jinning Subprefecture, Yunnan Prefecture, had the courtesy name Ruhou and was from Huanggang County, Huguang. He was a tribute student of the yiyou year.
Wu Shangjing, registrar in the Registry of Tengchong Guard, had the courtesy name Zongzheng and was from Tongcheng County, Huguang. He was an Imperial University student.

Proofreading Officials:
Tang Zuo, magistrate of Binchuan Subprefecture in Dali Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yikui and was from Lingchuan County, Guangxi. He was a tribute student of the bingzi year.
Jing Luan, magistrate of Taihe County in Dali Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yingqi and was from Puding Guard, Guizhou. He was a tribute student of the renwu year.
Dong Cuan, magistrate of Dingbian County in Chuxiong Prefecture, had the courtesy name Rushou and was a native of Macheng, Huguang, registered in Fang County. He was an Imperial University student.
Wang Shiqing, registrar in the Registry of Lijiang Military and Civil Prefecture, had the courtesy name Chengxuan and was from She County, Zhili. He was an Imperial University student.
Song Hanmei, registrar in the Registry of Chuxiong Prefecture, had the courtesy name Shichang and was from Zhao Subprefecture, Zhili. He was an Imperial University student.

Patrol Officials:
Su Gang, commander of Yunnan Central Guard, had the courtesy name Guowei and was from Jinan Prefecture, Shandong.
Chen Qi, vice commander of Guangnan Guard, had the courtesy name Renfu and was from Tongcheng County, Huguang.
Ma Sheng, assistant commander of Yunnan Left Guard, had the courtesy name Tengxiao and was from He Subprefecture, Zhili.
Ji Zhang, assistant commander of Yunnan Right Guard, had the courtesy name Guoqi and was from Rugao County, Zhili.
Zhang Wei, assistant commander of Yunnan Right Guard, had the courtesy name Kewei and was from Jun Subprefecture, Huguang [?].
Fang Xiong, assistant commander of Yunnan Central Guard, had the courtesy name Shiying and was from Xuancheng County, Zhili.

Search and Inspection Officials:
Yang Ao, commander of Yunnan Right Guard, had the courtesy name Pengju and was from Fengcheng County, Jiangxi.

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
雲南右衞指揮同知汪軒〔良策直隸合肥縣人〕
雲南右衞指揮同知李潮〔宗源直隸宿遷縣人〕
雲南右衞指揮同知孫世爵〔君錫直隸淶水縣人〕
雲南前衞指揮僉事田略〔子奇直隸太和縣人〕
廣南衞指揮僉事王鰲〔汝立直隸蒙城縣人〕
供給官
雲南都指揮使司經歷司經歷瞿良翰〔周臣四川達州人監生〕
雲南等處承宣布政使司經歷司都事劉蘭〔時芳湖廣衡山縣籍貴州前衞人監生〕
雲南等處承宣布政使司照磨所照磨吳時秩〔伯禮江西臨川縣人知印〕
===
雲南等處提刑按察司照磨所照磨党夢熊〔應周陝西富平縣籍耀州人監生〕
雲南府通判吳顯〔仲微直隸石埭縣人監生〕
雲南府經歷司經歷馮驎〔從化湖廣攸縣籍貴州平溪衞人監生〕
廣南衞經歷司經歷喻暉〔子升四川內江縣人吏員〕
雲南右衞經歷司知事萬璋〔朝用四川內江縣人吏員〕
順寧府經歷司經歷周珙〔良器湖廣桂東縣人監生〕
雲南府昆明縣縣丞林克立〔崇禮福建閩縣人吏員〕
楚雄府南安州吏目關節〔介卿直隸大河衞人監生〕
雲南等處承宣布政使司理問所提控案牘王曜〔明之四川南溪縣人吏員〕
punctuated:
雲南右衞指揮同知汪軒〔良策，直隸合肥縣人〕。雲南右衞指揮同知李潮〔宗源，直隸宿遷縣人〕。雲南右衞指揮同知孫世爵〔君錫，直隸淶水縣人〕。雲南前衞指揮僉事田略〔子奇，直隸太和縣人〕。廣南衞指揮僉事王鰲〔汝立，直隸蒙城縣人〕。

供給官：
雲南都指揮使司經歷司經歷瞿良翰〔周臣，四川達州人，監生〕。雲南等處承宣布政使司經歷司都事劉蘭〔時芳，湖廣衡山縣籍，貴州前衞人，監生〕。雲南等處承宣布政使司照磨所照磨吳時秩〔伯禮，江西臨川縣人，知印〕。雲南等處提刑按察司照磨所照磨党夢熊〔應周，陝西富平縣籍，耀州人，監生〕。雲南府通判吳顯〔仲微，直隸石埭縣人，監生〕。雲南府經歷司經歷馮驎〔從化，湖廣攸縣籍，貴州平溪衞人，監生〕。廣南衞經歷司經歷喻暉〔子升，四川內江縣人，吏員〕。雲南右衞經歷司知事萬璋〔朝用，四川內江縣人，吏員〕。順寧府經歷司經歷周珙〔良器，湖廣桂東縣人，監生〕。雲南府昆明縣縣丞林克立〔崇禮，福建閩縣人，吏員〕。楚雄府南安州吏目關節〔介卿，直隸大河衞人，監生〕。雲南等處承宣布政使司理問所提控案牘王曜〔明之，四川南溪縣人，吏員〕。

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
視其所以觀其所由察其所安人焉廋哉
人焉廋哉
天地之道博也厚也高也明也悠也久也
以德服人者中心悅而誠服也如七十子
之服孔子也
易
九二見龍在田利見大人
===
象曰雷在天上大壯君子以非禮弗履
鼓之以雷霆潤之以風雨日月運行一寒
一暑乾道成男坤道成女
履和而至謙尊而光復小而辨於物恒雜
而不厭損先難而後易益長裕而不設
困窮而通井居其所而遷巽稱而隱
書
肇十有二州封十有二山濬川
爾惟德罔小萬邦惟慶
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

視其所以，觀其所由，察其所安，人焉廋哉？人焉廋哉？

天地之道，博也，厚也，高也，明也，悠也，久也。

以德服人者，中心悅而誠服也，如七十子之服孔子也。

易

九二：見龍在田，利見大人。

象曰：「雷在天上，大壯；君子以非禮弗履。」

鼓之以雷霆，潤之以風雨，日月運行，一寒一暑。乾道成男，坤道成女。

履，和而至；謙，尊而光；復，小而辨於物；恒，雜而不厭；損，先難而後易；益，長裕而不設；困，窮而通；井，居其所而遷；巽，稱而隱。

書

肇十有二州，封十有二山，濬川。

爾惟德罔小，萬邦惟慶。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Look at what a person does, observe the course he follows, and examine where he finds contentment. How can he hide? How can he hide?

The way of Heaven and Earth is broad, substantial, lofty, luminous, enduring, and lasting.

Those who submit to someone because of his virtue are pleased in their innermost hearts and submit sincerely, as the seventy disciples submitted to Kongzi (Confucius).

Book of Changes (Yijing)

Nine in the second place: A dragon appears in the fields. It is beneficial to see the great man.

The Image says: “Thunder is above Heaven: Great Strength. Thus the gentleman takes no step contrary to ritual propriety.”

They stir things with thunder and thunderbolts and moisten them with wind and rain. The sun and moon move in their courses; cold and heat alternate. The way of Qian makes the male; the way of Kun makes the female.

Treading (Lü) is harmonious and reaches its goal; Modesty (Qian) is honored and radiant; Return (Fu) is slight, yet distinguishes itself among things; Constancy (Heng) encounters complexity without weariness; Decrease (Sun) is difficult at first and easy afterward; Increase (Yi) enlarges abundance without contrivance; Oppression (Kun) is straitened yet finds passage; the Well (Jing) stays in its place yet extends its influence; the Gentle (Xun) adapts to circumstances yet remains hidden.

Book of Documents (Shu)

He first established twelve provinces, designated twelve mountains as their principal mountains, and dredged the rivers.

As for your virtuous deeds, none is too small: the myriad states will rejoice in them.

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
三八政一曰食二曰貨三曰祀四曰司空
五曰司徒六曰司冦七曰賓八曰師
治民祗懼不敢荒寧
詩
爲絺爲綌服之無斁
瞻彼中原其祁孔有儦儦俟俟或羣或友
悉率左右以燕天子旣張我弓旣挾我
矢發彼小豝殪此大兕以御賓客且以
酌醴
===
王命召伯定申伯之宅登是南邦世執其
功
於皇武王無競維烈允文文王克開厥後
嗣武受之勝殷遏劉耆定爾功
春秋
秋公會衞侯于桃丘弗遇 冬十有二月
丙午齊侯衞侯鄭伯來戰于郎 俱桓公
十年春正月齊人衞人鄭人盟于惡曹
桓公十有一年
punctuated:
三、八政：一曰食，二曰貨，三曰祀，四曰司空，五曰司徒，六曰司冦，七曰賓，八曰師。
治民祗懼，不敢荒寧。

詩
爲絺爲綌，服之無斁。
瞻彼中原，其祁孔有。儦儦俟俟，或羣或友。悉率左右，以燕天子。旣張我弓，旣挾我矢，發彼小豝，殪此大兕，以御賓客，且以酌醴。
王命召伯，定申伯之宅。登是南邦，世執其功。
於皇武王，無競維烈。允文文王，克開厥後。嗣武受之，勝殷遏劉，耆定爾功。

春秋
秋，公會衞侯于桃丘，弗遇。冬，十有二月，丙午，齊侯、衞侯、鄭伯來戰于郎。俱桓公十年。春，正月，齊人、衞人、鄭人盟于惡曹。桓公十有一年。
translation_en:
Third, the eight affairs of government: the first is food; the second, goods; the third, sacrifices; the fourth, the Minister of Works; the fifth, the Minister of Education; the sixth, the Minister of Justice; the seventh, guests; and the eighth, the army.
Govern the people with reverence and apprehension, not daring to lapse into idle ease.

Book of Odes
Make fine and coarse cloth of hemp; wear it without tiring of it.
Look at that broad plain: its game is exceedingly abundant. Some run, some stand still, in herds or in pairs. Lead all your attendants, left and right, to give pleasure to the Son of Heaven. We have drawn our bows and tucked our arrows ready; we shoot that little sow and bring down this great wild ox, to entertain the guests and pour out sweet wine.
The king commanded the Earl of Shao to establish the residence of the Earl of Shen. Raise up this southern state, and maintain its achievements from generation to generation.
Ah, august King Wu! Unrivalled were his achievements. Truly cultured was King Wen, who opened the way for his successors. His heir, King Wu, received his legacy, conquered Yin, and stopped the slaughter, firmly establishing your achievement.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In autumn, the duke went to meet the Marquis of Wei at Taoqiu, but did not meet him. In winter, in the twelfth month, on the bingwu day, the Marquis of Qi, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Zheng came to do battle at Lang. Both entries are from the tenth year of Duke Huan.
In spring, in the first month, men of Qi, Wei, and Zheng made a covenant at Ecao. The eleventh year of Duke Huan.

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
遂伐楚僖公四年諸侯遂救許僖公六年
晉人執鄭伯晉欒書帥師伐鄭成公九年
春叔弓會楚子于陳昭公九年六月叔鞅
如京師昭公二十有二年
禮記
侍坐於先生先生問焉終則對請業則起
請益則起
故聖人參於天地並於鬼神以治政也
廉直勁正莊誠之音作而民肅敬
===
孝子之有深愛者必有和氣有和氣者必
有愉色有愉色者必有婉容
第貳塲
論
先王守禮樂之本
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢選高才生受左氏穀梁春秋古文尚
書毛詩詔建初八年
擬唐以裴度爲中書侍郎同平章事誥元
punctuated:
遂伐楚，僖公四年。諸侯遂救許，僖公六年。晉人執鄭伯，晉欒書帥師伐鄭，成公九年。春，叔弓會楚子于陳，昭公九年。六月，叔鞅如京師，昭公二十有二年。
禮記
侍坐於先生，先生問焉，終則對；請業則起，請益則起。
故聖人參於天地，並於鬼神，以治政也。
廉直勁正莊誠之音作，而民肅敬。
孝子之有深愛者，必有和氣；有和氣者，必有愉色；有愉色者，必有婉容。
第貳塲
論
先王守禮樂之本。
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢選高才生受《左氏》《穀梁》《春秋》《古文尚書》《毛詩》詔，建初八年。
擬唐以裴度爲中書侍郎同平章事誥，元
translation_en:
…then attacked Chu. Fourth year of Duke Xi. The feudal lords then came to the aid of Xu. Sixth year of Duke Xi. The men of Jin seized the Earl of Zheng; Luan Shu of Jin led an army against Zheng. Ninth year of Duke Cheng. In spring, Shu Gong met the Viscount of Chu at Chen. Ninth year of Duke Zhao. In the sixth month, Shu Yang went to the royal capital. Twenty-second year of Duke Zhao.
Book of Rites
When seated in attendance upon a teacher, if the teacher asks a question, wait until he has finished before answering. Rise when requesting instruction, and rise when requesting further explanation.
Thus the sage forms a triad with Heaven and Earth and stands alongside the ghosts and spirits in conducting government.
When music expressing integrity, uprightness, firmness, rectitude, solemnity, and sincerity arises, the people become solemn and reverent.
A filial son who has deep love will surely have a gentle manner; one with a gentle manner will surely have a cheerful expression; one with a cheerful expression will surely have a gracious countenance.
Second Session
Discourse
The former kings preserved the foundations of rites and music.
One topic from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials [?].
Compose an edict in the voice of a Han emperor selecting highly talented students to study the Zuo and Guliang traditions of the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Old Text Book of Documents, and the Mao tradition of the Book of Odes. Eighth year of Jianchu.
Compose a proclamation in the voice of a Tang emperor appointing Pei Du as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Jointly Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery. Yuan…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
和十年
擬宋輔臣謝
賜
御製瑞聖園觀稼城南觀麥詩表祥符九年
判語五條
擅勾屬官
隱蔽差役
服舍違式
優恤軍屬
===
冒破物料
第叁場
策五道
問自古聖人首出庶物智垂製作範圍兩
儀其煥有之章載賡之歌渾噩弘肆光
昭汗簡所謂風行水上爲章于天不可
尚已嗣是炎劉以降趙宋以前誼辟英
君摛辭麗藻代不乏人第無裨化理讀
者病之洪惟我
punctuated:
和十年。
擬宋輔臣謝賜御製《瑞聖園觀稼》《城南觀麥》詩表，祥符九年。
判語五條：擅勾屬官；隱蔽差役；服舍違式；優恤軍屬；冒破物料。
第叁場
策五道
問：自古聖人首出庶物，智垂製作，範圍兩儀。其煥有之章、載賡之歌，渾噩弘肆，光昭汗簡。所謂風行水上，爲章于天，不可尚已。嗣是炎劉以降，趙宋以前，誼辟英君，摛辭麗藻，代不乏人。第無裨化理，讀者病之。洪惟我
translation_en:
…the tenth year of Yuanhe [815].
Draft a memorial in the voice of the Song chief councillors expressing thanks for receiving the imperially composed poems “Viewing the Crops at Ruisheng Garden” and “Viewing the Wheat South of the City.” Ninth year of Xiangfu [1016].
Five legal judgments, on the following subjects: summoning subordinate officials without authorization; concealing persons liable for labor service; clothing and residences that violate prescribed standards; granting preferential relief to military dependents; and fraudulently claiming expenditures of materials.
Third Session
Five Policy Questions
Question: From antiquity, sages have risen above all other beings, employing their wisdom to bequeath institutions and encompassing Heaven and Earth. Their resplendent writings and their songs composed in response were uncontrived, expansive, and free-flowing, shining brilliantly in the historical records. They were what is meant by wind moving over water and patterns formed in Heaven: nothing could surpass them. Thereafter, from the Liu house of Han, associated with the virtue of Fire, down through the Zhao house of Song, worthy sovereigns [?] and illustrious rulers who displayed eloquence and elegant literary ornament were found in every age. Yet their writings did not benefit moral transformation and governance, a failing readers deplore. We reverently reflect upon our…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝堯思舜文赫著簡素賁飾萬物冠
冕百王藏
秘府而播天壤百六十年于茲矣諸士子於
國初儒臣之仰讚
御製文集之珍傳諒心醉服膺久矣其詳著于
篇將轉聞於
上以為法
祖右文之助
問上世聖君事必師古遜志時敏帝學肇
===
開宿衛環列庶常吉士侍御僕從罔匪
正人其講臣固無定職勸學亦無定所
矣廼若白虎石渠講筵有地侍講侍讀
勸學有人至於宋朝經幄彌重其益弘
多備載汗青皆可指述洪惟
皇祖兵戈倥偬不忘文學橫經啓沃典學緝熈
揆之商周不多讓矣迨夫
列聖右文祖孫一道講讀尤詳此固執事者所
願聞也諸生其縷陳之毋隱
punctuated:
太祖高皇帝堯思舜文，赫著簡素，賁飾萬物，冠冕百王，藏秘府而播天壤，百六十年于茲矣。諸士子於國初儒臣之仰讚、御製文集之珍傳，諒心醉服膺久矣。其詳著于篇，將轉聞於上，以為法祖右文之助。
問：上世聖君，事必師古，遜志時敏，帝學肇開。宿衛環列，庶常吉士、侍御僕從，罔匪正人。其講臣固無定職，勸學亦無定所矣。廼若白虎、石渠，講筵有地；侍講、侍讀，勸學有人。至於宋朝，經幄彌重，其益弘多，備載汗青，皆可指述。洪惟皇祖，兵戈倥偬，不忘文學，橫經啓沃，典學緝熈，揆之商周，不多讓矣。迨夫列聖右文，祖孫一道，講讀尤詳。此固執事者所願聞也。諸生其縷陳之，毋隱。
translation_en:
… Emperor Taizu Gao, with thoughts like Yao’s and literary refinement like Shun’s, shone brilliantly upon the written page, adorned all things, and stood foremost among the rulers of every age. His writings have been preserved in the palace repositories and circulated throughout the world for some 160 years now. You candidates have surely long been captivated by, and taken deeply to heart, the reverent praises offered by the Confucian officials at the founding of the dynasty and the treasured transmission of the Collected Imperial Writings. Set these matters out fully in your essays, so that they may be conveyed to His Majesty and help him emulate his ancestor and honor literary learning.
Question: The sage rulers of antiquity invariably took antiquity as their model in their undertakings; humble in aspiration and constantly diligent, they inaugurated imperial learning. Palace guards stood arrayed about them; the worthy men appointed to regular service, their attendants, and their servants were all upright men. Yet their lecturers had no fixed offices, nor was there any fixed place for encouraging study. Later, at the White Tiger Hall and the Stone Canal Pavilion, there were designated places for scholarly lectures; with Expositors-in-waiting and Readers-in-waiting, there were designated men to encourage learning. By the Song dynasty, the imperial classical lectures acquired still greater importance and brought extensive benefits. These matters are fully recorded in the histories and can all be identified and recounted. We reverently recall that our imperial ancestor, amid the turmoil of warfare, never forgot literary learning. With the classics opened before him, he received instruction that enlightened and nourished his mind; he constantly pursued learning and ever greater illumination. Measured against the rulers of Shang and Zhou, he yielded little to them. Subsequently, the successive sage emperors honored literary learning, ancestor and descendants following a single Way, and lectures and readings became still more thorough. These are precisely the matters that we who conduct this examination wish to hear about. You students should set them out point by point, withholding nothing.

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
問漢唐宋開創之主悉有佐命翊運之臣
爲之指授而登壇裹瘡而徒鬭迨其成
功則圖形畫閣勒碑刻銘河山帶礪天
日在鑒可謂厚且至矣然議者於兹每
有憾焉得非諸君猶有萬一之鈌薄者
乎我
皇祖龍飛淮甸鹿逐胡元於一時佐命翊運諸
臣手足腹心恩禮無間崇階高爵世耀
簪纓追念存歿
===
廟庭配享殊無粟髮之可訾議者寧不爲盛德
事哉方今海内宫居而粒食擊壤而歌
遊秋毫皆我
皇祖君臣開創之遺也諸生其揄揚於篇以驗
朝家忠厚之澤
問尚書春秋仲尼裁定雖本古史魯史記
而作不可槩謂之史也自遷固而下二
晉所紀南北所載類有譏評或謂可與
左丘明鴈行可使范曄北面可使陳壽
punctuated:
問：漢、唐、宋開創之主，悉有佐命翊運之臣，爲之指授而登壇，裹瘡而徒鬭。迨其成功，則圖形畫閣，勒碑刻銘，河山帶礪，天日在鑒，可謂厚且至矣。然議者於兹每有憾焉，得非諸君猶有萬一之鈌薄者乎？我皇祖龍飛淮甸，鹿逐胡元，於一時佐命翊運諸臣，手足腹心，恩禮無間，崇階高爵，世耀簪纓，追念存歿，廟庭配享，殊無粟髮之可訾議者，寧不爲盛德事哉？方今海内宫居而粒食，擊壤而歌遊，秋毫皆我皇祖君臣開創之遺也。諸生其揄揚於篇，以驗朝家忠厚之澤。

問：《尚書》、《春秋》，仲尼裁定，雖本古史、魯史記而作，不可槩謂之史也。自遷、固而下，二晉所紀、南北所載，類有譏評。或謂可與左丘明鴈行，可使范曄北面，可使陳壽
translation_en:
Question: The founding rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song all had ministers who assisted them in receiving Heaven’s mandate and furthered their dynastic fortunes. These ministers ascended the command platform at their rulers’ direction, bound their wounds, and fought on foot [?]. Once their achievements were complete, their portraits were displayed in painted galleries and their deeds inscribed on stone monuments. Pledges were made to endure until the rivers became narrow as belts and the mountains small as whetstones, with the sun and Heaven as witnesses. Such treatment may be called generous and consummate. Yet commentators have often found cause for regret in these matters. Could it be that these rulers still showed some slight deficiency or meanness?

Our imperial ancestor rose like a dragon in the Huai region and contended for the realm against the Mongol Yuan. He treated the ministers who assisted his mandate and furthered his fortunes at that time as his own limbs and trusted confidants, showing them favor and courtesy without estrangement. With exalted ranks and high titles, their families enjoyed the splendor of official distinction for generations. He remembered both the living and the dead, and had them share in the sacrifices in the imperial ancestral temple. There was not the slightest ground for censure. Was this not an act of magnificent virtue? Today, throughout the realm, people live in houses and eat grain, play at striking the earth, and sing at their leisure. Every smallest benefit is a legacy of the founding achievements of our imperial ancestor and his ministers. You candidates should celebrate these achievements in your essays, demonstrating the blessings bestowed by the dynasty’s loyalty and generosity.

Question: The Book of Documents and the Spring and Autumn Annals were edited and settled by Zhongni [Confucius]. Although composed on the basis of ancient historical records and the historical records of Lu, they cannot simply be classified as histories. From Sima Qian and Ban Gu onward, the records of the two Jin dynasties and the accounts of the Northern and Southern dynasties have generally attracted criticism and appraisal. Some say that a historian may rank alongside Zuo Qiuming, may make Fan Ye face north as his pupil, and may make Chen Shou…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
作衙官晉史而下以奴僕命之又謂是
非頗謬於聖人崇勢利而羞貧賤輕仁
義而賤死節或譏其朱紫無別鬼怪詼
諧號稱穢史作史不以難歟迨我
憲皇誕命儒臣本朱子綱目脩續宋元綱目之
書其筆削之公義例之美殆將同符尚
書春秋而陋遷固晉唐之史於下風矣
諸君子沉酣羣史誦法
聖謨舊矣其詳言之毋略
===
問選將而任分之以閫自升陔之師牧野
之役已然矣若漢之高光宋之藝祖是
三君者以雄武之資或混一區宇或光
復舊物其選任之方駕馭之術凡懷鉛
握槧者類能言之可縷數其故歟仰惟
皇祖攘狄驅胡丕成鴻業度越千古當時論兵
馭將之略藏之冊府垂之玉牒赫赫若
前日事焉固臣工之所素講者也方今
逆庸不庭
punctuated:
作衙官，晉史而下以奴僕命之；又謂是非頗謬於聖人，崇勢利而羞貧賤，輕仁義而賤死節；或譏其朱紫無別，鬼怪詼諧，號稱穢史。作史不以難歟？迨我憲皇誕命儒臣，本朱子綱目，脩續宋元綱目之書，其筆削之公、義例之美，殆將同符《尚書》《春秋》，而陋遷固晉唐之史於下風矣。諸君子沉酣羣史，誦法聖謨舊矣，其詳言之，毋略。

問：選將而任，分之以閫，自升陔之師、牧野之役已然矣。若漢之高光、宋之藝祖，是三君者，以雄武之資，或混一區宇，或光復舊物，其選任之方、駕馭之術，凡懷鉛握槧者類能言之，可縷數其故歟？仰惟皇祖攘狄驅胡，丕成鴻業，度越千古。當時論兵馭將之略，藏之冊府，垂之玉牒，赫赫若前日事焉，固臣工之所素講者也。方今逆庸不庭，
translation_en:
…serve as subordinate officers, and consign the histories of the Jin and later periods to the rank of slaves and servants. Yet others say that their judgments of right and wrong depart considerably from those of the sages: they exalt power and profit and regard poverty and low station as shameful; they slight benevolence and righteousness and disparage dying for one’s principles. Some criticize their failure to distinguish vermilion from purple—that is, the correct from the spurious—and their accounts of ghosts, marvels, and jests, calling them “filthy histories.” Is writing history not difficult? Then our Emperor Xian solemnly commanded his Confucian officials to take Master Zhu’s Outline and Details as their basis and compile its continuation for the Song and Yuan. The impartiality of its editorial judgments and the excellence of its principles and conventions may well place it alongside the Book of Documents and the Spring and Autumn Annals, relegating the histories of Sima Qian, Ban Gu, and the Jin and Tang to an inferior position. You gentlemen have long immersed yourselves in the histories and studied and taken as your model the sage emperor’s designs. Explain these matters fully, without abbreviation.

Question: Selecting generals, appointing them, and assigning them independent military commands was already practiced at the time of the campaign at Shenggai [?] and the battle of Muye. Consider Gaozu and Guangwu of the Han and the founding emperor of the Song. These three rulers, endowed with martial prowess, either united the realm or recovered their former heritage. Their methods of selecting and appointing generals and their techniques for directing and controlling them are matters that virtually anyone who handles a writer’s lead and wooden tablets can discuss. Can you enumerate and explain them in detail? We reverently reflect that our imperial ancestor repelled the Di and expelled the Hu, accomplishing a mighty enterprise that surpassed all earlier ages. His strategies for discussing warfare and controlling generals are preserved in the imperial archives and transmitted in the imperial records, as vividly manifest as though these events had occurred only yesterday. These are certainly matters that officials have habitually studied. At present, the rebel Yong [?] refuses to acknowledge imperial authority…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
聖人赫怒遣將授鉞重兵自天而下飲馬富良
之濱勒勳銅柱之表盖有日矣諸生其
悉陳之勿諉曰軍旅之事未之學焉
punctuated: 聖人赫怒，遣將授鉞，重兵自天而下，飲馬富良之濱，勒勳銅柱之表，盖有日矣。諸生其悉陳之，勿諉曰：「軍旅之事，未之學焉。」
translation_en: …His Majesty, in blazing wrath, dispatches generals and bestows the battle-axe of command. A mighty army descends from Heaven; the day will surely come when it waters its horses on the banks of the Fuliang River and inscribes its achievements upon the bronze pillar. You candidates should set forth your views fully. Do not evade the question by saying, “I have never studied military affairs.”

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
視其所以觀其所由察其所安人焉廋哉
人焉廋哉
馬應義
同考試官教諭沈批〔是題作者體貼傳註不明文多牽滯簡明通暢僅見此篇故錄〕
考試官訓導穆批〔甚得聖人觀人之意〕
考試官教諭鄭批〔典則〕
===
惟致審於觀人則人無難知矣蓋人不可以不
知也苟觀之不審何能得其情哉昔夫子之意
若曰人固未易知也而亦不難知也顧吾所以
觀之者何如耳故始則視履焉以考其行果爲
善歟抑爲惡歟自其顯者而别之也事雖善矣
而意之所從來未可知也吾則因事焉以逆其
志果爲己歟抑爲人歟又自其微者而觀之也
所由雖善然猶未知其心之所樂者果何如也
吾於是而加察焉或好德之無斁歟抑矯强於
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

視其所以，觀其所由，察其所安，人焉廋哉？人焉廋哉？

馬應義

同考試官教諭沈批〔是題作者體貼傳註不明，文多牽滯，簡明通暢，僅見此篇，故錄。〕

考試官訓導穆批〔甚得聖人觀人之意。〕

考試官教諭鄭批〔典則。〕

惟致審於觀人，則人無難知矣。蓋人不可以不知也，苟觀之不審，何能得其情哉？昔夫子之意若曰：人固未易知也，而亦不難知也，顧吾所以觀之者何如耳。故始則視履焉，以考其行，果爲善歟？抑爲惡歟？自其顯者而别之也。事雖善矣，而意之所從來未可知也，吾則因事焉，以逆其志，果爲己歟？抑爲人歟？又自其微者而觀之也。所由雖善，然猶未知其心之所樂者果何如也。吾於是而加察焉，或好德之無斁歟？抑矯强於
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Look at what a person does, observe what motivates him, and examine what he finds contentment in. How can a person conceal himself? How can a person conceal himself?”

Ma Yingyi

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: 〔Those writing on this topic have failed to grasp clearly the meaning of the commentaries, and their prose is often strained and impeded. This essay alone was concise, clear, and fluent; hence its inclusion.〕

Comment by Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor: 〔It captures very well the sage’s intent in observing people.〕

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: 〔Classical and exemplary.〕

Only by exercising thorough scrutiny in observing people can one make them no longer difficult to know. For one cannot dispense with knowing people; if one observes them without scrutiny, how can one apprehend their true circumstances? The Master’s meaning in former times was as if to say: People are indeed not easily known, yet neither are they difficult to know. It depends only on how I observe them. Thus, at the outset, I look at their conduct to assess their actions: are they doing good, or doing evil? This is to distinguish them by what is manifest. Though their deeds may be good, the source of their intentions cannot yet be known. I therefore use their deeds to discern their purposes: are they acting for their own self-cultivation, or for the approval of others? This is further to observe them through what is subtle. Though their motives may be good, I still do not know what it is that their hearts truly delight in. At this point I scrutinize them further: do they love virtue without ever wearying of it? Or do they strain to force themselves into it for …

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
一時歟蓋有以推其至隱而究其中心之誠否
也夫始焉而求之事繼焉而求之意又繼焉而
求之心既不因事而遺意又不因意而遺心則
夫顯微無間始終一德者可以知其為君子否
則皆不免於小人之歸彼雖欲匿之也烏得而
匿之謂之曰人焉廋哉人焉廋哉信乎人莫能
欺而觀人之道盡矣抑考之夫子嘗曰吾以貌
觀人失之子羽以言觀人失之宰予他日又有
論篤色莊患不知人之訓則夫子於此一事蓋
===
屢言之豈非以人之不知則無以考德而省已
故詳於觀人者乃其所以自觀也歟
天地之道博也厚也高也明也悠也久也
段有成
同考試官教諭戴 批 平平寫出理致自在非淺學可到
考試官訓導穆 批 體認精切
考試官教諭鄭 批 善作中庸之義者
論造化本於誠而各極其盛焉蓋誠體物而不
punctuated:
一時歟？蓋有以推其至隱，而究其中心之誠否也。夫始焉而求之事，繼焉而求之意，又繼焉而求之心，既不因事而遺意，又不因意而遺心，則夫顯微無間、始終一德者，可以知其為君子；否則皆不免於小人之歸。彼雖欲匿之也，烏得而匿之？謂之曰：「人焉廋哉！人焉廋哉！」信乎人莫能欺，而觀人之道盡矣。抑考之，夫子嘗曰：「吾以貌觀人，失之子羽；以言觀人，失之宰予。」他日又有「論篤色莊」患不知人之訓，則夫子於此一事蓋屢言之。豈非以人之不知，則無以考德而省已，故詳於觀人者，乃其所以自觀也歟？
天地之道，博也、厚也、高也、明也、悠也、久也。
段有成
同考試官教諭戴批：平平寫出，理致自在，非淺學可到。
考試官訓導穆批：體認精切。
考試官教諭鄭批：善作《中庸》之義者。
論造化本於誠，而各極其盛焉。蓋誠體物而不
translation_en:
…for a moment? This allows one to probe what is most deeply hidden and determine whether the person is sincere at heart. First one seeks in his deeds, then in his intentions, and then again in his heart. If one neither neglects intentions because of deeds nor neglects the heart because of intentions, one can recognize as a gentleman someone whose manifest and hidden aspects are consistent and whose virtue remains constant from beginning to end. Otherwise, he cannot escape being classed as a petty man. Though he might wish to conceal himself, how could he do so? Hence the words: “How can a man hide? How can a man hide?” Truly, no one can deceive us, and the method of observing people is fully expressed here. Moreover, on examining the matter, we find that the Master once said: “When I judged people by their appearance, I was mistaken about Ziyu; when I judged people by their words, I was mistaken about Zai Yu.” On another occasion, in speaking of “earnest discourse and a solemn demeanor,” he also warned of the difficulty of knowing people. Thus the Master spoke repeatedly about this matter. Was this not because, without knowing others, one has no means to assess virtue and examine oneself? Careful observation of others is therefore the means by which one observes oneself.
“The Way of Heaven and Earth is broad, substantial, lofty, brilliant, far-reaching, and enduring.”
Duan Youcheng
Comment by Associate Examiner Dai, Instructor: “Written with unassuming simplicity, its principles and meaning emerge naturally. This is beyond the reach of shallow learning.”
Comment by Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor: “His understanding is precise and penetrating.”
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “One who skillfully expounds the meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean.”
The argument is that the workings of creation are rooted in sincerity, and that Heaven and Earth each thereby attain their fullest greatness. For sincerity gives substance to things and does not…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
遺也孰謂天地之極盛不本於誠之所爲乎宜
中庸言之以明至誠無息之功用也且夫天地
之道誠而已矣語其理則無二言其運則不息
故其爲道雖無聲臭之可名要之一誠實爲造
化之根柢則其盛何如哉自地言之人但見其
隤然而已而不知其質之凝也一氣之所磅礴
求之愈遠而莫知其畔岸測之愈深而莫知其
底止是何其博厚乎蓋坤道之盛所以載物者
在是矣自天言之人但見其確然而已而不知
===
其象之垂也一氣之所充周穹窿冲漠上徹於
無際宣朗昭融旁燭於無疆是何其高明乎蓋
乾道之盛所以覆物者在是矣然博厚高明又
豈局於淺近而法象於一時哉殆見地位乎下
而安貞不遷天位乎上而運轉有恒推之於前
而不見其始引之於後而莫知其終蓋一氣之
所貫徹所謂博厚高明者又極於悠久而有以
成乎物矣向使非誠則造化亦幾乎息矣烏能
各極其盛之若是哉卽此則至誠之功用可推
punctuated: 遺也。孰謂天地之極盛不本於誠之所爲乎？宜《中庸》言之，以明至誠無息之功用也。且夫天地之道，誠而已矣。語其理則無二，言其運則不息。故其爲道，雖無聲臭之可名，要之一誠，實爲造化之根柢，則其盛何如哉？自地言之，人但見其隤然而已，而不知其質之凝也，一氣之所磅礴，求之愈遠而莫知其畔岸，測之愈深而莫知其底止，是何其博厚乎！蓋坤道之盛，所以載物者在是矣。自天言之，人但見其確然而已，而不知其象之垂也，一氣之所充周，穹窿冲漠，上徹於無際；宣朗昭融，旁燭於無疆，是何其高明乎！蓋乾道之盛，所以覆物者在是矣。然博厚高明，又豈局於淺近而法象於一時哉？殆見地位乎下而安貞不遷，天位乎上而運轉有恒，推之於前而不見其始，引之於後而莫知其終。蓋一氣之所貫徹，所謂博厚高明者，又極於悠久而有以成乎物矣。向使非誠，則造化亦幾乎息矣，烏能各極其盛之若是哉？卽此則至誠之功用可推
translation_en:
…leaves nothing out. Who could say that the utmost fullness of Heaven and Earth is not rooted in what sincerity accomplishes? Fittingly, the Doctrine of the Mean speaks of this to illuminate the efficacy of perfect sincerity’s ceaseless activity. The Way of Heaven and Earth is simply sincerity. In its principle it is undivided; in its operation it is unceasing. Thus, although this Way has neither sound nor scent by which it may be named, in sum, sincerity alone is truly the root of creation and transformation. How great, then, is its fullness!

Speaking of Earth, people see only its yielding repose, without understanding that its substance is the congealing of the single vital force in its vast expanse. The farther one seeks, the less one can discover its boundaries; the deeper one measures, the less one can discover its bottom. How broad and thick it is! Herein lies the fullness of the Way of Kun, the Receptive, by which it bears all things. Speaking of Heaven, people see only its firmness, without understanding that its manifestation overhead is the single vital force filling all space. Vaulted, empty, and still, it extends upward without limit; clear, bright, and radiant, it illuminates all around without bounds. How lofty and luminous it is! Herein lies the fullness of the Way of Qian, the Creative, by which it covers all things.

Yet how could such breadth, thickness, loftiness, and luminosity be confined to what is shallow and near, or manifest their patterns and images only at a single moment? We see Earth situated below, steadfast in repose and unchanging, and Heaven situated above, constant in its revolutions. Tracing them backward, we cannot see their beginning; following them forward, we cannot know their end. The single vital force pervades them throughout: what we call breadth, thickness, loftiness, and luminosity also attain the utmost endurance and duration, thereby bringing things to completion. Were it not for sincerity, creation and transformation would all but cease. How could Heaven and Earth each attain such utmost fullness? From this, the efficacy of perfect sincerity may be inferred…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
矣大抵天地之道皆實理聖人之德皆實心其
致用一也然而位育之効必本於中和之致而
彌綸參贊非盡性者不能也是聖人有功於天
地豈特同之而已哉然則未至於聖者當何如
亦曰思誠而已矣
以德服人者中心悅而誠服也如七十子
之服孔子也
楊茂時
同考試官訓導許批題本平易作者類騁浮辭前後
總繞惟此篇見理頗明遣語簡當亦滇士之難得者
考試官訓導穆批平實
考試官教諭鄭批不事雕琢而意已足
大賢論王道得人之應而深著其出於誠也蓋
人之相感者心也王道誠矣則人之應之也又
豈有不誠者哉宜孟子以聖德之感人者形容
之也且其意若曰惟道爲能公天下而無私惟
誠可以通天下而無間蓋嘗觀諸王者德蘊諸
己必達之於政而民之沐其休澤者咸尊之爲
punctuated:
矣。大抵天地之道皆實理，聖人之德皆實心，其致用一也。然而位育之効，必本於中和之致，而彌綸參贊，非盡性者不能也。是聖人有功於天地，豈特同之而已哉？然則未至於聖者當何如？亦曰思誠而已矣。

以德服人者，中心悅而誠服也，如七十子之服孔子也。

楊茂時

同考試官訓導許批：題本平易，作者類騁浮辭，前後總繞，惟此篇見理頗明，遣語簡當，亦滇士之難得者。

考試官訓導穆批：平實。

考試官教諭鄭批：不事雕琢而意已足。

大賢論王道得人之應，而深著其出於誠也。蓋人之相感者，心也。王道誠矣，則人之應之也，又豈有不誠者哉？宜孟子以聖德之感人者形容之也。且其意若曰：惟道爲能公天下而無私，惟誠可以通天下而無間。蓋嘗觀諸王者，德蘊諸己，必達之於政，而民之沐其休澤者，咸尊之爲
translation_en:
…may thus be inferred. In general, the Way of Heaven and Earth consists entirely of real principle, and the virtue of the sage consists entirely of a sincere heart; their operation is one. Yet the effect of establishing Heaven and Earth in their proper places and nurturing all things must rest upon bringing equilibrium and harmony to their utmost. Only one who fully realizes his nature can encompass the cosmic order and assist its transforming and nurturing work. Thus the sage contributes to Heaven and Earth: how could he merely be their equal? What, then, should those who have not yet attained sagehood do? Simply strive for sincerity.

“Those who submit to another’s virtue rejoice in their inmost hearts and submit sincerely, as the seventy disciples submitted to Kongzi.”

Yang Maoshi

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor: The topic is straightforward, but writers generally indulge in empty phrases and circle around it from beginning to end. This essay alone shows a fairly clear grasp of principle and uses concise, apt language. Such work is rare indeed among the scholars of Yunnan.

Comment by Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor: Plain and substantial.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: Without elaborate ornament, the meaning is already fully expressed.

The great worthy discusses the response that the Kingly Way wins from people and makes especially clear that it springs from sincerity. For it is through the heart that people move one another. If the Kingly Way is sincere, how could people’s response to it fail to be sincere as well? It is fitting that Mengzi should describe this through the power of sagely virtue to move people. His meaning is, moreover, as if to say: only the Way can treat all under Heaven impartially, without selfishness; only sincerity can establish communion throughout all under Heaven without obstruction. Consider the true kings: the virtue they harbor within themselves must find expression in their government, and the people who enjoy their beneficent bounty all revere them as …

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
元后政非徒法必本之於心而民之蒙其惠利
者咸戴之爲父母非强之也上以誠感則下以
誠應媚茲之念盖有維諸中而不可解者非要
之也上旣好仁則下必好義親比之意盖實由
於衷而不能已也然果何所似哉譬如七十子
之於孔子仰道德之高厚終身以之爲依歸荷
恩義之綢繆無往不隆其師事陳蔡之厄困矣
猶相從而不忍舍匡人之圍急矣雖冒險在所
不辭盖其感之者皆至德而服之者皆真心區
===
區尊禮之間不足言矣王者思服之民亦何以
異於是哉噫此王道之所以爲大也歟抑論之
三代以降王道之不行也久矣漢文之天資近
道然亦雜於黃老願治如唐太宗猶未免有假
之之意然皆足以致一代之治况純用德教者
其效當何如耶至是然後知孟子之言爲有驗
彼謂王道不可行者特未之思耳
易
九二見龍在田利見大人
punctuated:
元后。政非徒法，必本之於心，而民之蒙其惠利者，咸戴之爲父母。非强之也，上以誠感，則下以誠應，媚茲之念，盖有維諸中而不可解者；非要之也，上旣好仁，則下必好義，親比之意，盖實由於衷而不能已也。然果何所似哉？譬如七十子之於孔子，仰道德之高厚，終身以之爲依歸；荷恩義之綢繆，無往不隆其師事。陳蔡之厄困矣，猶相從而不忍舍；匡人之圍急矣，雖冒險，在所不辭。盖其感之者皆至德，而服之者皆真心，區區尊禮之間不足言矣。王者思服之民，亦何以異於是哉？噫！此王道之所以爲大也歟！抑論之，三代以降，王道之不行也久矣。漢文之天資近道，然亦雜於黃老；願治如唐太宗，猶未免有假之之意。然皆足以致一代之治，况純用德教者，其效當何如耶？至是然後知孟子之言爲有驗，彼謂王道不可行者，特未之思耳。

易

九二：見龍在田，利見大人。
translation_en:
…their sovereign. Government is not merely a matter of laws; it must be rooted in the heart. The people who receive its benefits all revere their ruler as a father and mother. This is not because they are compelled: when those above move others through sincerity, those below respond with sincerity. Their affectionate thoughts are bound within their hearts and cannot be undone. Nor is this affection exacted from them: when those above delight in benevolence, those below will assuredly delight in righteousness. Their desire for closeness truly arises from within and cannot be restrained.

What, then, does this resemble? It is like the relationship of the seventy disciples to Confucius. They looked up to the loftiness and depth of his moral virtue and took him as their guide and refuge throughout their lives. Receiving his deeply entwined kindness and righteousness, wherever they went they served him with the utmost reverence as their teacher. Though the ordeal in Chen and Cai was grievous, they continued to follow him and could not bear to leave. Though the encirclement by the people of Kuang was perilous, they did not shrink from facing danger. What moved them was consummate virtue, and their submission came entirely from sincere hearts. Mere outward observances of respect scarcely deserve mention. How could the people who lovingly submit to a true king differ from them? Ah! Is this not what makes the Kingly Way great?

To consider the matter further: since the Three Dynasties, the Kingly Way has long gone unpracticed. Emperor Wen of Han was naturally close to the Way, yet his rule was also mixed with the teachings of Huang-Lao. Even one as eager for good government as Emperor Taizong of Tang could not altogether escape the intention of borrowing the Way for his own purposes. Yet both were able to bring good order to their age. How much greater, then, should be the effects of relying wholly upon moral instruction? Only then do we recognize that Mencius’s words are borne out. Those who say that the Kingly Way cannot be practiced have simply failed to reflect upon it.

Book of Changes

Nine in the second place: A dragon appears in the field. It is beneficial to see the great man.

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
馬應義
同考試官教諭沈批九二備龍德而當正中之時者
也作者措辭多類九五殊失本旨此作得之
考試官訓導穆批理明辭暢
考試官教諭鄭批發揮象占明當可取
聖人於乾之九二擬以顯德之象示以仰德之
占盖九二備龍德於已爲人所利見者也聖人
擬象示占之意良有以哉昔伏羲畫乾之卦爻
至九二周公繫辭盖謂非德不足以善世非時
===
不足以顯德九二君子備剛健中正之德當出
潜離隱之時位雖在下也然盛德至善之懿不
俟教令而輝光所被自有舍舊從新之化時雖
未遇也然天德王道之妙無假言說而心迹所
及自有遷善敏德之休是猶神龍起蟄霖雨將
於此而普施也龍見于田膏澤將於此而廣布
也其象如此占者值之當何如哉必以是大人
者偉然斯世之望于焉尊德樂道而趨承之不
違卓乎萬民之瞻于焉致敬盡禮而親比之恐
punctuated:
馬應義

同考試官教諭沈批：「九二備龍德而當正中之時者也。作者措辭多類九五，殊失本旨，此作得之。」
考試官訓導穆批：「理明辭暢。」
考試官教諭鄭批：「發揮象占，明當可取。」

聖人於乾之九二，擬以顯德之象，示以仰德之占。盖九二備龍德於已，爲人所利見者也。聖人擬象示占之意，良有以哉！昔伏羲畫乾之卦爻，至九二，周公繫辭，盖謂非德不足以善世，非時不足以顯德。九二君子備剛健中正之德，當出潜離隱之時。位雖在下也，然盛德至善之懿，不俟教令，而輝光所被，自有舍舊從新之化；時雖未遇也，然天德王道之妙，無假言說，而心迹所及，自有遷善敏德之休。是猶神龍起蟄，霖雨將於此而普施也；龍見于田，膏澤將於此而廣布也。其象如此，占者值之，當何如哉？必以是大人者，偉然斯世之望，于焉尊德樂道，而趨承之不違；卓乎萬民之瞻，于焉致敬盡禮，而親比之恐
translation_en:
Ma Yingyi

Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor, comments: “Nine in the second place possesses the dragon’s virtue and stands at a time of proper centrality. Writers often phrase their answers as though discussing nine in the fifth place, seriously missing the original meaning. This composition grasps it.”
Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is clear and the language fluent.”
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “Its exposition of the image and prognostication is clear, appropriate, and worthy of acceptance.”

For nine in the second place of Qian, the sage devised an image of manifest virtue and supplied a prognostication indicating that virtue should be looked up to. For nine in the second place possesses the dragon’s virtue within himself and is one whom it benefits others to see. There is indeed good reason for the sage’s intention in devising the image and supplying the prognostication! Long ago, Fuxi drew the hexagram Qian and its lines. When the Duke of Zhou appended a statement to nine in the second place, his meaning was that without virtue one cannot bring goodness to the world, and without the proper time one cannot manifest virtue. The gentleman represented by nine in the second place possesses the virtues of strength, vigor, centrality, and correctness, and has reached the time to emerge from concealment and leave seclusion. Although his position is low, the excellence of his abundant virtue and supreme goodness needs no teaching or commands: wherever its radiance reaches, people are naturally transformed, abandoning the old and following the new. Although he has not yet met his opportunity, the subtle efficacy of heavenly virtue and the kingly Way requires no verbal explanation: wherever his intentions and deeds extend, there naturally follows the blessing of turning toward goodness and striving in virtue. This is like a divine dragon rising from hibernation, with soaking rains about to fall everywhere; like a dragon appearing in the fields, with nourishing moisture about to spread far and wide. Such is the image. What, then, should someone who encounters it in divination do? Surely, recognizing this great man as the magnificent hope of the age, one should honor virtue and delight in the Way, hastening to attend upon him without departing from him; recognizing him as the exalted focus of all the people’s regard, one should show reverence, fulfill every courtesy, and draw close to him, fearing…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
後上焉者寤寐臣隣而克勤乎下交之儀則謀
猷相資大業以之而成矣下焉者仰止神聖而
聿興乎快覩之念則矜式所在習俗以之而美
矣何利如之占者若有見龍之德則當利見九
五在上之大人也周公擬象示占之意精矣哉
抑因是而求之大舜矣歷山之耕河濱之陶身
雖側微而濬哲文明温恭允塞其德固已昭著
於天下而升聞于帝堯矣當時耕者讓畔器不
苦窳以至主祭而神享主事而民安澤及於物
===
豈非天下利見之時乎是必有如是聖人之德
而後可以當是爻之用
履和而至謙尊而光復小而辨於物恒雜
而不厭損先難而後易益長裕而不設
困窮而通井居其所而遷巽稱而隱
劉舉良
同考試官教諭沈批講九德抑揚處辭不費而理已
具可以占所養矣
考試官訓導穆批文有變態自超衆作
punctuated:
後。上焉者寤寐臣隣，而克勤乎下交之儀，則謀猷相資，大業以之而成矣；下焉者仰止神聖，而聿興乎快覩之念，則矜式所在，習俗以之而美矣。何利如之？占者若有見龍之德，則當利見九五在上之大人也。周公擬象示占之意精矣哉！抑因是而求之，大舜矣！歷山之耕，河濱之陶，身雖側微，而濬哲文明，温恭允塞，其德固已昭著於天下，而升聞于帝堯矣。當時耕者讓畔，器不苦窳，以至主祭而神享，主事而民安，澤及於物，豈非天下利見之時乎？是必有如是聖人之德，而後可以當是爻之用。

履和而至，謙尊而光，復小而辨於物，恒雜而不厭，損先難而後易，益長裕而不設，困窮而通，井居其所而遷，巽稱而隱。

劉舉良

同考試官教諭沈批：講九德抑揚處，辭不費而理已具，可以占所養矣。

考試官訓導穆批：文有變態，自超衆作。
translation_en:
…falling behind. If those above yearn, waking and sleeping, for ministers close to them, and diligently observe the proprieties of intercourse with those below, their plans and counsels will support one another, and great undertakings will thereby be accomplished. If those below look up to the sage and divine man and eagerly wish for the joy of beholding him, they will have a model to emulate, and customs will thereby improve. What benefit could equal this? If the person consulting the oracle possesses the virtue of the dragon appearing in the field, it is fitting that he should find it beneficial to see the great man above, in the nine in the fifth place. How refined was the Duke of Zhou’s intention in devising images and indicating their divinatory meaning!

If we seek an example of this, there is the great Shun. When he plowed at Lishan and made pottery on the riverbank, his station was obscure and humble; yet he was profoundly wise, cultivated and enlightened, gentle and reverent, sincere and trustworthy. His virtue was already manifest throughout the world, and its fame had reached Emperor Yao. At that time, cultivators yielded the boundaries of their fields to one another, and pottery was no longer poorly made. Later, when he presided over sacrifices, the spirits accepted them; when he directed affairs, the people were at peace, and his beneficence extended to all things. Was this not a time when all under Heaven benefited from seeing him? Only one who possesses such sagely virtue can fulfill the function of this line.

“Treading is harmonious and reaches its goal; Modesty is honored and radiant; Return is slight, yet distinguishes itself among things; Constancy encounters complexity without weariness; Decrease is difficult at first and easy afterward; Increase brings lasting abundance without contrivance; Oppression is straitened yet finds passage; the Well remains in its place yet reaches others; the Gentle adapts to circumstances yet remains hidden.”

Liu Juliang

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: “In explaining the contrasting qualities of the nine virtues, he uses no superfluous words, yet fully conveys their principles. From this one can judge the depth of his cultivation.”

Comment by Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor: “The composition displays varied forms of expression and naturally surpasses the other submissions.”

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭鄭批簡潔粋徹得易本旨
大傳論九卦之德之妙以明處憂患之道也夫
易卦之德周天下之用也即九卦而德皆不偏
焉其於處憂患也何有昔吾夫子大傳論九卦
之德而再陳之若謂易非聖人不能作德非諸
卦不能備然或涉於一偏未免滯於日用是故
禮者順人情而非强世若和矣然品節詳明事
理精當而實爲至焉謙者德欲盛而禮欲恭若
卑矣然天道所益人道所好而尊且光焉復以
===
一陽生於羣陰之下何其小也然善端既復欲
不能間矣豈以小而無辨乎恒以一身混於紛
華之中何其雜也然常德在我久而不變矣豈
以雜而有厭乎至若懲忿窒慾以脩身損先爲
難從事既久則無忿可懲無慾可窒也何易如
之遷善改過以長善益實自裕究而言之則善
所本有過所本無也可設之有窮與困巽困爲
柔揜不能以自振者但實德既脩心無怨尤無
入而不自得矣靜與動反井居其所不能以自
punctuated:
考試官敎諭鄭批：簡潔粋徹，得易本旨。
大傳論九卦之德之妙，以明處憂患之道也。夫易卦之德，周天下之用也。即九卦而德皆不偏焉，其於處憂患也何有？昔吾夫子大傳論九卦之德而再陳之，若謂易非聖人不能作，德非諸卦不能備。然或涉於一偏，未免滯於日用。是故禮者，順人情而非强世，若和矣；然品節詳明，事理精當，而實爲至焉。謙者，德欲盛而禮欲恭，若卑矣；然天道所益，人道所好，而尊且光焉。復以一陽生於羣陰之下，何其小也！然善端既復，欲不能間矣，豈以小而無辨乎？恒以一身混於紛華之中，何其雜也！然常德在我，久而不變矣，豈以雜而有厭乎？至若懲忿窒慾以脩身，損先爲難；從事既久，則無忿可懲，無慾可窒也，何易如之？遷善改過以長善，益實自裕；究而言之，則善所本有，過所本無也，可設之有？窮與困巽，困爲柔揜，不能以自振者；但實德既脩，心無怨尤，無入而不自得矣。靜與動反，井居其所，不能以自
translation_en:
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “Concise, pure, and penetrating; it grasps the fundamental meaning of the Book of Changes.”

The Great Commentary discusses the subtle workings of the virtues of the nine hexagrams to illuminate the way to meet anxiety and adversity. The virtues of the hexagrams of the Book of Changes encompass every application under Heaven. Even in these nine hexagrams, their virtues are all free of one-sidedness: what difficulty, then, could there be in meeting anxiety and adversity? Formerly, our Master discussed the virtues of the nine hexagrams in the Great Commentary and set them forth a second time. It is as though he were saying that only a sage could compose the Changes, and only through the various hexagrams could virtue be fully represented. Yet any lapse into one-sidedness inevitably obstructs its application in daily life.

Thus ritual follows human feelings without coercing the world, and seems harmonious; yet its distinctions and regulations are detailed and clear, and its handling of affairs and principles is exact and fitting, so it truly reaches perfection. In Modesty (Qian), virtue should be abundant and ritual conduct respectful, seemingly placing one low; yet this is what the Way of Heaven augments and the way of humanity favors, so it is honored and radiant. In Return (Fu), a single yang line arises beneath the assembled yin lines: how small it is! Yet once the beginnings of goodness have returned, desires cannot intrude. Could its smallness mean that it lacks discernment? In Constancy (Heng), one mingles amid the world’s manifold splendors: how mixed its circumstances are! Yet enduring virtue resides within oneself and remains unchanged over time. Could this mingling produce weariness?

As for restraining anger and blocking desires to cultivate oneself, Decrease (Sun) is difficult at first. Once one has practiced it for a long time, however, there is no anger left to restrain and no desire left to block. What could be easier? Turning toward goodness and correcting faults to foster goodness, Increase (Yi) indeed brings abundance of itself. Examined ultimately, goodness is what one originally possesses, and faults are what one originally lacks: how could these be artificially established [?]?

“Exhaustion and distress, yielding” [?]: in Oppression (Kun), the firm is covered by the yielding and cannot raise itself up. Yet once substantial virtue has been cultivated, the heart harbors neither resentment nor blame, and wherever one goes, one is at ease. Stillness is the opposite of movement: the Well (Jing) remains in its place and cannot itself …

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
動者但剛中爲泉上出爲功自有利澤及物矣
以至巽德之制盖以一心之權度運萬用之機
宜經以處其常也權以通其變也泛應曲當又
何形迹之可窺乎噫君子反身脩德以處憂患
之道盖已盡於此矣抑考文王當羑里之時而
演易以憂患之情發之辭變象占之間皆開物
成務之意故夫子曰其辭危危者使平由是推
之六十四卦皆德也夫子獨陳九卦者偶舉此
以見例耳若乾言誠坤言敬敬立而誠存聖學
===
無餘事也又以見乾坤之理可以總括六十四
卦之蘊
書
肇十有二州封十有二山濬川
段有成
同考試官教諭戴 批 不蹈陳言自出一機軸簡潔明
盡無踰此篇
考試官訓導穆 批 語意純正
考試官教諭鄭 批 分析明而有含蓄
punctuated:
動者，但剛中爲泉，上出爲功，自有利澤及物矣。以至巽德之制，盖以一心之權度，運萬用之機宜，經以處其常也，權以通其變也。泛應曲當，又何形迹之可窺乎？噫！君子反身脩德以處憂患之道，盖已盡於此矣。抑考文王當羑里之時而演易，以憂患之情發之，辭、變、象、占之間，皆開物成務之意。故夫子曰：「其辭危，危者使平。」由是推之，六十四卦皆德也。夫子獨陳九卦者，偶舉此以見例耳。若乾言誠，坤言敬，敬立而誠存，聖學無餘事也。又以見乾坤之理，可以總括六十四卦之蘊。
書
肇十有二州，封十有二山，濬川。
段有成
同考試官教諭戴批：不蹈陳言，自出一機軸，簡潔明盡，無踰此篇。
考試官訓導穆批：語意純正。
考試官教諭鄭批：分析明而有含蓄。
translation_en:
…move on its own; yet its firmness at the center constitutes the spring, and bringing water upward constitutes its achievement, so that its benefits naturally extend to other things. As for the regulation of virtue represented by Xun (the Gentle), this is to use the weighing and measuring capacity of the single mind to direct the appropriate responses to myriad circumstances: constant principles address what is regular, while discretionary judgment accommodates change. Responding broadly and fitting every particular, what outward traces could it leave to be discerned? Ah! The gentleman’s way of turning inward to cultivate virtue and thereby dealing with trouble and adversity is fully expressed here.
Consider, moreover, how King Wen elaborated the Changes while confined at Youli, giving expression to his feelings of anxiety and distress. In its statements, transformations, images, and divinations, his intention throughout was to disclose the nature of things and bring undertakings to completion. Thus the Master said: “Its statements convey danger; awareness of danger brings peace.” By extension, all sixty-four hexagrams concern virtue. That the Master set out only nine hexagrams means merely that he selected these as examples. Thus Qian (the Creative) speaks of sincerity, and Kun (the Receptive) of reverence. When reverence is established and sincerity preserved, nothing remains beyond these in the learning of the sages. This also shows that the principles of Qian and Kun can encompass the profundities of all sixty-four hexagrams.
Book of Documents
“He first established twelve provinces, designated twelve mountains as their principal mountains, and dredged the rivers.”
Duan Youcheng
Comment by Associate Examiner Dai, Instructor: “He does not tread the worn paths of conventional phrasing, but devises an approach of his own. For concision, clarity, and completeness, no essay surpasses this one.”
Comment by Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor: “The language and meaning are pure and correct.”
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “The analysis is clear, yet leaves meaning implicit.”

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
史臣記聖人疆理之周而防患之豫焉夫治莫
先於疆理而亦莫急於水患之防也聖人因舊
而增脩之亦惟其宜而已矣昔史臣之意若曰
人徒知有虞之治為無為而不知其初之大有
為也何則九州之制昉自中古及舜即位以冀
青之地視之他州為廣也於是始分冀之東為
并東北為幽又分青之東北為營也若夫九州
則惟仍其舊焉豈非所謂十二州乎增官屬溥
化理而吏治為之一新也九山之封其來已乆
===
然州域既增則亦不可以無鎮也於是封營丘
於幽恒山於并又封醫無閭之山於營若夫九
山則惟因之而不改也豈非所謂十二山乎立
表識崇祝號而祀事為之有屬也九川滌源似
在不必濬矣舜則以為水患出於不測而備禦
在所當先乃為之脩利隄防以止其潰為之通
達溝瀆以開其障使凡十二州之水莫不各安
其所庶有以保平成之偉績也是則州之增非
侈也山之封非瀆也而川之濬又非過慮也皆
punctuated: 史臣記聖人疆理之周，而防患之豫焉。夫治莫先於疆理，而亦莫急於水患之防也。聖人因舊而增脩之，亦惟其宜而已矣。昔史臣之意若曰：人徒知有虞之治為無為，而不知其初之大有為也。何則？九州之制昉自中古，及舜即位，以冀青之地視之，他州為廣也。於是始分冀之東為并，東北為幽，又分青之東北為營也。若夫九州，則惟仍其舊焉。豈非所謂十二州乎？增官屬，溥化理，而吏治為之一新也。九山之封，其來已乆，然州域既增，則亦不可以無鎮也。於是封營丘於幽，恒山於并，又封醫無閭之山於營。若夫九山，則惟因之而不改也。豈非所謂十二山乎？立表識，崇祝號，而祀事為之有屬也。九川滌源，似在不必濬矣。舜則以為水患出於不測，而備禦在所當先，乃為之脩利隄防以止其潰，為之通達溝瀆以開其障，使凡十二州之水莫不各安其所，庶有以保平成之偉績也。是則州之增非侈也，山之封非瀆也，而川之濬又非過慮也，皆
translation_en:
The court historian records the sage’s thorough ordering of the territory and his foresight in preventing calamities. In government, nothing takes precedence over ordering the territory, and nothing is more urgent than guarding against floods. The sage expanded and improved existing arrangements, doing only what circumstances required. The historian’s meaning was perhaps this: people know only that the rule of Youyu was one of nonaction; they do not know how much purposeful action went into its beginnings. Why was this so? The system of nine provinces originated in middle antiquity. When Shun ascended the throne, he considered the territories of Ji and Qing to be more extensive than the other provinces [?]. He therefore first divided off eastern Ji to form Bing and its northeast to form You, and also divided off northeastern Qing to form Ying. As for the nine original provinces, he retained their existing arrangements. Were these not the so-called twelve provinces? He increased the subordinate official staff and spread moral transformation and orderly government, thereby renewing official administration.

The designation of the nine mountains had a long history. Yet once the provincial territories had increased in number, the new provinces too could not lack their guardian mountains. He therefore designated Yingqiu in You, Hengshan in Bing, and the mountain of Yiwulü in Ying. As for the nine original mountains, he retained them without alteration. Were these not the so-called twelve mountains? He erected markers and honored the mountains with titles used in ritual invocations, so that sacrificial observances had their assigned objects.

The sources of the nine rivers had been cleared, and further dredging might have seemed unnecessary. Shun, however, held that floods arise unexpectedly and that defensive preparations must come first. He therefore repaired and improved embankments to prevent breaches, and opened up ditches and channels to clear obstructions, ensuring that the waters throughout all twelve provinces remained within their proper bounds. In this way he hoped to preserve the great achievement of bringing the land and waters into order. Thus, increasing the number of provinces was no extravagance; designating the mountains was no profanation of ritual; and dredging the rivers was no excessive anxiety. All were…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
行所無事而已聖人何心哉抑論之舜卽位之
初汲汲焉惟土宇山川是務若於治不甚切者
殊不知體國經野乃先王之所以奉若天道舍
之不務其何以一道德而同風俗也哉噫帝舜
不復作矣然而萬世而下猶可以按迹職方興
思河洛謂非當時之功不可也
三八政一曰食二曰貨三曰祀四曰司空
五曰司徒六曰司宼七曰賓八曰師
陶庚
===
同考試官敎諭戴批質而不俚核而有序箕子演疇
之意藹然可見
考試官訓導穆批講八政處不晦不混宜錄以式
考試官敎諭鄭批整潔得體
君子之演八政必以序而列其目也蓋王者之
政凡以為民但所係不能無緩急耳宜乎箕子
叙次之以告武王治天下之法也且其意若曰
禹因洛書左三之數而第為八政其理則因乎
天而不可易其用則切於民而不可離何以言
punctuated:
行所無事而已，聖人何心哉？抑論之，舜卽位之初，汲汲焉惟土宇山川是務，若於治不甚切者。殊不知，體國經野，乃先王之所以奉若天道；舍之不務，其何以一道德而同風俗也哉？噫！帝舜不復作矣。然而萬世而下，猶可以按迹職方，興思河洛，謂非當時之功，不可也。
三、八政：一曰食，二曰貨，三曰祀，四曰司空，五曰司徒，六曰司宼，七曰賓，八曰師。
陶庚
同考試官敎諭戴批：質而不俚，核而有序，箕子演疇之意，藹然可見。
考試官訓導穆批：講八政處，不晦不混，宜錄以式。
考試官敎諭鄭批：整潔得體。
君子之演八政，必以序而列其目也。蓋王者之政，凡以為民，但所係不能無緩急耳。宜乎箕子叙次之，以告武王治天下之法也。且其意若曰：禹因洛書左三之數，而第為八政，其理則因乎天而不可易，其用則切於民而不可離。何以言
translation_en:
…merely acting without forcing matters. What private purpose could the sage have had? Yet consider this: when Shun first took the throne, he urgently devoted himself to the territory, mountains, and rivers, seemingly matters of no immediate relevance to government. Such a view fails to recognize that laying out the capital and ordering the countryside were how the former kings reverently followed the Way of Heaven. If these tasks were neglected, how could moral principles be unified and customs brought into accord? Alas! Emperor Shun will never arise again. Yet even ten thousand generations later, one can still examine his traces in the records of territorial administration and reflect upon the Yellow and Luo Rivers. One cannot deny that this results from his achievements at that time.
Third, the eight affairs of government: the first is food; the second, goods; the third, sacrifices; the fourth, the Minister of Works; the fifth, the Minister of Education; the sixth, the Minister of Justice; the seventh, guests; and the eighth, the army.
Tao Geng
Comment by Associate Examiner Dai, Instructor: Substantial without being vulgar, precise and orderly: Jizi’s intention in expounding the categories is abundantly evident.
Comment by Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor: The exposition of the eight affairs of government is neither obscure nor confused. It should be recorded as a model.
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: Neat, polished, and appropriate in form.
When the gentleman expounds the eight affairs of government, he must enumerate them in their proper order. The government of a true king is entirely for the people, but the matters it concerns necessarily differ in urgency. It was therefore fitting that Jizi should arrange them in sequence to explain to King Wu the method of governing All under Heaven. His meaning was approximately this: Yu followed the number three on the left of the Luo Writing and assigned the eight affairs of government to the third category. Their principles accord with Heaven and cannot be altered; their application intimately concerns the people and cannot be dispensed with. How can this be explained…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
之彼民無食則無以為命而重農力本在所當
先故一曰食焉非貨則無以為資而阜財惠商
亦不容緩故二曰貨焉生養遂而孝敬生則祭
以報本亦理之所不容已者是以有祀焉而列
之於三然民不可渙散而無居則有司空掌土
而宮室之制興故居四焉亦不可逸居而無教
則有司徒掌教而學校之建廣故居五焉道化
尼而淫慝作則刑以禁姦亦勢之所不能免者
是以有司宼之設而序之於六人情非禮不通
===
於是乎有賓以親邦國賓處乎順故居七焉禍
亂非兵不弭於是乎有師以平邦國師權乎變
是以居末而為八政之終事焉為治者果能行
此則民生無不厚而彝倫又豈有不叙者哉抑
因是而考之武王焉重民五教惟食喪祭而六
典建官終周世不改孰謂非箕子啓之耶至於
所以為之則又本之人君之心是以列五事於
八政之先而首以敬用為言故曰必有關雎麟
趾之意然後可以行周官之法度
punctuated: 之？彼民無食則無以為命，而重農力本在所當先，故一曰食焉。非貨則無以為資，而阜財惠商亦不容緩，故二曰貨焉。生養遂而孝敬生，則祭以報本亦理之所不容已者，是以有祀焉，而列之於三。然民不可渙散而無居，則有司空掌土，而宮室之制興，故居四焉。亦不可逸居而無教，則有司徒掌教，而學校之建廣，故居五焉。道化尼而淫慝作，則刑以禁姦亦勢之所不能免者，是以有司宼之設，而序之於六。人情非禮不通，於是乎有賓以親邦國；賓處乎順，故居七焉。禍亂非兵不弭，於是乎有師以平邦國；師權乎變，是以居末，而為八政之終事焉。為治者果能行此，則民生無不厚，而彝倫又豈有不叙者哉？抑因是而考之武王焉，重民五教，惟食喪祭，而六典建官，終周世不改，孰謂非箕子啓之耶？至於所以為之，則又本之人君之心，是以列五事於八政之先，而首以敬用為言。故曰：「必有關雎麟趾之意，然後可以行周官之法度。」
translation_en:
…this? Without food, the people have no means of sustaining life; therefore, honoring agriculture and devoting effort to the fundamental occupation must come first. Thus the first item is food. Without goods, they have no resources, and increasing wealth and benefiting commerce likewise admit of no delay. Thus the second item is goods. Once their livelihood and nurture are secured, filial devotion and reverence arise. Sacrifices to repay their sources of existence are then something that principle does not permit them to forgo. Hence sacrifices are included and ranked third. Yet the people cannot be left scattered and without dwellings. Thus the Minister of Works administers the land, and the institutions governing palaces and houses arise; hence this office ranks fourth. Nor may the people dwell at ease without instruction. Thus the Minister of Education oversees instruction, and the establishment of schools is extended; hence this office ranks fifth. When moral transformation is obstructed and depravity arises, punishments to restrain wrongdoing become an unavoidable necessity. Hence the office of Minister of Justice is established and ranked sixth. Human sentiments cannot find expression without ritual, so there is the reception of guests to foster amity among the states. The reception of guests belongs to the orderly course of affairs, and therefore ranks seventh. Disaster and disorder cannot be quelled without armed force, so there is the army to pacify the states. Military action requires discretionary responses to exceptional circumstances; hence it comes last, as the final undertaking among the eight measures of government. If those who govern can indeed carry these out, the people’s livelihood will everywhere prosper. How, then, could the enduring human relationships fail to be properly ordered?
Moreover, let us examine King Wu in light of this. He attached importance to the people and the five teachings, and to food, mourning, and sacrifice; offices were established under the six canons of administration and remained unchanged throughout the Zhou dynasty. Who could say that Jizi did not enlighten him in these matters? As for what enables these measures to be carried out, it is rooted in the ruler’s heart. Hence the five personal affairs are placed before the eight measures of government, introduced with the injunction to apply them reverently. Thus it is said: “Only when one possesses the spirit of ‘The Ospreys’ (Guanju) and ‘The Qilin’s Hoofs’ (Linzhi) can one put into practice the statutes and institutions of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan).”

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
詩
王命召伯定申伯之宅登是南邦世執其
功
楊茂時
同考試官訓導許批〔推本黍苗以著城謝之功於世執處以作式為輔寓說自非他作可及〕
考試官訓導穆批〔先王封申伯之意是如此〕
考試官教諭鄭批〔溫潤詳盡錄之〕
周王封親臣有以建其業而欲以永其傳也夫
===
建國而命大臣親之可謂致重矣使傳之不永
又何以裕其後哉宣王之舅申伯出封于謝尹
吉甫作詩以送之及此若謂申伯之生也嶽實
降神而其功也懋在王室謝邑之封何如哉彼
立國建侯周之懿典也王以召伯而授厥命使
之因是謝人以經營其居列爵分土國有常經
也召伯以司空而任若事于焉率彼烝徒以大
啓其宇以定經制以辨章程奠雄鎮于一方肅
庸謝功于是乎告成矣原隰水泉之治墉垣家
punctuated:
詩

王命召伯，定申伯之宅，登是南邦，世執其功。

楊茂時

同考試官訓導許批〔推本黍苗以著城謝之功，於世執處以作式為輔寓說，自非他作可及。〕
考試官訓導穆批〔先王封申伯之意是如此。〕
考試官教諭鄭批〔溫潤詳盡，錄之。〕

周王封親臣，有以建其業而欲以永其傳也。夫建國而命大臣親之，可謂致重矣。使傳之不永，又何以裕其後哉？宣王之舅申伯出封于謝，尹吉甫作詩以送之。及此，若謂申伯之生也，嶽實降神，而其功也，懋在王室。謝邑之封何如哉？彼立國建侯，周之懿典也。王以召伯而授厥命，使之因是謝人以經營其居。列爵分土，國有常經也。召伯以司空而任若事，于焉率彼烝徒，以大啓其宇，以定經制，以辨章程。奠雄鎮于一方，肅庸謝功，于是乎告成矣。原隰水泉之治，墉垣家
translation_en:
Book of Odes

“The king commanded the Earl of Shao to establish the Earl of Shen’s residence, to raise up this southern domain, and to maintain its achievements through the generations.”

Yang Maoshi

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor: 〔The essay traces matters back to “Millet Sprouts” (Shu miao) to bring out the achievement of fortifying Xie. In discussing “maintain through the generations,” it introduces “serving as a model” as a supporting explanation. Other compositions certainly cannot match it.〕
Comment by Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor: 〔Such was the former king’s intention in enfeoffing the Earl of Shen.〕
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: 〔Gentle and polished, thorough and detailed. Include it.〕

When the king of Zhou enfeoffed a minister close to him, he provided the means to establish that minister’s undertaking and wished to perpetuate its transmission. Indeed, to establish a state and command a great minister to attend personally to it may be called the utmost mark of regard. If its transmission were not enduring, how could provision be made for his descendants?

The Earl of Shen, King Xuan’s maternal uncle, departed to take up his fief at Xie, and Yin Jifu composed a poem to see him off. At this passage, it is as though he were saying: at the Earl of Shen’s birth, the sacred mountain indeed sent down its divine power, and his meritorious service to the royal house was outstanding. What, then, of his enfeoffment at Xie?

Establishing states and investing lords was an admirable institution of Zhou. The king entrusted his command to the Earl of Shao, directing him to draw upon the people of Xie to plan and build the Earl of Shen’s residence. Assigning ranks and apportioning territory followed the state’s established norms. The Earl of Shao, as Minister of Works, undertook this task. Thereupon he led the assembled workers to enlarge the domain, establish its institutional arrangements, and distinguish its regulations. A mighty stronghold was established in that region; the work at Xie was reverently carried out and brought to completion. The ordering of the uplands and lowlands, waters and springs, and the walls and houses …

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
室之立慰王心于九重翼翼南國于是乎底績
矣然此豈特示寵異于一時大封拜于今日而
已哉蓋繼序其皇君之所以望臣也將俾世其
職者保有成業于以衍國祚於靈長不顯亦世
士之所以生周也將俾作之後者念茲戎功于
以綿國脉于悠久世德之作求永為南國之式
後之繼申猶申之繼甫也而蕃翰者有所藉矣
舊服之纘承恒為周室之輔後賢之繼述有光
于上世之開承也而于宣者有所賴矣是則申
===
伯之封非倖致宣王之錫非濫及有周封建之
典于是可見而吉甫播揚以為贈也固宜抑論
申伯以元舅之親出封于謝宣王豈直為親親
已也蓋申伯德業聞望足為當時之重而謝之
為邑實作鎮于南土所以鎮定而綏服之者亦
不可匪其人也崧高之作反覆於蕃翰作式為
憲之說而激勸感發之意默寓其間故讀其詩
則宣王親賢懷遠之道當時友朋勸示之益俱
可想見于千載之上
punctuated:
室之立，慰王心于九重，翼翼南國，于是乎底績矣。然此豈特示寵異于一時，大封拜于今日而已哉？蓋繼序其皇，君之所以望臣也。將俾世其職者保有成業，于以衍國祚於靈長。不顯亦世，士之所以生周也。將俾作之後者念茲戎功，于以綿國脉于悠久。世德之作求，永為南國之式，後之繼申，猶申之繼甫也，而蕃翰者有所藉矣。舊服之纘承，恒為周室之輔，後賢之繼述，有光于上世之開承也，而于宣者有所賴矣。是則申伯之封非倖致，宣王之錫非濫及，有周封建之典，于是可見，而吉甫播揚以為贈也，固宜。
抑論申伯以元舅之親出封于謝，宣王豈直為親親已也？蓋申伯德業聞望，足為當時之重，而謝之為邑，實作鎮于南土，所以鎮定而綏服之者，亦不可匪其人也。《崧高》之作，反覆於蕃翰、作式、為憲之說，而激勸感發之意，默寓其間。故讀其詩，則宣王親賢懷遠之道，當時友朋勸示之益，俱可想見于千載之上。
translation_en:
…the establishment of dwellings brought comfort to the king’s heart within his innermost palace; the orderly southern states thus saw the work brought to completion. Yet was this merely to display exceptional favor for a moment, or to confer a great investiture today, and nothing more? For “continuing the succession and making it splendid” expresses what a ruler expects of his ministers. He would have those who inherit their offices preserve the achievements already established, thereby extending the dynasty’s good fortune far into the future. “Illustrious through successive generations” describes how these officers sustain Zhou. He would have those who arise afterward keep these great accomplishments in mind, thereby perpetuating the dynasty’s lifeblood for ages to come. By carrying forward the virtue of their forebears, they would forever serve as models for the southern states. Those who later succeed Shen would be like Shen succeeding Fu, and there would thus be men upon whom to depend as bulwarks of the realm. By inheriting their former duties, they would always assist the royal house of Zhou. The worthy men of later generations, continuing and carrying forward this work, would bring glory to what earlier generations had begun and maintained; and the work of spreading royal influence [?] would have men upon whom to rely. Thus Shen Bo’s enfeoffment was no windfall, and King Xuan’s bestowal was no indiscriminate favor. Here one can discern Zhou’s institutions for establishing fiefs and lords. It was certainly fitting that Jifu should celebrate these deeds in a poem presented as a parting gift.
Furthermore, considering that Shen Bo, as the king’s senior maternal uncle, was sent out to receive a fief at Xie, could King Xuan have acted solely out of affection for his kin? Shen Bo’s virtue, accomplishments, reputation, and standing were sufficient to make him a figure of great consequence in his time. Xie, moreover, served as a stronghold in the southern lands. The man charged with stabilizing that region and bringing it peacefully into allegiance therefore had to be suited to the task. The poem Lofty Mountains (Song gao) repeatedly speaks of serving as a bulwark, setting an example, and providing a standard; an intention to encourage, exhort, and inspire is quietly embedded throughout. Thus, reading this poem, we can envision, across a thousand years, both King Xuan’s way of drawing worthy men close and winning over distant peoples, and the benefits of the encouragement and guidance that friends offered one another in that age.

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
於皇武王無競維烈允文文王克開厥後
嗣武受之勝殷遏劉耆定爾功
楊錫文
同考試官訓導許批模寫周公象功作樂之意明白
可錄
考試官訓導穆批講題意能知輕重取之
考試官教諭鄭批腴而整
詩人頌王者有大功必表其因所啓以成功也
蓋周有天下固武王之功而啓之者則文王也
===
詩人推本而言之也有以夫此周公象武王之
功爲大武之樂首之以嗟嘆之詞若曰大哉武
王之爲君也聖武布昭而興王之績上格于天
皇靈丕振而創造之功有隆于古其烈之盛天
下無得而競矣然豈無所自哉蓋允矣思文之
文王也脩和有夏而維新之命有以立後世仰
承之基開國之規模固自岐周而肇啓矣輯寧
邦家而有二之業足以爲後人憑藉之地興周
之氣象固自遷豐而光顯矣故我武王之嗣興
punctuated:
於皇武王，無競維烈！允文文王，克開厥後。嗣武受之，勝殷遏劉，耆定爾功。

楊錫文

同考試官訓導許批：模寫周公象功作樂之意，明白可錄。
考試官訓導穆批：講題意能知輕重，取之。
考試官教諭鄭批：腴而整。

詩人頌王者有大功，必表其因所啓以成功也。蓋周有天下，固武王之功，而啓之者則文王也。詩人推本而言之也，有以夫！此周公象武王之功爲大武之樂，首之以嗟嘆之詞，若曰：大哉，武王之爲君也！聖武布昭，而興王之績上格于天；皇靈丕振，而創造之功有隆于古。其烈之盛，天下無得而競矣。然豈無所自哉？蓋允矣，思文之文王也！脩和有夏，而維新之命有以立後世仰承之基，開國之規模固自岐周而肇啓矣；輯寧邦家，而有二之業足以爲後人憑藉之地，興周之氣象固自遷豐而光顯矣。故我武王之嗣興
translation_en:
“Ah, august King Wu, unmatched were your achievements! Truly cultured was King Wen, who could open the way for his successors. Succeeding him, Wu received his legacy, conquered Yin, and halted slaughter, bringing your achievement to completion.”

Yang Xiwen 楊錫文

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor: “It depicts clearly the Duke of Zhou’s intention in making music to represent these achievements. Worth recording.”
Comment by Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor: “In explaining the topic’s meaning, he understands the relative weight of its parts. Accept it.”
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “Rich and well ordered.”

When poets praise a king’s great achievements, they invariably make clear whose pioneering work he relied upon to accomplish them. For although Zhou’s possession of All under Heaven was indeed King Wu’s achievement, it was King Wen who opened the way. The poet had good reason to trace it to its source!

Here the Duke of Zhou made the music of the Great Martial Dance (Dawu) to represent King Wu’s achievements, beginning with words of admiration, as if to say: Great indeed was King Wu as a ruler! His sagely martial prowess shone far and wide, and his accomplishment in establishing the royal dynasty reached Heaven above. His august might was greatly displayed, and his achievement in founding the dynasty surpassed those of antiquity. Such was the greatness of his deeds that none under Heaven could rival them. Yet could they have been without a source?

Truly cultivated indeed was King Wen! He brought harmony to the lands of Xia, and the renewed Mandate thereby established a foundation that later generations could reverently inherit. The plan for founding the state thus had its beginnings in Qizhou. He brought peace to the realm, and his achievement in possessing two-thirds of it provided a footing upon which his successors could rely. The promise of Zhou’s rise thus shone forth from the time of his move to Feng. Thus, when our King Wu arose as his successor …

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
也思寵受之重而致駿惠之功於鑠之師既興
戎衣一著遂勝殷于牧野純熈之時既會大介
是用因止殺于崇朝由是上而天命于周而有
僕允陟元后而一代之大業以成維揚之武視
文考而有光也下而人心于周而攸同奄有萬
方而帝王之大統以集丕承之烈蓋自今而致
定也夫功雖開于文王而實成于武王此武王
之功所以為大也歟抑是詩也雖象武功而作
孔子之論樂極于周道四達禮樂交通有聲之
===
雅亦曰皇王維辟無思不服武王之有天下固
非以力取之者而允文文王有此武功亦非不
足于武可知矣前後相承文武並用所以創成
周八百年之業非偶然也大武桓賚之歌揚之
宗廟三復之猶可想見其盛
春秋
遂伐楚僖公四年諸侯遂救許僖公六年
黨宗正
考試官訓導穆批善發褒貶齊桓之意
punctuated:
也，思寵受之重，而致駿惠之功。於鑠之師既興，戎衣一著，遂勝殷于牧野；純熈之時既會，大介是用，因止殺于崇朝。由是，上而天命于周而有僕，允陟元后，而一代之大業以成，維揚之武，視文考而有光也；下而人心于周而攸同，奄有萬方，而帝王之大統以集，丕承之烈，蓋自今而致定也。夫功雖開于文王，而實成于武王，此武王之功所以為大也歟！抑是詩也，雖象武功而作，孔子之論樂，極于周道四達、禮樂交通。《有聲》之雅亦曰：「皇王維辟，無思不服。」武王之有天下，固非以力取之者；而允文文王有此武功，亦非不足于武，可知矣。前後相承，文武並用，所以創成周八百年之業，非偶然也。《大武》《桓》《賚》之歌，揚之宗廟，三復之，猶可想見其盛。

春秋

遂伐楚，僖公四年。諸侯遂救許，僖公六年。

黨宗正

考試官訓導穆批：善發褒貶齊桓之意。
translation_en:
…when he succeeded to the throne, he reflected on the weight of the favor he had received and accomplished the work of following his predecessor with utmost devotion. Once his glorious army had risen, he donned his battle robes and defeated Yin at Muye. When the moment of resplendent good fortune arrived, he put his great armor to use and brought the killing to an end within a single morning. Thus, above, Heaven conferred its mandate upon Zhou, which gained its servants; he truly ascended as supreme sovereign, and the great undertaking of a dynasty was accomplished. His martial prowess, displayed abroad, added luster to that of his cultured deceased father. Below, the hearts of the people converged upon Zhou; he possessed the myriad regions, and the great imperial succession was united in him. His achievement in grandly carrying on his inheritance was thereby firmly established. Although King Wen began the undertaking, King Wu brought it to completion: is this not what made King Wu’s achievement so great?

Yet although this poem was composed to represent martial achievement, Confucius’s discussion of its music culminates in the Way of Zhou reaching in all four directions and rites and music permeating everywhere. The Greater Ode “There Is a Sound” (You sheng) likewise says: “The august king is sovereign; none thinks of withholding submission.” King Wu’s possession of All-under-Heaven was certainly not something he seized by force. And that the truly cultured King Wen possessed such martial accomplishments shows that he, too, was by no means deficient in military prowess. Predecessor and successor carried on one another’s work, employing both civil and martial means: their founding and completion of Zhou’s eight-hundred-year enterprise was no accident. The songs “Great Martial” (Da wu), “Martial Majesty” (Huan), and “Bestowal” (Lai) resound in the ancestral temple. Reciting them repeatedly, one can still envision that flourishing age.

Spring and Autumn Annals

“They thereupon attacked Chu.” Fourth year of Duke Xi.
“The feudal lords thereupon came to the aid of Xu.” Sixth year of Duke Xi.

Dang Zongzheng

Comment by Examiner Mu, Instructor: “Skillfully brings out the intent behind the praise and censure of Duke Huan of Qi.”

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭鄭批嚴整可錄
伯主攘外失於專春秋譏之恤小合於義春秋
善之此楚之伐許之救而齊霸之得失判矣且
伐楚者齊桓公也伐之何如曰爲其乆病中國
也乆病中國而伐之功弗少矣君子顧於桓乎
譏之何曰爲其失於專征也征伐自天子出受
命于祖受成于學非臣下可得而擅也桓公是
舉不待天王之命爰興八國之師彤弓未錫而
閫制自由牙璋未啓而天討奚在噫文武之建
===
侯也以蕃王室也賢如桓吾方望其宗周而先
天下也今也討有罪之國而已涉無王之嫌主
中夏之盟而首犯先王之令回視羲和之征桓
不逮胤侯遠矣書曰臣無作威桓其昧之經書
伐而曰遂者譏其專也此義行則蔑視君父者
懼而君臣之分嚴矣哉救許者亦齊桓公也救
之何如曰爲其近罹楚禍也近罹楚禍而救之
事亦常耳君子顧於桓乎善之何曰爲其急於
救患也夷虜爲中國患如火斯焚如水斯溺非
punctuated:
考試官敎諭鄭批：嚴整可錄。

伯主攘外失於專，春秋譏之；恤小合於義，春秋善之。此楚之伐、許之救，而齊霸之得失判矣。且伐楚者，齊桓公也。伐之何如？曰：爲其乆病中國也。乆病中國而伐之，功弗少矣。君子顧於桓乎譏之，何？曰：爲其失於專征也。征伐自天子出，受命于祖，受成于學，非臣下可得而擅也。桓公是舉，不待天王之命，爰興八國之師；彤弓未錫而閫制自由，牙璋未啓而天討奚在？噫！文武之建侯也，以蕃王室也。賢如桓，吾方望其宗周而先天下也。今也討有罪之國，而已涉無王之嫌；主中夏之盟，而首犯先王之令。回視羲和之征，桓不逮胤侯遠矣。書曰：「臣無作威。」桓其昧之。經書伐而曰遂者，譏其專也。此義行，則蔑視君父者懼，而君臣之分嚴矣哉！救許者，亦齊桓公也。救之何如？曰：爲其近罹楚禍也。近罹楚禍而救之，事亦常耳。君子顧於桓乎善之，何？曰：爲其急於救患也。夷虜爲中國患，如火斯焚，如水斯溺，非
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: Rigorous and well ordered; worthy of inclusion.

When a hegemon repels external enemies but errs in acting on his own authority, the Spring and Autumn Annals censures him; when he cares for a small state in accordance with righteousness, the Annals commends him. Thus the attack on Chu and the relief of Xu distinguish the merits and faults of Qi’s hegemony. Now, it was Duke Huan of Qi who attacked Chu. What justified this attack? The answer is that Chu had long afflicted the Central States. To attack a state that had long afflicted the Central States was no small achievement. Why, then, does the noble man nevertheless censure Duke Huan? Because he erred in undertaking a punitive expedition on his own authority. Punitive campaigns proceed from the Son of Heaven: the commander receives his mandate in the ancestral temple and his settled instructions in the school. They are not something a subject may undertake at his own discretion. In this undertaking, Duke Huan did not await the Heavenly King’s command but raised the armies of eight states. Before receiving the vermilion bow, he exercised military command as he pleased; before the toothed jade tablet had been brought forth to authorize mobilization, what warrant was there for punishment on Heaven’s behalf? Alas! Kings Wen and Wu established the feudal lords to protect the royal house. Of one as worthy as Duke Huan, I would have expected that he would honor Zhou and lead all under Heaven in doing so. Yet now, in chastising a guilty state, he had already incurred the suspicion of disregarding the king; in presiding over the covenant of the Central States, he was himself the first to violate the former kings’ commands. Looking back to the expedition against Xi and He, Duke Huan fell far short of the Marquis of Yin. The Book of Documents says: “A minister must not exercise awe-inspiring authority.” Duke Huan seems to have been blind to this. The Classic records the attack with the word “thereupon” to censure his unauthorized action. If this principle prevails, those who disdain their ruler and father will be afraid, and the distinction between ruler and subject will be strictly maintained!

It was also Duke Huan of Qi who relieved Xu. What justified this relief? The answer is that Xu had recently suffered calamity at Chu’s hands. To relieve a state recently afflicted by Chu was merely an ordinary undertaking. Why, then, does the noble man nevertheless commend Duke Huan? Because he acted urgently to relieve distress. When the barbarians afflict the Central States, it is like being burned by fire or drowned by water; it is not …

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
盟主所得緩焉者也桓之是役不待逾時之久
卽移六國之兵楚旅還轅而外侮以禦許人安
堵而小國以寧噫湯文之字小也以除暴橫也
强如桓吾方恐其討鄭而忽許難也今也遏荐
食之謀而凶暴有所懲解倒懸之厄而弱小有
所恃回視凡伯之伐桓其過衛宣遠矣詩曰戎
狄是膺桓其以之經書救而曰遂者善之尤也
此義行則輕棄諸姬者懼而恤患之義昭矣哉
是則伐而書遂貶其遂也救而書遂褒其遂也
===
所謂美惡不嫌同辭其此之謂夫抑伐楚過矣
難掩夫服楚之功救許功矣難掩夫失黃之過
此伯者假之之私而非若王者之純乎公也然
考之當時王政不行諸侯僭亂而為桓公者猶
知以尊周攘夷為念兵車之屬六乘車之會三
帥諸侯而朝天子使天下猶知有共主焉則其
有功於周室亦不淺矣桓其可盡訾哉
晉人執鄭伯欒書帥師伐鄭成公九年
楊本聰
punctuated:
盟主所得緩焉者也。桓之是役，不待逾時之久，卽移六國之兵。楚旅還轅，而外侮以禦；許人安堵，而小國以寧。噫！湯文之字小也，以除暴橫也。强如桓，吾方恐其討鄭而忽許難也。今也，遏荐食之謀，而凶暴有所懲；解倒懸之厄，而弱小有所恃。回視凡伯之伐，桓其過衛宣遠矣。《詩》曰：「戎狄是膺。」桓其以之。經書「救」而曰「遂」者，善之尤也。此義行，則輕棄諸姬者懼，而恤患之義昭矣哉！是則伐而書「遂」，貶其遂也；救而書「遂」，褒其遂也。所謂美惡不嫌同辭，其此之謂夫！抑伐楚過矣，難掩夫服楚之功；救許功矣，難掩夫失黃之過。此伯者假之之私，而非若王者之純乎公也。然考之當時，王政不行，諸侯僭亂，而為桓公者猶知以尊周攘夷為念。兵車之屬六，乘車之會三，帥諸侯而朝天子，使天下猶知有共主焉，則其有功於周室亦不淺矣。桓其可盡訾哉！

晉人執鄭伯，欒書帥師伐鄭。成公九年。
楊本聰
translation_en:
…something over which the leader of the alliance could afford to delay. In this campaign, Duke Huan promptly redirected the troops of six states, without waiting for time to pass. The army of Chu turned its chariots homeward, and foreign aggression was repelled; the people of Xu remained secure in their homes, and the small state enjoyed peace. Ah! Tang and King Wen cherished small states by eliminating violent oppression. Powerful as Huan was, I had feared that he would attack Zheng and neglect Xu’s plight. Now, however, he checked the plan to devour one state after another, thus chastening the violent; he relieved distress as acute as being hung upside down, thus giving the weak and small someone to rely upon. Looking back at the attack on Fan Bo, Huan far surpassed Duke Xuan of Wei. The Book of Odes says: “Strike against the Rong and Di.” Huan acted accordingly. When the Classic records “rescue” and says “thereupon,” it expresses particular approval. If this principle prevails, those who lightly abandon the states of the Ji lineage will be afraid, and the duty to relieve distress will become manifest! Thus, when an attack is recorded with “thereupon,” the continuation of action is censured; when a rescue is recorded with “thereupon,” the continuation is praised. Surely this is what is meant by saying that praise and blame need not avoid using the same wording!

Yet although attacking Chu was a fault, it cannot obscure his achievement in bringing Chu to submission; although rescuing Xu was an achievement, it cannot obscure his fault in allowing Huang to be lost. This reveals the self-interest of a hegemon who borrows the forms of virtue, unlike a true king’s complete devotion to the common good. Nevertheless, consider the circumstances of that time: royal government no longer operated, and the regional lords usurped authority and caused disorder. Yet Duke Huan still knew to concern himself with honoring Zhou and repelling the Yi. He assembled the lords six times with war chariots and three times with ceremonial carriages, and led them in paying court to the Son of Heaven, so that all under Heaven still recognized a common sovereign. His service to the house of Zhou was therefore substantial. Can Huan be condemned without qualification?

“The men of Jin seized the Earl of Zheng; Luan Shu led an army to attack Zheng.” Ninth year of Duke Cheng.
Yang Bencong.

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官訓導穆批辭不煩而有斷制深得謹嚴之
旨
考試官教諭鄭批不失傳意
春秋紀伯討之非有所以明大分者有所以正
大防者此見春秋之義不可以一端求也且鄭
懷楚賂而會楚晉惡鄭貳而討鄭乃因鄭成之
朝而執於銅鞮隨遣欒書伐其國焉夫晉本侯
也窮諸人何居邦典定諸侯之獄司隸掌執人
之事大司寇之職周官之法度不可干也鄭固
===
罪矣晉始執也不以王命既執也不歸京師君
子曰執而無命則不臣不臣則不爵窮諸人賤
之也豈復得為伯討乎於時伯蠲行成晉戮之
矣略而不紀者何曰天下有大分君臣是已成
非蠲之君蠲非成之臣耶君實有國神之主而
民之望也成執于晉進退惟其所制榮辱莫之
或知國之患莫大乎此蠲之身庸足多乎傳曰
既執其君矣則行人為輕明此則天下皆知君
之為重而後其君者寡矣貴有常尊大分不既
punctuated:
考試官訓導穆批：辭不煩而有斷制，深得謹嚴之旨。
考試官教諭鄭批：不失傳意。
春秋紀伯討之非，有所以明大分者，有所以正大防者，此見春秋之義不可以一端求也。且鄭懷楚賂而會楚，晉惡鄭貳而討鄭，乃因鄭成之朝而執於銅鞮，隨遣欒書伐其國焉。夫晉本侯也，窮諸人何居？邦典定諸侯之獄，司隸掌執人之事，大司寇之職，周官之法度不可干也。鄭固罪矣，晉始執也，不以王命；既執也，不歸京師。君子曰：「執而無命，則不臣；不臣，則不爵。」窮諸人，賤之也，豈復得為伯討乎？於時伯蠲行成，晉戮之矣。略而不紀者何？曰：天下有大分，君臣是已。成非蠲之君，蠲非成之臣耶？君實有國，神之主而民之望也。成執于晉，進退惟其所制，榮辱莫之或知，國之患莫大乎此。蠲之身，庸足多乎？傳曰：「既執其君矣，則行人為輕。」明此，則天下皆知君之為重，而後其君者寡矣。貴有常尊，大分不既
translation_en:
