Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The wording is concise yet decisive, fully capturing the principle of scrupulous rigor.”
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “It preserves the meaning of the commentary.”
When the Spring and Autumn Annals records the wrongs committed in a hegemon’s punitive actions, it does so both to clarify the fundamental distinctions of rank and to uphold the fundamental boundaries. This shows that the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals cannot be sought from a single perspective. Zheng, coveting Chu’s gifts, met with Chu; Jin, resenting Zheng’s divided allegiance, took punitive action against Zheng. Taking advantage of Duke Cheng of Zheng’s court visit, Jin detained him at Tongdi and then dispatched Luan Shu to attack his state. Now the ruler of Jin was a marquis: why reduce him to the designation “a man”? The statutes of the realm prescribe the adjudication of cases involving the feudal lords; the Director of Convict Labor oversees the arrest of persons. These are duties of the Minister of Justice [?], and the regulations of the Offices of Zhou must not be infringed. Zheng was indeed guilty, but when Jin first detained its ruler, it acted without the king’s command; after detaining him, it did not deliver him to the royal capital. The gentleman says: “To detain someone without a command is to fail in one’s duty as a subject; one who fails in that duty is not accorded his noble title.” Reducing him to “a man” debases him. How could this still qualify as a hegemon’s legitimate punitive action?
At that time, Bo Juan went to negotiate peace, and Jin put him to death. Why does the text omit this and leave it unrecorded? The answer is that the world has a fundamental distinction of rank: that between ruler and subject. Was Duke Cheng not Juan’s ruler, and was Juan not Cheng’s subject? The ruler possesses the state; he presides over its sacrifices to the spirits and is the focus of the people’s hopes. Cheng was held captive in Jin, his every movement subject to its control, his honor or humiliation beyond anyone’s knowing. No calamity for a state could be greater than this. How much weight, then, should Juan’s own fate carry? The commentary says: “Once they have detained his ruler, the envoy is of lesser importance.” When this is understood, all under Heaven will recognize the ruler’s paramount importance, and few will put their ruler second. The exalted have their enduring position of honor; has the fundamental distinction of rank not already …

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
定矣哉於時楚子重侵陳以救鄭矣削而不書
者何曰天下有大防夷夏是巳晉非禮義之國
楚非禽獸與隣者耶景雖不競猶主夏盟者也
鄭附于楚德之不懷而威焉是畏親之不篤而
利焉是從變之不善一至於此楚之救庸足多
乎傳曰鄭無可救之善楚不得有能救之名明
此則天下皆知夷之可鄙而變於夷者鮮矣夷
不亂華大防不既嚴矣哉于以見聖人之筆削
無非為君臣夷夏計也國史焉得而與夫抑楚
===
奚待責乎鄭奚足責乎晉景嗣伯中國所仰無
亦以德禮招携懷遠乎鄭與楚合而即來朝過
而悔矣執其身伐其國戮其使暴也夫召陵之
禮楚使蕭魚信鄭不疑桓乎悼乎賢於景也遠
矣雖然仲知有以教之也景不桓不悼也臣又
不仲不知也禮信焉攸施故曰為政在人
禮記
故聖人參於天地並於鬼神以治政也
梁佐
punctuated:
定矣哉？於時楚子重侵陳以救鄭矣，削而不書者何？曰：天下有大防，夷夏是巳。晉非禮義之國，楚非禽獸與隣者耶？景雖不競，猶主夏盟者也。鄭附于楚，德之不懷而威焉是畏，親之不篤而利焉是從，變之不善一至於此，楚之救庸足多乎？傳曰：「鄭無可救之善，楚不得有能救之名。」明此，則天下皆知夷之可鄙，而變於夷者鮮矣。夷不亂華，大防不既嚴矣哉？于以見聖人之筆削，無非為君臣夷夏計也，國史焉得而與夫？抑楚奚待責乎？鄭奚足責乎？晉景嗣伯，中國所仰，無亦以德禮招携懷遠乎？鄭與楚合而即來朝，過而悔矣。執其身，伐其國，戮其使，暴也夫！召陵之禮楚使，蕭魚信鄭不疑，桓乎，悼乎，賢於景也遠矣！雖然，仲、知有以教之也。景不桓不悼也，臣又不仲不知也，禮信焉攸施？故曰：「為政在人。」

《禮記》
故聖人參於天地，並於鬼神，以治政也。
梁佐
translation_en:
…would not the great distinction then be firmly established? At that time, Zizhong of Chu invaded Chen to rescue Zheng. Why was this omitted and left unrecorded? The answer is: the world has a great boundary—that between the Yi and the Xia. Was Jin not a state of ritual propriety and righteousness, and was Chu not a state akin to birds and beasts? Though Duke Jing was weak, he still presided over the alliances of the Xia states. Zheng attached itself to Chu: it cherished no virtue but feared force; it remained faithful to no kinship but pursued advantage. Its transformation for the worse had reached such a point—how could Chu’s rescue deserve praise? The Commentary says: “Zheng possessed no goodness that warranted rescue; Chu could not be credited with the merit of rescuing it.” Once this is understood, all under Heaven will recognize that the Yi are contemptible, and few will adopt their ways. With the Yi unable to disrupt the Hua, would not the great boundary then be rigorously maintained? From this we see that the sage’s inclusions and deletions were all made with regard to ruler and minister, Yi and Xia. How could the annals of the states compare with them?

Yet why need Chu even be reproached? Why is Zheng even worth reproaching? Duke Jing of Jin inherited the hegemony, and the central states looked up to him. Should he not have used virtue and ritual propriety to attract the estranged and win over the distant? Zheng allied itself with Chu but then promptly came to court: it had erred and repented. To seize its ruler, attack its state, and kill its envoy—this was brutality! The courteous treatment of Chu’s envoy at Shaoling, and the trust in Zheng without suspicion at Xiaoyu: how far superior Dukes Huan and Dao were to Duke Jing! Nevertheless, Zhong and Zhi had ways of instructing them. Jing was neither Huan nor Dao, and his ministers were neither Zhong nor Zhi. How, then, could ritual propriety and trust be put into practice? Thus it is said: “The conduct of government depends on the men.”

Book of Rites
“Thus the sage forms a triad with Heaven and Earth and stands alongside the spirits in conducting government.”
Liang Zuo

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官訓導穆批見理精到而文足以發
考試官教諭鄭批講叅並處與衆自別
記者言聖人法造化以爲治以見治道之原也
蓋道之大原出於天也聖人法造化以爲治夫
豈私意臆度而爲之哉禮運承上章言政之意
以爲君者政之所自出也政者君之所由安也
能治其政以安其身舍聖人其誰與哉是故兩
儀奠而法象形道運於天地而不已也聖人則
仰觀俯察裁而成之以知其化育焉二氣行而
===
屈伸著事寓於鬼神而有迹也聖人則彰往察
來擬而議之以成其變化焉內蘊易簡之理而
覆載之功我其賛之參其兩而爲三矣中涵寂
感之幾而動靜之樞我其握之並其二而爲一
矣夫此豈有他哉凡以治吾之政而已蓋政莫
先於立教也體天地之撰而變通之則所以立
極而垂訓者資之愈深而教於是乎立矣政莫
要於定制也因鬼神之故而損益之則所以開
物而成務者循之可久而制於是乎定矣運用
punctuated:
考試官訓導穆批：見理精到，而文足以發。
考試官教諭鄭批：講叅並處，與衆自別。
記者言聖人法造化以爲治，以見治道之原也。蓋道之大原出於天也，聖人法造化以爲治，夫豈私意臆度而爲之哉？《禮運》承上章言政之意，以爲君者，政之所自出也；政者，君之所由安也。能治其政以安其身，舍聖人其誰與哉？是故兩儀奠而法象形，道運於天地而不已也。聖人則仰觀俯察，裁而成之，以知其化育焉。二氣行而屈伸著，事寓於鬼神而有迹也。聖人則彰往察來，擬而議之，以成其變化焉。內蘊易簡之理，而覆載之功，我其賛之，參其兩而爲三矣；中涵寂感之幾，而動靜之樞，我其握之，並其二而爲一矣。夫此豈有他哉？凡以治吾之政而已。蓋政莫先於立教也，體天地之撰而變通之，則所以立極而垂訓者，資之愈深，而教於是乎立矣。政莫要於定制也，因鬼神之故而損益之，則所以開物而成務者，循之可久，而制於是乎定矣。運用
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor: His grasp of principle is penetrating and exact, and his writing adequately brings it out.
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: His exposition of “forming a triad with” and “standing alongside” distinguishes him from the others.
The compiler of the Record of Rites says that the sage models his governance on the creative transformations of nature, thereby revealing the source of the Way of government. For the great source of the Way issues from Heaven. When the sage models his governance on these creative transformations, could he possibly act on private notions and conjecture? The “Evolution of Rites” chapter continues the preceding section’s discussion of government: the ruler is the source from which government proceeds, and government is the means by which the ruler secures himself. Who but a sage could order his government and thereby secure his own person?
Thus, when the two powers, Heaven and Earth, are established and their patterns and images take form, the Way operates ceaselessly between Heaven and Earth. The sage looks upward and examines downward, shaping and completing their workings so as to understand their transforming and nurturing activity. When the two vital forces move and their contraction and expansion become manifest, affairs have their basis in ghosts and spirits and leave discernible traces. The sage brings the past to light and examines what is to come, comparing and deliberating so as to bring their transformations to completion. Inwardly he holds the principles of ease and simplicity: “I shall assist Heaven and Earth in their work of covering and supporting all things,” joining those two to form a triad. Within himself he contains the subtle springs of stillness and responsiveness: “I shall grasp the pivot of movement and stillness,” standing alongside ghosts and spirits and uniting their duality into one.
Could there be any other purpose in this? It is all simply to put one’s government in order. In government, nothing takes precedence over establishing moral instruction. By embodying the workings of Heaven and Earth and adapting them to changing circumstances, the sage draws ever more deeply upon them as the means to establish the supreme standard and transmit instruction; moral teaching is thereby established. In government, nothing is more essential than fixing institutions. By following the underlying workings of ghosts and spirits and making appropriate reductions and additions, the sage provides enduring practices for bringing things to fruition and accomplishing affairs; institutions are thereby fixed. Putting this into operation …

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
於一心推之萬變而皆宜所謂同民心而出治
道者此也建立於一時垂之萬世而無弊所謂
一道德而同風俗者此也夫然則政豈有不正
而身豈有不安者哉考之下文有曰君者立於
無過之地者也夫能正其身而無過則亦聖人
而已雖然記者之言蓋本於中庸也夫政即三
重也無過即寡過也參即建之而不悖也並即
質之而無疑也三代有道之長率由乎此後世
乃欲以區區智力把持天下毋怪乎其治之不
===
古若也噫
廉直勁正莊誠之音作而民肅敬
楊作舟
考試官訓導穆批不以金石絲竹入講蓋知音樂
之辨者
考試官教諭鄭批分析字義明白當是作者
記者審樂音之敬而知民心之敬焉夫音生於
心也心苟敬矣而其發之於音也寧不敬哉樂
記此章申言首章之意若謂心感於中而無常
punctuated:
於一心，推之萬變而皆宜，所謂同民心而出治道者，此也。建立於一時，垂之萬世而無弊，所謂一道德而同風俗者，此也。夫然則政豈有不正，而身豈有不安者哉？考之下文，有曰：「君者，立於無過之地者也。」夫能正其身而無過，則亦聖人而已。雖然，記者之言蓋本於《中庸》也。夫政即三重也，無過即寡過也，參即建之而不悖也，並即質之而無疑也。三代有道之長，率由乎此。後世乃欲以區區智力把持天下，毋怪乎其治之不古若也。噫！

廉直勁正莊誠之音作，而民肅敬。
楊作舟
考試官訓導穆批：「不以金石絲竹入講，蓋知音樂之辨者。」
考試官教諭鄭批：「分析字義明白，當是作者。」

記者審樂音之敬，而知民心之敬焉。夫音生於心也，心苟敬矣，而其發之於音也，寧不敬哉？《樂記》此章申言首章之意，若謂心感於中而無常
translation_en:
…within a single mind, and extended to all the myriad changes, it is appropriate to each. This is what is meant by bringing the people's hearts into accord and bringing forth the way of governance. Established at one time and handed down through ten thousand generations without ill effects, this is what is meant by unifying moral principles and bringing customs into accord. If so, how could government fail to be correct, or the ruler's person fail to be secure? Examining the text below, we find: “The ruler stands in a position free from error.” One who can rectify his person and remain free from error must surely be a sage. Nevertheless, the words of the compiler of the Record are grounded in the Doctrine of the Mean. Government corresponds to its “three weighty matters”; being without error corresponds to making few errors; forming a triad corresponds to establishing something without contradiction; and standing alongside corresponds to testing something without doubt. The long endurance of the Way under the Three Dynasties invariably proceeded from this. Later ages sought instead to hold the realm in their grasp through paltry cleverness and force. No wonder their governance fell short of antiquity! Alas!

“When sounds of integrity, straightforwardness, strength, rectitude, solemnity, and sincerity arise, the people become solemn and reverent.”
Yang Zuozhou
Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “He does not introduce bells, chimestones, strings, or pipes into his exposition: evidently he understands the distinction between tones and music.”
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “His analysis of the meanings of the words is clear; he surely qualifies as an accomplished writer.”

The compiler of the Record examines the reverence in musical sounds and thereby knows the reverence in the people's hearts. Sounds arise from the heart. If the heart is reverent, how could its expression in sound fail to be reverent? This chapter of the Record of Music elaborates the meaning of its opening chapter, as though saying that the heart is stirred within, with no fixed pattern…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
音發於外而有象然則音之作也豈惟喜怒可
知而已哉彼其應以生變稜隅整飭不混而淆
何其廉也變以成方節奏簡徑不句而曲何其
直也至剛至健抑之愈高無反無側守之愈確
又何其勁正乎恪恭祗慎不怠以荒純一敦固
不二而雜又何其莊誠乎倜然於永言之際而
有不可犯者存聽之者惕然而有所興也毅然
於咏歎之餘而有不可奪者在聞之者悚然而
知所勵也是音也果何從而生耶必其有所戒
也有嚴有翼而慄慄之是將有所畏也惟兢惟
一而惺惺之匪懈守之愈嚴而惰慢之心無自
而投則其音之不可犯也固也不然則姦而濫
矣寧不蕩然而忘返乎斂之愈約而非僻之心
無由而入則其音之不可奪也宜也不然則湎
而淫矣寧不蕭然而莫振乎以是而觀則知音
之本於心也尚矣心不能敬而徒矯飾於聲音
之末以求其敬也胡可得哉抑又論之惟敬則
肅惟廉則勁而莊惟直則正而誠故曰其敬心
punctuated: 音發於外而有象。然則音之作也，豈惟喜怒可知而已哉？彼其應以生變，稜隅整飭，不混而淆，何其廉也！變以成方，節奏簡徑，不句而曲，何其直也！至剛至健，抑之愈高；無反無側，守之愈確，又何其勁正乎！恪恭祗慎，不怠以荒；純一敦固，不二而雜，又何其莊誠乎！倜然於永言之際，而有不可犯者存，聽之者惕然而有所興也；毅然於咏歎之餘，而有不可奪者在，聞之者悚然而知所勵也。是音也，果何從而生耶？必其有所戒也，有嚴有翼，而慄慄之是將；有所畏也，惟兢惟一，而惺惺之匪懈。守之愈嚴，而惰慢之心無自而投，則其音之不可犯也固也；不然，則姦而濫矣，寧不蕩然而忘返乎？斂之愈約，而非僻之心無由而入，則其音之不可奪也宜也；不然，則湎而淫矣，寧不蕭然而莫振乎？以是而觀，則知音之本於心也尚矣。心不能敬，而徒矯飾於聲音之末，以求其敬也，胡可得哉？抑又論之，惟敬則肅，惟廉則勁而莊，惟直則正而誠。故曰：「其敬心
translation_en:
…sound issues outward and takes perceptible form. When sound arises, then, is it only joy and anger that can be discerned? In responding, it produces variations: its contours are orderly and distinct, neither confused nor muddled. How clear-cut it is! Its variations form patterns: its rhythms are simple and direct, neither bent nor crooked. How straight it is! Utterly firm and vigorous, the more it is pressed down, the higher it rises; neither turning back nor inclining to either side, the more it is maintained, the firmer it becomes. How strong and upright it is! Respectful and circumspect, it never lapses through indolence; single-minded, earnest, and steadfast, it admits neither divided purpose nor admixture. How solemn and sincere it is! Lofty amid the sustained singing, it possesses something that cannot be affronted; those who listen become alert and are stirred to action. Resolute amid the lingering chants and sighs, it possesses something that cannot be wrested away; those who hear it are awed and know to exert themselves.

From where, indeed, does such sound arise? Surely there is something against which the heart guards: solemn and reverent, it sustains its trembling vigilance. There is something it fears: cautious and single-minded, it remains wakeful and never slackens. The stricter its watch, the less opportunity thoughts of indolence and arrogance have to intrude; naturally, then, its sound cannot be affronted. Otherwise, the sound would be depraved and unrestrained: would it not drift away and forget to return? The more closely the heart gathers itself inward, the less opportunity wrongful and perverse thoughts have to enter; fittingly, then, its sound cannot be wrested away. Otherwise, the sound would be indulgent and excessive: would it not become dispirited and fail to rally?

Viewed in this light, we see how fundamental it is that sound is rooted in the heart. If the heart cannot be reverent, and one merely contrives an outward semblance in sound, which is only its final manifestation, how could one thereby attain reverence? To discuss it further: reverence brings solemnity; being clear-cut brings strength and gravity; being straight brings uprightness and sincerity. Thus it is said: “Its reverent heart…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
感者其聲直以廉義已盡矣然民心之所以敬
者則又在先王德澤入之之深而禮義養之之
固也故曰先王愼所以感之者
第貳場
論
先王守禮樂之本
馬應義
同考試官敎諭沈批〔前輩謂作論如文與可畫竹觀〕
〔子殆胸中有全竹者滇士中不多得也首選允宜〕
考試官訓導穆批〔法度嚴密意味深長殆探本之〕
〔論也可敬可服〕
考試官敎諭鄭批〔文勢若長江大河文彩若奇葩〕
〔麗卉低頭東野之拜將不敢抗顏於子矣〕
論曰聖人之爲斯世也天而已矣夫苟至於天
焉吾知藏於人心之微而不在於耳目觀瞻之
頃關於天地之大而不假於器數聲容之末是
則無體無聲者也萬一聖人於此弗以天處之
而以人御之强揠而矯拂睽疑而乖違則萬轍
punctuated:
感者，其聲直以廉，義已盡矣。然民心之所以敬者，則又在先王德澤入之之深，而禮義養之之固也。故曰：「先王愼所以感之者。」

第貳場

論

先王守禮樂之本

馬應義

同考試官敎諭沈批〔前輩謂作論如文與可畫竹，觀〕〔子殆胸中有全竹者，滇士中不多得也，首選允宜。〕

考試官訓導穆批〔法度嚴密，意味深長，殆探本之〕〔論也，可敬可服。〕

考試官敎諭鄭批〔文勢若長江大河，文彩若奇葩〕〔麗卉，低頭東野之拜，將不敢抗顏於子矣。〕

論曰：聖人之爲斯世也，天而已矣。夫苟至於天焉，吾知藏於人心之微，而不在於耳目觀瞻之頃；關於天地之大，而不假於器數聲容之末。是則無體無聲者也。萬一聖人於此弗以天處之，而以人御之，强揠而矯拂，睽疑而乖違，則萬轍
translation_en:
…is moved, its sound is upright and restrained.” The meaning has already been fully expressed. Yet the people's reverence also depends on how deeply the former kings' virtue and beneficence penetrated their hearts, and how firmly ritual and righteousness nurtured them. Thus it is said: “The former kings were circumspect about the means by which they moved the people.”

Second Session

Discourse

The Former Kings Preserved the Foundations of Ritual and Music

By Ma Yingyi

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: “Our predecessors said that composing a discourse is like Wen Yuke painting bamboo. Judging by your work, you surely have the whole bamboo already in your breast. Such a talent is rarely found among the scholars of Yunnan; selection for first place is entirely fitting.”

Comment by Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor: “Its method and structure are rigorous and meticulous; its meaning is profound and enduring. This is surely a discourse that probes the foundations. It commands respect and admiration.”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “The sweep of the writing resembles the Yangzi and the Yellow River; its literary brilliance resembles rare blossoms and splendid flowers. Bowing my head in the manner of Dongye, I would not dare face you as an equal.”

The discourse reads: The sage's work in this world is simply to accord with Heaven. If it indeed attains to Heaven, I know that it lies hidden in the subtle recesses of the human heart, rather than in what momentarily meets the ears and eyes; it concerns the vastness of Heaven and Earth, rather than depending on such secondary matters as implements, numerical prescriptions, sounds, and ceremonial bearing. It is thus without form or sound. Should the sage, in this matter, fail to act according to Heaven and instead govern through human contrivance—forcing growth as though pulling up shoots, distorting and thwarting, doubting and diverging—then myriad tracks…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
千岐爭馳競逐人者勝而天者微矣聖人與天
同運者也而肯以人勝天耶唐之太宗何如主
也而遽謂治之隆替不關於禮樂焉是人矣而
非天也先王守禮樂之本宋儒司馬光殆懼夫
後世之昧者弗察焉而覺之也請終言之禮云
而不以玉帛樂云而不以鍾鼓孔子之言也禮
所以節文乎仁義樂所以樂乎仁義孟子之言
也知孔孟論禮樂之旨則知司馬氏探先王禮
樂之本矣夷攷其時衣裳宫室之制作樂崇德
===
之旨固聞諸易也而說焉未詳所謂禮樂者猶
夫太始之天也伯夷寅清之言后夔直温之教
固聞諸書也而語焉未竟所謂禮樂者猶夫太
初之天也噫不灼其影昧者弗見也不烈其聲
聵者弗聞也聖人於此將聽其岐轍之紛紜騰
口之靡定哉聖人要亦有變通宜民之術矣於
是以開闢天地之規模而極夫世變江河之思
慮亦惟因夫民心固有之禮而示之以禮禮一
順也天也順之外固無禮矣因人心固有之樂
punctuated: 千岐，爭馳競逐，人者勝而天者微矣。聖人與天同運者也，而肯以人勝天耶？唐之太宗何如主也，而遽謂治之隆替不關於禮樂焉？是人矣，而非天也。先王守禮樂之本，宋儒司馬光殆懼夫後世之昧者弗察焉，而覺之也。請終言之。禮云而不以玉帛，樂云而不以鍾鼓，孔子之言也。禮所以節文乎仁義，樂所以樂乎仁義，孟子之言也。知孔孟論禮樂之旨，則知司馬氏探先王禮樂之本矣。夷攷其時，衣裳宫室之制、作樂崇德之旨，固聞諸《易》也，而說焉未詳，所謂禮樂者猶夫太始之天也。伯夷寅清之言、后夔直温之教，固聞諸《書》也，而語焉未竟，所謂禮樂者猶夫太初之天也。噫！不灼其影，昧者弗見也；不烈其聲，聵者弗聞也。聖人於此，將聽其岐轍之紛紜、騰口之靡定哉？聖人要亦有變通宜民之術矣。於是以開闢天地之規模，而極夫世變江河之思慮，亦惟因夫民心固有之禮而示之以禮。禮，一順也，天也；順之外固無禮矣。因人心固有之樂
translation_en:
…a thousand diverging paths, racing and competing with one another: the human prevails, while the heavenly grows faint. The sage moves in concert with Heaven; would he willingly let the human overcome the heavenly? What sort of ruler was Taizong of the Tang, that he should so readily declare that the flourishing or decline of government had nothing to do with rites and music? This is the human, not the heavenly. The former kings preserved the foundations of rites and music. Sima Guang, the Song Confucian scholar, presumably feared that the unenlightened of later ages would fail to perceive this, and therefore sought to awaken them. Allow me to complete the explanation. To speak of rites without meaning jade and silk, and of music without meaning bells and drums: these are the words of Confucius. Rites regulate and give patterned expression to benevolence and righteousness; music gives joy in benevolence and righteousness: these are the words of Mencius. Understanding what Confucius and Mencius meant in discussing rites and music, one understands how Sima Guang sought out the foundations of the former kings’ rites and music.

Examining those times dispassionately, we certainly learn from the Book of Changes of the institutions of clothing and palaces, and of the purpose of making music to exalt virtue. Yet its explanation is not detailed: what it calls rites and music is still like Heaven at the primordial beginning. We certainly learn from the Book of Documents of Bo Yi’s words concerning reverence and purity, and Hou Kui’s teaching concerning uprightness and gentleness. Yet its account is not exhaustive: what it calls rites and music is still like Heaven at the first inception. Alas! Unless its image shines brightly, the benighted cannot see it; unless its sound rings forcefully, the deaf cannot hear it. Would the sage, in these circumstances, simply allow divergent paths to proliferate in confusion and clamorous voices to remain unsettled? Surely the sage also possesses methods of adapting to circumstances for the people’s benefit. Thus, with a scope comparable to the opening of Heaven and Earth, he exhausts his deliberations upon the river-like flow of worldly change. He does no more than follow the rites inherent in the people’s hearts and make them manifest through ritual. Rites are wholly a matter of accord: they are Heaven. Beyond accord there are assuredly no rites. Following the music inherent in the human heart…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而示之以樂樂一和也天也和之外固無樂矣
於戲禮焉而示之以禮之天樂焉而示之以樂
之天聖人無迺斲天下之朴而不欲遊於堯舜
民相忘之天歟殆不然遭適至之時神化裁之
妙雲興波動而清明不移朴分質剖而渾厚猶
在所謂無體無聲而人心之天者固自若也故
曰聖人之爲斯世也天而已矣夫以人道之大
經而維持人文之脉絡而接續吾聖人爲禮樂
計也蓋已悉矣而議禮樂者往往築室而聚訟
===
何哉良有由矣蓋自夫比屋可封之俗弗見焉
而後世談禮者始索之文爲之末自夫康衢詩
歌之詠弗聞焉而後世議樂者始求之形器之
粗是則外矣而非內迹矣而非化尚安能囿一
世民物於至順至和之天歟知乎此則知先王
所以敎禮樂者悉原於天也天者何觀諸其道
而已天不變道亦不變一氣之相爲流通自太
極而來至於今不易也日月之在天至於今明
也江河之在地至於今流也山嶽至於今峙草
punctuated: 而示之以樂。樂一和也，天也，和之外固無樂矣。於戲！禮焉而示之以禮之天，樂焉而示之以樂之天，聖人無迺斲天下之朴，而不欲遊於堯舜民相忘之天歟？殆不然。遭適至之時，神化裁之妙，雲興波動而清明不移，朴分質剖而渾厚猶在，所謂無體無聲而人心之天者，固自若也。故曰：聖人之爲斯世也，天而已矣。夫以人道之大經而維持，人文之脉絡而接續，吾聖人爲禮樂計也，蓋已悉矣。而議禮樂者往往築室而聚訟，何哉？良有由矣。蓋自夫比屋可封之俗弗見焉，而後世談禮者始索之文爲之末；自夫康衢詩歌之詠弗聞焉，而後世議樂者始求之形器之粗。是則外矣而非內，迹矣而非化，尚安能囿一世民物於至順至和之天歟？知乎此，則知先王所以敎禮樂者，悉原於天也。天者何？觀諸其道而已。天不變，道亦不變。一氣之相爲流通，自太極而來，至於今不易也；日月之在天，至於今明也；江河之在地，至於今流也；山嶽至於今峙，草
translation_en:
…and reveals music to them through music. Music is wholly harmony: it is Heaven. Outside harmony there is assuredly no music. Ah! In ritual, he reveals the Heaven inherent in ritual; in music, he reveals the Heaven inherent in music. Could the sage be hewing away the uncarved simplicity of the world, unwilling to roam in that heavenly state in which Yao and Shun and their people forgot one another? Surely not. Meeting the fitting moment, he brings wondrous efficacy to the subtle work of transforming and ordering. Clouds rise and waves surge, yet clarity remains undisturbed; the uncarved block is divided and its substance cut apart, yet its rich integrity remains. What is called the Heaven of the human heart, without form or sound, remains just as it was. Thus I say: what the sage does for this world is simply Heaven.

By upholding the great norms of the human Way and continuing the vital threads of human culture, our sage has surely considered ritual and music in their entirety. Yet those who discuss ritual and music repeatedly resemble house-builders beset by conflicting advice and gather in disputation. Why? There is indeed a reason. Once the custom whereby every household was worthy of enfeoffment ceased to be seen, later generations discussing ritual began to seek it in the incidental details of formal observances. Once the songs sung along the broad thoroughfares ceased to be heard, later generations discussing music began to seek it in the crude externals of physical forms and instruments. These are outward things, not inward ones; traces, not transformation. How could they still encompass the people and things of an entire age within the Heaven of utmost accord and harmony? Understanding this, one understands that the former kings’ teaching of ritual and music originated entirely in Heaven.

What is Heaven? Simply observe its Way. Heaven does not change, nor does the Way. The single vital energy circulates through all things; from the Great Ultimate down to the present, this has not changed. The sun and moon in the heavens shine to this day; the rivers upon the earth flow to this day; the mountains stand to this day; grasses…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
木禽獸蟲魚至於今蕃且育也凡若此者非有
度數焉而成禮非有均節焉而成樂所謂不言
而化無爲而成者也茲其所謂無體之禮無聲
之樂也而道實爲之故曰天也夫天也其孰能
知之曰唯聖人能知之其孰能體之曰唯聖人
能體之何也禮也者人心之禮卽人心之天也
樂也者人心之樂亦人心之天也由是聖人因
其天者而敎禮樂焉叙爲彝倫脩爲人紀置之
充然大順之域夏籥之用殷輅之乘周冕之服
===
不與焉洽爲德澤流爲雅頌納於藹然至和之
中大夏之興大濩之作大武之奏不與焉當時
所謂禮樂者惟見其四極和寧而已惟見其萬
民咸悅而已惟見其江漢無犯而已尊其尊親
其親而辭遜於天高地下之間茲無體之禮也
聲相應氣相求而舞蹈於蟲鳴螽躍之地茲無
聲之樂也論至於斯則知聖人之心大乎天地
不足爲容皦乎日月不足爲明嵬乎泰華不足
爲高渾乎江河不足爲流轉知之者天也同之
punctuated: 木禽獸蟲魚至於今蕃且育也。凡若此者，非有度數焉而成禮，非有均節焉而成樂，所謂不言而化、無爲而成者也。茲其所謂無體之禮、無聲之樂也，而道實爲之，故曰天也。夫天也，其孰能知之？曰：唯聖人能知之。其孰能體之？曰：唯聖人能體之。何也？禮也者，人心之禮，卽人心之天也；樂也者，人心之樂，亦人心之天也。由是聖人因其天者而敎禮樂焉，叙爲彝倫，脩爲人紀，置之充然大順之域，夏籥之用、殷輅之乘、周冕之服不與焉；洽爲德澤，流爲雅頌，納於藹然至和之中，大夏之興、大濩之作、大武之奏不與焉。當時所謂禮樂者，惟見其四極和寧而已，惟見其萬民咸悅而已，惟見其江漢無犯而已。尊其尊，親其親，而辭遜於天高地下之間，茲無體之禮也；聲相應，氣相求，而舞蹈於蟲鳴螽躍之地，茲無聲之樂也。論至於斯，則知聖人之心大乎，天地不足爲容；皦乎，日月不足爲明；嵬乎，泰華不足爲高；渾乎，江河不足爲流轉。知之者，天也；同之
translation_en:
…trees, birds, beasts, insects, and fish continue to flourish and reproduce to this day. In all such things, ritual takes shape without prescribed measures, and music takes shape without regulated rhythms. This is what is meant by transformation without speech and accomplishment without deliberate action. This is the so-called ritual without form and music without sound. It is truly the Way that brings these about; hence we call it Heaven.

As for Heaven, who can understand it? The answer is: only the sage can understand it. Who can embody it? The answer is: only the sage can embody it. Why? Ritual is the ritual of the human heart; it is Heaven within the human heart. Music is the music of the human heart; it too is Heaven within the human heart. Thus the sage teaches ritual and music on the basis of what is heavenly within people. He orders this into the enduring human relationships and cultivates it into the guiding principles of human conduct, placing people in a realm filled with perfect concord. The use of the Xia flute, riding in the Yin carriage, and wearing the Zhou ceremonial cap have no part in this. He diffuses it as beneficent influence and lets it flow into elegant odes and hymns, bringing people into an abundant, utterly harmonious realm. The staging of the Great Xia dance, the performance of the Great Huo dance, and the playing of the Great Martial dance have no part in this.

What was then called ritual and music was apparent simply in peace and harmony extending to the four ends of the world, in the joy of all the people, and in the absence of transgression in the Jiang and Han regions. Honoring those worthy of honor, cherishing one’s kin, and practicing deference between lofty Heaven and lowly Earth: this is ritual without form. Sounds answering one another, kindred vital forces seeking one another, and people dancing upon the earth where insects chirp and grasshoppers leap: this is music without sound.

Pursuing the discussion thus far, we recognize that the sage’s heart is so great that Heaven and Earth cannot contain it; so bright that sun and moon cannot match its brilliance; so lofty that Mount Tai and Mount Hua cannot match its height; so vast and flowing that the Yangzi and Yellow Rivers cannot match its movement. What understands it is Heaven; what shares in it …

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
者道也化之者人也漸而澤之者天下後世也
天也聖人也不可以差殊觀也故曰天也奚俟
求諸旦暮之功索諸形器之末哉抑嘗因光之
慨夫唐而考夫唐之禮樂矣蓋自貞觀垂統内
有慚德而閨門之禮樂紊矣顯慶多中决之政
而朝廷之禮樂廢矣一傳而有斜封墨勅之濫
再傳而有漁陽召亂之釁又再傳而有閹宦擅
政之禍上下李唐諸君所謂垂統弗正而繼體
昏風將倂其本而仆之人矣而非天也烏足以
===
言禮樂哉是無怪乎司馬氏憂深思遠而爲中
正和平之論以開夫時君世主之天也有子曰
君子務本曾子曰此謂知本愚於光禮樂之言
亦云是爲論
表
擬宋輔臣謝賜
御製瑞聖園觀稼城南觀麥詩表祥符九年
劉舉良
同考試官教諭沈批麗而能則冲淡可喜
punctuated:
者，道也；化之者，人也；漸而澤之者，天下後世也。天也，聖人也，不可以差殊觀也，故曰天也。奚俟求諸旦暮之功，索諸形器之末哉？抑嘗因光之慨夫唐，而考夫唐之禮樂矣。蓋自貞觀垂統，内有慚德，而閨門之禮樂紊矣；顯慶多中决之政，而朝廷之禮樂廢矣。一傳而有斜封墨勅之濫，再傳而有漁陽召亂之釁，又再傳而有閹宦擅政之禍。上下李唐諸君，所謂垂統弗正而繼體昏，風將倂其本而仆之，人矣，而非天也，烏足以言禮樂哉？是無怪乎司馬氏憂深思遠，而爲中正和平之論，以開夫時君世主之天也。有子曰：「君子務本。」曾子曰：「此謂知本。」愚於光禮樂之言亦云是。爲論。
表
擬宋輔臣謝賜御製瑞聖園觀稼城南觀麥詩表，祥符九年。
劉舉良
同考試官教諭沈批：麗而能則，冲淡可喜。
translation_en:
…is the Way; those transformed by him are the people; those gradually imbued with his beneficence are all under Heaven and the generations to come. Heaven and the sage cannot be regarded as different; hence the designation “Heaven.” Why need one seek this in achievements of a morning or evening, or search for it in the peripheral details of material forms and implements?
Taking Guang’s lament over the Tang as my starting point, I have also examined the Tang’s rites and music. From the founding of the dynastic succession in the Zhenguan era, there were shameful failings within the imperial household, and its rites and music fell into disorder. During the Xianqing era, many governmental decisions were made within the palace, and the court’s rites and music were abandoned. One succession later came the abuse of irregular appointments issued in slant-sealed envelopes and ink-written edicts; another succession brought the outbreak of rebellion at Yuyang; and yet another brought the calamity of eunuchs monopolizing government. Surveying the rulers of the Li house of Tang from beginning to end, we see what is meant by establishing a succession improperly and having benighted successors: the prevailing wind would topple the dynasty, roots and all. This was human conduct, not Heaven. How could it merit discussion in terms of rites and music?
It is thus no wonder that Sima, with profound concern and far-reaching reflection, composed a discourse on centrality, correctness, harmony, and peace, to awaken the Heaven-endowed nature of the rulers of his own and subsequent ages. Master You said, “The gentleman attends to the root.” Master Zeng said, “This is called knowing the root.” In my humble view, the same may be said of Guang’s words on rites and music. Thus concludes this discourse.
Memorial
A proposed memorial in the voice of Song chief councillors, expressing thanks for the gift of the imperially composed poems “Viewing the Crops in Ruisheng Garden” and “Viewing the Wheat South of the City.” Ninth year of the Xiangfu era [1016].
Liu Juliang
Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: “Elegant yet conforming to proper standards; its unforced simplicity is pleasing.”

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官訓導穆批駢儷中委曲詳盡殆傑作也宜
冠本房
考試官教諭鄭批冲腴典則四六之擅場者
臣某等言某年月日欽蒙
聖恩特賜瑞聖園觀稼城南觀麥詩者伏以靈
苗瑞實呈異穎於星田
聖藻仙葩捧
宸辭於龍檢啓函拜
賜拭目增榮臣等誠懽誠忭稽首頓首竊惟
===
周朝以農事肇國故豳風以七月陳詩多
稼偉曾孫之詠興紀丘園來牟藹后稷之
傳情垂隴畝惟克艱而後罔艱思無逸乃
能有逸迨夫王跡旣熄慨矣刪後無詩大
風沛筑念靡及於桑麻夜帳楚歌涕徒悲
於姬侍芝房花萼惟騁雕纖雞塞玉笙虛
工流麗文不在茲時將有待茲蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
禹稼蕃滋
punctuated:
考試官訓導穆批：駢儷中委曲詳盡，殆傑作也，宜冠本房。
考試官教諭鄭批：冲腴典則，四六之擅場者。
臣某等言：某年月日，欽蒙聖恩，特賜瑞聖園觀稼、城南觀麥詩者。伏以靈苗瑞實，呈異穎於星田；聖藻仙葩，捧宸辭於龍檢。啓函拜賜，拭目增榮。臣等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首。竊惟周朝以農事肇國，故豳風以七月陳詩。多稼偉曾孫之詠，興紀丘園；來牟藹后稷之傳，情垂隴畝。惟克艱而後罔艱，思無逸乃能有逸。迨夫王跡旣熄，慨矣刪後無詩。大風沛筑，念靡及於桑麻；夜帳楚歌，涕徒悲於姬侍。芝房花萼，惟騁雕纖；雞塞玉笙，虛工流麗。文不在茲，時將有待。茲蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，禹稼蕃滋。
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor: Within its parallel phrasing, the treatment is nuanced and exhaustive. This is surely a masterpiece and deserves first place in this marking room.
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: Serene yet rich, classical and well regulated: an outstanding achievement in four-and-six prose.
Your servants, So-and-so and the others, state: On such-and-such a day, month, and year, we reverently received Your Majesty’s gracious special gift of the poems Viewing the Crops in Ruisheng Garden and Viewing the Wheat South of the City. We humbly reflect: numinous seedlings and auspicious grain display extraordinary ears in fields beneath the stars; with reverence we hold Your sacred compositions, blossoms of immortals, Your imperial words enclosed in dragon-adorned covers. Opening the case, we bow to receive the gift; wiping our eyes to read, we feel our honor increased. Your servants, truly joyful and truly delighted, bow our heads to the ground and kowtow.
We respectfully consider that the Zhou dynasty founded its realm upon agriculture; hence the Airs of Bin set forth the poem The Seventh Month. Abundant crops magnify the song of the royal descendant, its inspiration recording the fields and gardens; wheat and barley flourish in the tradition of Hou Ji, its sentiments extending to the cultivated furrows. Only by mastering hardship can one thereafter be free of hardship; only by keeping freedom from idleness in mind can one enjoy repose. When the traces of the true kings had faded, alas, after the editing of the Odes there was no more poetry. The Great Wind, accompanied by the zhu zither at Pei, gave no thought to mulberry and hemp; the Song of Chu, sung at night within the tent, shed tears merely in sorrow for a consort. The Fungal Chamber and Flower Calyx merely indulged in intricate ornament; Chicken Frontier and Jade Mouth Organ [?] vainly perfected flowing elegance. The true literary tradition did not reside in these: it awaited its proper time. Now, indeed, we have humbly encountered 〇〇〇〇 [four circles in the transcription], under whom crops flourish as in the days of Yu…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
堯文炳蔚
青宫浴德灼見小人之依
丹詔騰輝獨高大雅之作
妙造化之機軸斲元氣之斧斤
滿心而溢弗出冥搜肆筆以成允為
天縱
湯銘舜典匪直清燕以摛辭孔思周情且乗
逸遊而麗藻
雕輦翠旃時臨內圃
===
珠旗玉軚載駕城南秋實春華欣欣然喜經
御覽銀韜金縷洋洋乎揮灑
瓊章一穗兩岐不數張君之詠十畝千石方輕
汜氏之書允矣掩蘭菊於漢篇卓哉越茨
梁於周雅仰符出洛俯陋橫汾
絲綸之寶射奎璧而爭光
菽粟之篇逈琳琅而振響臣等啣
命自
天感恩無地飽百祿之素餐荷十行之
punctuated: 堯文炳蔚。青宫浴德，灼見小人之依；丹詔騰輝，獨高大雅之作。妙造化之機軸，斲元氣之斧斤。滿心而溢，弗出冥搜；肆筆以成，允為天縱。湯銘舜典，匪直清燕以摛辭；孔思周情，且乗逸遊而麗藻。雕輦翠旃，時臨內圃；珠旗玉軚，載駕城南。秋實春華，欣欣然喜經御覽；銀韜金縷，洋洋乎揮灑瓊章。一穗兩岐，不數張君之詠；十畝千石，方輕汜氏之書。允矣掩蘭菊於漢篇，卓哉越茨梁於周雅。仰符出洛，俯陋橫汾。絲綸之寶，射奎璧而爭光；菽粟之篇，逈琳琅而振響。臣等啣命自天，感恩無地，飽百祿之素餐，荷十行之
translation_en:
…Yao’s literary brilliance shines resplendently. While cultivating virtue in the Palace of the Heir Apparent, Your Majesty clearly discerned what sustains the common people; now your vermilion edict radiates splendor, and your composition stands alone in the loftiness of the Greater Odes. You command the wondrous loom of creation and wield the axe that shapes primordial vitality. Your words overflow from a full heart, without abstruse searching; freely setting brush to paper, you complete them—truly a gift of Heaven. Like Tang’s Inscription and the Canon of Shun, they are more than literary embellishments composed in tranquil leisure; embodying Confucius’s thought and the sentiments of the Zhou, you also fashion splendid verse during leisurely excursions. In a carved imperial carriage beneath kingfisher-green banners, you sometimes visit the inner gardens; with pearl-adorned flags and a jade carriage [?], you drive south of the city.

Autumn fruits and spring blossoms rejoice exuberantly to receive your imperial gaze; silver sheaths and golden threads accompany the magnificent outpouring of your jewel-like composition [?]. A single ear with two branches: Master Zhang’s verse need no longer be reckoned; a thousand shi of grain from ten mu: even Fan’s agricultural treatise now seems slight. Truly, your work eclipses the orchids and chrysanthemums of Han verse; outstanding indeed, it surpasses the thatched roofs and fishing weirs of the Zhou Odes. Above, it accords with the auspicious writing that emerged from the Luo River; beneath it, the song of crossing the Fen seems paltry. The treasure of your imperial words rivals the radiance of the Kui and Bi constellations; your poem on beans and grain resounds with a music surpassing the chime of precious jades [?]. We, your servants, have received our charge from Heaven and can find no means to repay your favor. Fed to satiety by your manifold emoluments, though rendering no service worthy of them, we gratefully receive your ten-line…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
賜札幸獲窺於
黼黻慚無補於涓埃方將什襲以珍藏至欲
銘心而鏤骨伏願
一人有慶恒先稼穡之艱難
萬壽無疆敢後岡陵之祝頌臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屛營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
===
聞
第叁塲
策
第一問
馬應羲
同考試官教諭沈批五答雄贍是策尤偉昔葛文康
謂記問之博當如陶隱居恥一事不知子豈其人歟健羨健羨
考試官訓導穆批其氣充其辭偉佳士也可敬可
服
punctuated:
賜札，幸獲窺於黼黻，慚無補於涓埃。方將什襲以珍藏，至欲銘心而鏤骨。伏願一人有慶，恒先稼穡之艱難；萬壽無疆，敢後岡陵之祝頌？臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屛營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁塲。
策。
第一問。
馬應羲。
同考試官教諭沈批：五答雄贍，是策尤偉。昔葛文康謂記問之博，當如陶隱居，恥一事不知。子豈其人歟？健羨，健羨！
考試官訓導穆批：其氣充，其辭偉，佳士也，可敬可服。
translation_en:
…the graciously bestowed letter. Fortunate to have glimpsed Your Majesty’s splendid composition, we are ashamed to have contributed not even the tiniest drop or speck. We shall wrap it in many layers and treasure it, and would engrave it upon our hearts and carve it into our bones. We humbly wish that the One Man, blessed with good fortune, may always give foremost thought to the hardships of sowing and reaping. May Your Majesty enjoy boundless longevity—how could we lag behind in offering blessings that liken it to the enduring hills and heights? Gazing toward Heaven and looking up to the Sage, we, your servants, cannot contain our fervent emotion and trembling awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third Session.
Policy Essays.
First Question.
Ma Yingxi.
Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: “All five answers are forceful and richly informed; this policy essay is especially outstanding. Ge Wenkang once said that breadth of acquired learning should be like that of Tao Yinju, who felt ashamed if there was even one thing he did not know. Could you be such a man? How I admire and envy you! How I admire and envy you!”
Comment by Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor: “His vital force is abundant; his diction is magnificent. He is an excellent scholar, worthy of respect and admiration.”

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭鄭批敷腴中度雋氣不羣殆真才
英也高薦何忝
古今能文者多矣必闔闢造化然後足以
爲聖人之藻彩帝王善文者衆矣必經緯
天地然後盡聖人之偉觀粤稽諸古黄竹
白雲垂芳帝籍玉書金簡爲章於天放勳
之文煥有虞舜之歌惟幾殷盤周誥炳若
丹靑充棟汗牛不一而足雖崆峒之碑漫
滅石鼓之文脫漏人猶競傳而寶之豈非
===
想陶唐之遺風羨宣王之大雅歟嗣是炎
劉以降趙宋以前誼辟英君代有作者沛
筑形歌唐殿載詠脩辭亦壯矣然未嘗思
治念不及民識者少之脩姱艷冶宫體雕
纖構思若豔矣然溺志嬪御慚德閨闈讀
者憾焉外此非無文也率皆疾風勁草溢
美臣隣賞花釣魚流連光景求其邁殷湯
之晨露掩重華之薫風者寂寥汗靑不多
見也洪惟我
punctuated:
考試官教諭鄭批：敷腴中度，雋氣不羣，殆真才英也。高薦何忝？

古今能文者多矣，必闔闢造化，然後足以爲聖人之藻彩；帝王善文者衆矣，必經緯天地，然後盡聖人之偉觀。粤稽諸古，黄竹白雲，垂芳帝籍；玉書金簡，爲章於天。放勳之文煥，有虞舜之歌惟幾，殷盤周誥，炳若丹靑，充棟汗牛，不一而足。雖崆峒之碑漫滅，石鼓之文脫漏，人猶競傳而寶之，豈非想陶唐之遺風，羨宣王之大雅歟？嗣是炎劉以降，趙宋以前，誼辟英君，代有作者。沛筑形歌，唐殿載詠，脩辭亦壯矣，然未嘗思治，念不及民，識者少之。脩姱艷冶，宫體雕纖，構思若豔矣，然溺志嬪御，慚德閨闈，讀者憾焉。外此非無文也，率皆疾風勁草，溢美臣隣；賞花釣魚，流連光景。求其邁殷湯之晨露，掩重華之薫風者，寂寥汗靑，不多見也。洪惟我
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “Rich and full, yet measured; its outstanding spirit is beyond the ordinary. Here indeed is a truly gifted talent. How could recommending him highly be undeserved?”

Many writers, ancient and modern, have excelled in composition. Yet only by encompassing the unfolding and closing of creation can their writing adequately serve as the sage’s literary adornment. Many emperors and kings have excelled in letters. Yet only by ordering heaven and earth can their writing fully display the sage’s grandeur. Looking back into antiquity, Yellow Bamboo and White Clouds left their enduring fragrance in imperial records; jade writings and golden tablets formed patterns in heaven. The literary brilliance of Fangxun shone forth, and the songs of Shun of Youyu concerned the subtle beginnings of affairs. The Pan Geng of Yin and the proclamations of Zhou gleamed like painted colors. Such writings filled buildings and made the oxen hauling them sweat: they were too numerous to enumerate. Although the inscription at Kongtong has worn away and the writings on the Stone Drums have suffered losses, people still vie to transmit and treasure them. Is this not because they yearn for the surviving influence of Taotang and admire the grand elegance of King Xuan?

Thereafter, from the Liu house of Han, which ruled under the virtue of fire, down to the time before the Zhao house of Song, worthy sovereigns and illustrious rulers produced writings in every age. At Pei, the zhu zither accompanied song; in Tang palace halls, verses were chanted. Their rhetoric was indeed magnificent, yet when they gave no thought to good government and their concern did not extend to the people, discerning readers thought little of them. Elaborate beauty and seductive ornament, the delicate embellishment of palace-style verse—their conceptions might seem splendid, yet when they abandoned themselves to palace women and disgraced their virtue in the inner chambers, readers regretted it. Nor were writings beyond these lacking. Most merely praised ministers to excess as “sturdy grass in a fierce wind,” or lingered over lovely scenes while enjoying flowers and fishing. If one seeks works surpassing Tang of Yin’s Morning Dew or eclipsing Chonghua’s Fragrant Wind, the historical record is sparse: few are to be found. Reverently we reflect upon our …

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝德侔天地道冠黃虞值奎壁宿啟列
之開紹帝王垂絕之統萬幾之暇作爲文
章揆雲漢之黼黻濯江漢之濤瀾易簡之
訓範圍兩儀昭回之光賁飾萬物猗歟盛
哉愚嘗拜觀
國初儒英之仰讚
御製文集之珍傳而窺其萬一矣請略陳之
登極之詔所以嚴華夷之防
大祀之文所以謹郊禋之禮
===
皇陵之碑述創業之艱難兗公之敕崇聖賢之
苗裔答
御殿之表而宰臣之體貌以隆草靖江之詔而
宮僚之責任斯重平蜀之製則昭旗常之
日月鐵券之文則錄佐
命之功庸誥湯和誥沐英尚元勳也誥李祺誥
黃琛貴戚里也勸農桑免租稅則后稷稼
穡之教也諭安南詔高麗則周王薄伐之
仁也誦循環之論而天道昭讀閱江之記
punctuated: 太祖高皇帝德侔天地，道冠黃虞，值奎壁宿啟列之開，紹帝王垂絕之統。萬幾之暇，作爲文章，揆雲漢之黼黻，濯江漢之濤瀾。易簡之訓，範圍兩儀；昭回之光，賁飾萬物。猗歟盛哉！愚嘗拜觀國初儒英之仰讚、御製文集之珍傳，而窺其萬一矣。請略陳之：登極之詔，所以嚴華夷之防；大祀之文，所以謹郊禋之禮；皇陵之碑，述創業之艱難；兗公之敕，崇聖賢之苗裔。答御殿之表，而宰臣之體貌以隆；草靖江之詔，而宮僚之責任斯重。平蜀之製，則昭旗常之日月；鐵券之文，則錄佐命之功庸。誥湯和，誥沐英，尚元勳也；誥李祺，誥黃琛，貴戚里也。勸農桑，免租稅，則后稷稼穡之教也；諭安南，詔高麗，則周王薄伐之仁也。誦循環之論，而天道昭；讀閱江之記，
translation_en:
…Taizu, the Gao Emperor, whose virtue equaled Heaven and Earth and whose Way surpassed those of Huangdi and Shun, came at a time when the Kui and Bi constellations inaugurated an opening [?], and continued the imperial succession that had nearly been broken. In moments of leisure amid his myriad affairs, he composed literary works, fashioning patterned splendors like those of the Milky Way and washing them in the billows of the Yangzi and Han rivers. His teachings of ease and simplicity encompassed Heaven and Earth; his circling radiance adorned all things. Ah, how magnificent! I have reverently examined the admiring praises of the outstanding scholars of our dynasty’s founding years and the treasured collection of imperially composed writings handed down to us, and have thereby glimpsed one ten-thousandth of this achievement. Allow me to set it out briefly.

His accession edict served to uphold strictly the boundary between the Chinese and the foreign peoples; his text for the Great Sacrifice served to ensure due observance of the suburban sacrificial rites. His inscription for the imperial mausoleum recounted the hardships of founding the dynasty; his edict concerning the Duke of Yan honored the descendants of the sages and worthies. By replying to the memorial concerning his taking his place in the imperial hall [?], he enhanced the ceremonial respect accorded his chief ministers; by drafting the edict concerning Jingjiang, he gave greater weight to the responsibilities of the princely household officials. His composition on the pacification of Shu made their achievements shine like the sun and moon upon commemorative banners; his text for the iron patent recorded the meritorious service of those who had helped establish his rule. His patents for Tang He and Mu Ying honored the foremost founding meritorious servants; those for Li Qi and Huang Chen exalted the imperial relatives by marriage. Encouraging farming and sericulture and remitting taxes embodied Hou Ji’s instruction in agriculture; admonishing Annan and issuing an edict to Gaoli embodied the benevolence of the Zhou king’s limited punitive campaigns. Reciting his discourse on cycles makes the Way of Heaven clear; reading his account of the Yuejiang Tower…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
而輿圖正水旱之說成而堯湯之心慰矣
伯夷之頌駁而韓柳之見卑矣秋宇澄清
之製姚姒之英藻也沛邑之歌寧不當北
面哉黃河良馬之文姬周之傑作也橫汾
之詠寧不拜下風哉
列聖相承天葩輝映迨今
皇上法
祖崇文頒繼統之詔而
大禮明降分祀之制而
===
大祭謹
敬一有箴髣髴唐虞精一之學也洪範有序
依稀夏禹九疇之演也
欽天有記聖王嚴恭之懿矩也緝熈之美不再
見耶四箴有註孔門傳授之心法也敬止
之風曾是加耶
睿製奎章崢嶸
秘府播之寰宇人誦家傳雖嵩衡岱華不足
以為高黃鍾大呂不足以為清大哉
punctuated:
而輿圖正。《水旱之說》成，而堯湯之心慰矣；《伯夷之頌》駁，而韓柳之見卑矣。《秋宇澄清》之製，姚姒之英藻也；《沛邑之歌》，寧不當北面哉？《黃河良馬》之文，姬周之傑作也；《橫汾之詠》，寧不拜下風哉？
列聖相承，天葩輝映。迨今皇上法祖崇文，頒繼統之詔而大禮明，降分祀之制而大祭謹。《敬一》有箴，髣髴唐虞精一之學也；《洪範》有序，依稀夏禹九疇之演也。《欽天》有記，聖王嚴恭之懿矩也，緝熈之美不再見耶？《四箴》有註，孔門傳授之心法也，敬止之風曾是加耶？睿製奎章，崢嶸秘府，播之寰宇，人誦家傳。雖嵩衡岱華不足以為高，黃鍾大呂不足以為清。大哉！
translation_en:
…and the realm’s territorial order is set right. When the Explanation of Floods and Droughts was completed, the concerns shared by Yao and Tang were assuaged; when the Eulogy of Bo Yi was refuted, the views of Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan were shown to be inferior. The imperial composition The Autumn Sky, Clear and Pure possesses the splendid literary artistry of Yao and Si—that is, Shun and Yu. Should not the Song of Pei bow northward before it as a subject? The piece The Yellow River and the Fine Horse is a masterpiece worthy of the Ji house of Zhou. Should not the song of crossing the Fen bow before its superiority?
The successive sage emperors inherited the throne, their heavenly literary blossoms illuminating one another. Now His Majesty follows his ancestors and honors literary culture. By issuing the edict on his succession, he clarified the Great Rites; by promulgating the decree on separate sacrifices, he ensured reverent observance of the great sacrifices. His Admonition on Revering Unity recalls the learning of refinement and single-mindedness under Tang and Yu—that is, Yao and Shun. His preface to the Great Plan recalls Yu of Xia’s exposition of the Nine Categories. His Record of Revering Heaven provides an exemplary standard of solemn reverence for sage kings: do we not see anew the beauty of unceasing cultivation of luminous virtue? His annotations to the Four Admonitions convey the teachings of the mind transmitted within the school of Confucius: could the practice of abiding in reverence surpass this? His sagely compositions, resplendent writings under the literary stars, stand lofty in the palace repositories and circulate throughout the world, recited by individuals and transmitted in every household. Even Song, Heng, Dai, and Hua cannot match their loftiness; even the Huangzhong and Dalü musical pitches cannot match their purity. Great indeed…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
王言眞有以追
皇祖之遐軌攀
列聖之逸駕矣於戲
堯言炳煥而如見
聖謨灝噩而孔彰愚也惟晝誦而味夜思而求
耳若廼鋪張對
天之洪休揚厲無前之偉績則自有文學供奉
之賢在草茅何足以語此幸執事進而敎
之
===
第二問
段有成
同考試官敎諭戴 批 五策涉筆動數百言不費探索
而斷决處深識講筵要領殆老成之見也一薦何忝
考試官訓導穆 批 結末數言足覘忠悃高選允宜
考試官敎諭鄭 批 講筵顛末歷述贍明是胷中有
書笥者
覽說命之書而後見講讀之所始披帝學
之篇而後知講筵之甚重何哉商周盛時
punctuated:
王言，眞有以追皇祖之遐軌，攀列聖之逸駕矣！於戲！堯言炳煥而如見，聖謨灝噩而孔彰。愚也惟晝誦而味，夜思而求耳。若廼鋪張對天之洪休，揚厲無前之偉績，則自有文學供奉之賢在，草茅何足以語此？幸執事進而敎之。

第二問
段有成

同考試官敎諭戴批：五策涉筆動數百言，不費探索，而斷决處深識講筵要領，殆老成之見也。一薦何忝？
考試官訓導穆批：結末數言，足覘忠悃，高選允宜。
考試官敎諭鄭批：講筵顛末，歷述贍明，是胷中有書笥者。

覽《說命》之書，而後見講讀之所始；披《帝學》之篇，而後知講筵之甚重。何哉？商周盛時，
translation_en:
…the imperial words truly suffice to follow the lofty course of the imperial ancestor and catch up with the swift carriages of the successive sage emperors! Ah! The words of Yao shine brilliantly, as though present before our eyes; the sage counsels, vast and august, are gloriously manifest. In my ignorance, I can only recite and savor them by day, ponder and seek their meaning by night. As for elaborating upon the great blessings received in response to Heaven and extolling unprecedented achievements, there are worthy literary attendants at court for that. How could an obscure rustic such as I be adequate to speak of these matters? I hope that you, honored sir, will advance and instruct me.

Second Policy Question
Duan Youcheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Dai, Instructor: “In each of the five policy essays, he readily writes several hundred words without laborious searching. Where he reaches his conclusions, he shows a profound understanding of the essentials of imperial lectures—judgments surely born of seasoned maturity. How could recommending him bring any discredit?”

Comment by Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor: “The few closing words suffice to reveal his sincere loyalty. Selection for a high place is fully warranted.”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “He recounts the imperial lectures from beginning to end with ample detail and clarity. Here is a man who carries a bookcase within his breast.”

Only after reading the Charge to Yue (Shuo ming) does one see the origins of lecturing and reading at court; only after opening the pages of Imperial Learning (Di xue) does one understand the great importance of imperial lectures. Why is this so? In the flourishing age of the Shang and Zhou…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
哲王世有師氏之職同與膳夫掖廷外朝
統於冢宰師保疑丞之外保氏史官之餘
靡人非賢靡地非學於戲至矣降而漢唐
古意寖失出入禁庭講論經學者似榮矣
然望之名儒出補外郡石顯憸巧播弄秘
庭白虎石渠之講讀果能不變其初耶橫
經帝幄紬繹陳編者似善矣然梨園之樂
汨亂聰明寧王之笛轉移心術集賢書院
之講學果能無改其舊耶甚者尚書樸學
厭而不好博士倚席廢而弗講駁乎無以
議為也迨夫宋室奎璧騰輝人文滋盛英
君誼辟銳意講筵勸學有所講讀有官以
水喻政得之小旻烹鮮喻治得之匪風善
詩學也薄征緩刑荒政論之脩德承天視
祲議之探禮學也上承下施蓋取諸鼎亂
極生治蓋取諸萃易學明也讀說命之篇
而三句特誦講五子之歌而六句再陳書
學深也論魯封疆講鄭鑄刑容非邃於春
punctuated: 哲王世有師氏之職，同與膳夫、掖廷、外朝統於冢宰。師保疑丞之外，保氏、史官之餘，靡人非賢，靡地非學。於戲，至矣！降而漢唐，古意寖失。出入禁庭、講論經學者似榮矣，然望之名儒，出補外郡；石顯憸巧，播弄秘庭。白虎、石渠之講讀，果能不變其初耶？橫經帝幄、紬繹陳編者似善矣，然梨園之樂，汨亂聰明；寧王之笛，轉移心術。集賢書院之講學，果能無改其舊耶？甚者，尚書樸學，厭而不好；博士倚席，廢而弗講。駁乎，無以議為也！迨夫宋室，奎璧騰輝，人文滋盛。英君誼辟，銳意講筵，勸學有所，講讀有官。以水喻政，得之小旻；烹鮮喻治，得之匪風：善詩學也。薄征緩刑，荒政論之；脩德承天，視祲議之：探禮學也。上承下施，蓋取諸鼎；亂極生治，蓋取諸萃：易學明也。讀說命之篇，而三句特誦；講五子之歌，而六句再陳：書學深也。論魯封疆，講鄭鑄刑，容非邃於春
translation_en:
…Under the sage kings, generation after generation maintained the office of Palace Mentor, which, together with the provisions officials, the palace quarters, and the outer court, came under the Minister of State. Beyond the preceptors, guardians, advisers, and assistants, and besides the Palace Guardians and historiographers, there was no one who was not worthy and no place that was not devoted to learning. Ah, how perfect it was!

Coming down to the Han and Tang, the spirit of antiquity gradually faded. Those who entered and left the inner palace to expound classical learning seemed honored indeed. Yet Wangzhi, a renowned Confucian scholar, was sent out to serve in a provincial commandery, while the crafty Shi Xian manipulated affairs within the palace. Could the lectures and readings at the White Tiger Hall and Stone Canal Pavilion truly have preserved their original purpose? Those who spread out the classics in the imperial tent and unraveled the meaning of ancient writings seemed to be doing good indeed. Yet the music of the Pear Garden clouded the ruler’s perception, and the Prince of Ning’s flute diverted his mind. Could the teaching at the Academy of Scholarly Worthies truly have remained unchanged? Worse still, plain learning in the Book of Documents was disliked and rejected; the erudites leaned their lecture mats aside, abandoning instruction. Such inconsistency scarcely merits discussion!

By the time of the Song dynasty, the literary constellations Kui and Bi shone brilliantly, and cultural accomplishment flourished. Illustrious rulers and righteous sovereigns devoted themselves earnestly to the imperial lectures. There were places for encouraging learning and officials charged with lecturing and reading. The comparison of government to water was drawn from “Lesser Heaven”; the comparison of governing to cooking small fish was drawn from “Unfavorable Wind”: this showed proficiency in the study of the Book of Odes. Light taxation and lenient punishments were discussed through the measures for famine relief; cultivating virtue to accord with Heaven was discussed through the duties of the Observer of Portents: this probed the learning of the rites. Support from below and beneficence from above were drawn from the hexagram “The Cauldron”; order arising when disorder reaches its extreme was drawn from “Gathering Together”: this showed clear understanding of the Book of Changes. When “The Charge to Yue” was read, three sentences were specially recited; when “The Songs of the Five Sons” was expounded, six sentences were presented once more: this showed profound learning in the Book of Documents. They discussed the boundaries of Lu and expounded Zheng’s casting of its penal laws in metal: could they have lacked profound understanding of the Spring…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
秋者歟中庸脩身大學入德容非優於記
禮者歟噫趙宋講筵有光帝學固可稱矣
然比隆商周賢聖繼作者則槩乎未之見
也恭惟我
皇祖甫入建康禮賢創舘首徴儒碩訪治談經
列聖相承講筵增重夷攷其時自微言以及大
政皆謀議之所先自公卿以及將吏皆咨
訪之所及宮僚之議叅之兩府藩屏之建
謀之侍臣桂彥良帝王心法之言則蒙
===
帝師之褒宋丞旨帝王傳心之論致動
天顏之喜祭酒吳顒次第進講則訓以中正之
道待制王禕進講大學則諭以德本之言
聞解縉正心之講而
睿覽至再喜士奇堯典之陳而稱善乂之講乾
之九四以儲貳為言則學士王達之見敏
也纂周易直指而備述本義則學士楊士
奇之論詳也留
神乙夜數御講筵春坊講章內閣改正尚書
punctuated:
秋者歟？中庸脩身，大學入德，容非優於記禮者歟？噫！趙宋講筵有光帝學，固可稱矣；然比隆商周，賢聖繼作者，則槩乎未之見也。
恭惟我皇祖甫入建康，禮賢創舘，首徴儒碩，訪治談經。列聖相承，講筵增重。夷攷其時，自微言以及大政，皆謀議之所先；自公卿以及將吏，皆咨訪之所及。宮僚之議，叅之兩府；藩屏之建，謀之侍臣。桂彥良帝王心法之言，則蒙帝師之褒；宋丞旨帝王傳心之論，致動天顏之喜。祭酒吳顒次第進講，則訓以中正之道；待制王禕進講大學，則諭以德本之言。聞解縉正心之講，而睿覽至再；喜士奇堯典之陳，而稱善。乂之講乾之九四，以儲貳為言，則學士王達之見敏也；纂周易直指而備述本義，則學士楊士奇之論詳也。留神乙夜，數御講筵。春坊講章，內閣改正；尚書
translation_en:
…the Spring and Autumn Annals? In cultivating oneself through the Doctrine of the Mean and entering into virtue through the Great Learning, could they have been anything but accomplished in the Record of Rites? Ah! The imperial lectures of the Zhao-Song dynasty lent lustre to imperial learning and certainly deserve praise. Yet, as for matching the splendour of the Shang and Zhou, when worthy and sage rulers arose in succession, we have scarcely seen their like.
We reverently reflect that, as soon as our imperial ancestor entered Jiankang, he honoured worthy men and established a hall, first summoning eminent Confucian scholars to consult them on government and discuss the classics. Successive sage sovereigns continued this practice, giving the imperial lectures still greater importance. Examining those times, we find that everything from subtle teachings to great affairs of state received priority in deliberations, and everyone from dukes and ministers to military commanders and administrative officials was consulted. Questions concerning palace officials were discussed with the two councils; the establishment of princely bulwarks was deliberated with attendant ministers. Gui Yanliang’s words on the essential teachings governing the minds of emperors and kings earned him praise as an “imperial preceptor”; the discourse by Song, Academician Recipient of Edicts [?], on the transmission of these teachings among emperors and kings brought joy to the imperial countenance. When Wu Yong, Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, presented lectures in sequence, the emperor instructed him in the Way of centrality and correctness. When Wang Yi, an Academician-in-Waiting, lectured on the Great Learning, the emperor admonished him with words about virtue as the root. Upon hearing Xie Jin’s lecture on rectifying the mind, the emperor read it twice; pleased with Shiqi’s exposition of the Canon of Yao, he pronounced it excellent. In the lecture on the fourth nine of the Qian hexagram [?], the discussion concerned the heir apparent: this showed the perceptiveness of Academician Wang Da. In compiling Direct Guidance to the Changes of Zhou and fully expounding the Original Meaning, Academician Yang Shiqi demonstrated the thoroughness of his interpretation. The emperor devoted his attention to study during the second watch of the night and frequently attended the imperial lectures. Lecture texts from the Spring Offices were revised by the Grand Secretariat; the Book of Documents…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
毛詩則解縉胡廣專閱焉經術何銳精也
周易春秋則幼孜士竒更覽焉古訓何探
賾也是誠以講學為治本以聖賢為家法
矣迨我
皇上察倫明物法
祖右文經筵日講而不間夫寒暑隨處用力而
靡二於宫庭隆體貌於細旃究心原於古
訓垂
敬一之旨衍四箴之義示學宫也正孔子先
===
師之號抑廣孝配享之非昭禮樂也雖商
宗之監成憲成王之酌祖道不是過矣一
何盛哉執事倘與薦焉則進陽爻退隂位
如昭素之辨乾龍闢君子闔小人若馮元
之推泰象尚當於
丹陛下陳之
第三問
楊茂時
同考試官訓導許批五策明實可錄而是篇尤嘉真
punctuated:
毛詩則解縉、胡廣專閱焉，經術何銳精也！周易、春秋則幼孜、士竒更覽焉，古訓何探賾也！是誠以講學為治本，以聖賢為家法矣。迨我皇上察倫明物，法祖右文，經筵日講而不間夫寒暑，隨處用力而靡二於宫庭，隆體貌於細旃，究心原於古訓，垂敬一之旨，衍四箴之義，示學宫也；正孔子先師之號，抑廣孝配享之非，昭禮樂也。雖商宗之監成憲、成王之酌祖道，不是過矣。一何盛哉！執事倘與薦焉，則進陽爻、退隂位，如昭素之辨乾龍；闢君子、闔小人，若馮元之推泰象，尚當於丹陛下陳之。
第三問
楊茂時
同考試官訓導許批：五策明實可錄，而是篇尤嘉，真
translation_en:
…As for the Mao Book of Odes, Xie Jin and Hu Guang examined it exclusively: how keen their dedication to classical learning! As for the Book of Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals, Youzi and Shiqi reviewed them in turn: how deeply they explored the ancient teachings! This was truly to make scholarly exposition the foundation of government and the sages and worthies the guiding models of the imperial house.
When our present Emperor came to rule, he examined human relationships and clarified the principles of things, emulated his ancestors, and honored literary learning. The Classics Colloquium and daily lectures continued uninterrupted through cold and heat; wherever he was, he applied himself with the same dedication as within the palace. He accorded lofty ceremonial respect to those on the fine lecture mats and investigated the foundations of the mind through ancient teachings. He issued his injunction on “Reverent Concentration on the One” and elaborated the meaning of the Four Admonitions to instruct the schools. He rectified Confucius’s title as First Teacher and rejected the impropriety of Guangxiao’s associated worship, thereby making rites and music manifest. Even the Shang ancestor’s adherence to established statutes and King Cheng’s drawing upon his ancestors’ way did not surpass this. How splendid indeed!
If you, honored examiners, should recommend me, I should yet present before the vermilion steps the principles of advancing the yang lines and withdrawing the yin positions, as Zhaosu did in distinguishing the dragons of the Qian hexagram; and of opening the way for gentlemen and closing it to petty men, as Feng Yuan did in expounding the image of the Tai hexagram.
Third Question
Yang Maoshi
Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Assistant Instructor: “The five policy essays are lucid and substantive, worthy of selection; this piece is especially commendable. Truly…”

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
策手也何惜高薦
考試官訓導穆批藻彩溢出而豐約中度是善揚
厲者取之
考試官敎諭鄭批周悉之見忠厚之言允宜錄出
以範來學
詠行葦之詩則知壽耇之當崇佩中庸之
旨則知臣工之宜體此三代之家法萬世
之懿矩也況開創之主其佐命之臣冒矢
石而不辭處風波而自任艱難備嘗茂著
===
勞烈功成之後謂宜貌敬心孚終始一致
而崇德報功可也奈何商周不作識者憾
焉犬馬土芥致歎軻書騎項溺冠貽譏青
史誅秦蹙項淮陰之績偉矣而卒招狗烹
之恨填國撫民酇侯之功高矣而未免械
繫之羞麟閣不名大臣之至禮也未幾而
有赤族之慘凌烟賦詩宰衡之至愛也無
何而形仆碑之咎迺若中令元勳鼎鐺有
耳魏公宿德倚重長城溥筦疾瘳而爵賞
punctuated:
策手也，何惜高薦！
考試官訓導穆批：藻彩溢出，而豐約中度，是善揚厲者，取之。
考試官敎諭鄭批：周悉之見，忠厚之言，允宜錄出，以範來學。
詠行葦之詩，則知壽耇之當崇；佩中庸之旨，則知臣工之宜體。此三代之家法，萬世之懿矩也。況開創之主，其佐命之臣，冒矢石而不辭，處風波而自任，艱難備嘗，茂著勞烈。功成之後，謂宜貌敬心孚，終始一致，而崇德報功可也。奈何商周不作，識者憾焉！犬馬土芥，致歎軻書；騎項溺冠，貽譏青史。誅秦蹙項，淮陰之績偉矣，而卒招狗烹之恨；填國撫民，酇侯之功高矣，而未免械繫之羞。麟閣不名，大臣之至禮也，未幾而有赤族之慘；凌烟賦詩，宰衡之至愛也，無何而形仆碑之咎。迺若中令元勳，鼎鐺有耳；魏公宿德，倚重長城。溥筦疾瘳，而爵賞
translation_en:
…a master of policy essays! Why hesitate to recommend him highly?
Examiner Mu, an Instructor, comments: “Literary brilliance overflows, yet elaboration and concision are properly balanced. This is someone skilled at celebrating worthy achievements. Select him.”
Examiner Zheng, a School Instructor, comments: “Comprehensive insights and words of loyalty and generosity: this certainly deserves to be recorded as a model for future students.”
When we recite the poem ‘The Reeds Along the Path,’ we understand that the aged should be honored; when we take to heart the meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean, we understand that ministers should be treated with consideration. These were the household principles of the Three Dynasties and exemplary standards for all ages. How much more does this apply to a founding ruler! The ministers who assisted him in establishing his mandate braved arrows and stones without demur and took responsibility amid turmoil. They experienced every hardship and rendered outstanding service. Once success had been achieved, surely he ought to show them outward respect and inward trust, remaining consistent from beginning to end, honoring virtue and rewarding merit. Alas, the likes of the Shang and Zhou rulers have not arisen again, to the regret of discerning men!
Treating ministers as dogs and horses or as dirt and weeds occasioned lament in the Book of Meng Ke; riding on their necks and urinating in their caps earned censure in the histories. In overthrowing Qin and crushing Xiang Yu, Huaiyin’s achievements were magnificent, yet he ultimately suffered the bitterness of the hunting dog boiled once its work was done. In securing the state and reassuring its people, the Marquis of Zan’s merit was great, yet he could not escape the humiliation of being put in fetters. Omitting a minister’s personal name in the Qilin Gallery was the highest courtesy toward a great minister, yet before long came the horror of his clan’s extermination. Composing a poem at Lingyan expressed the deepest affection for a chief minister, yet soon afterward came the fault of toppling his commemorative stele.
As for the founding merit of the Secretariat Director, ‘the cauldron and cooking pot have ears’ [?]; for the longstanding virtue of the Duke of Wei, he was relied upon as a Great Wall. When Pu Guan [?] recovered from illness, ranks and rewards were bestowed upon…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
醫工夷簡抱病而剪鬚親賜其體貌之尊
崇禮意之優渥固未能同符商周聖武之
君其視漢唐銕薄之主則彼善於此矣仰
惟
皇祖龍飛淮甸鹿逐胡元以忠孝爲家法以禮
義爲國維元勳碩德旣崇爵於上龍旣禱
之餘
縟典盛儀復追報於喬木見思之日中山不
祿則欷歔而流涕開平櫬至則痛哭而拊
膺武靖之功奇矣不以甥舅之貴戚而或
掩良禎之績茂矣不以兄弟之并用而見
疑稱吾子房而不名重劉基也
賜百歲之衣而慰藉禮宋濂也俞忠烈病革則
曰平章知予問疾乎天性骨肉之恩不是
加也郭靖海起避則曰第坐不汝關焉家
人父子之愛不是過也覽竹帛之舊績而
六王之元祀以崇龍蛇一章不媿汗於茲
耶勒鼎彝之前勳而列侯之爵以厚弓藏
punctuated:
醫工。夷簡抱病，而剪鬚親賜。其體貌之尊崇，禮意之優渥，固未能同符商周聖武之君；其視漢唐銕薄之主，則彼善於此矣。
仰惟皇祖龍飛淮甸，鹿逐胡元，以忠孝爲家法，以禮義爲國維。元勳碩德，旣崇爵於上龍旣禱之餘；縟典盛儀，復追報於喬木見思之日。中山不祿，則欷歔而流涕；開平櫬至，則痛哭而拊膺。武靖之功奇矣，不以甥舅之貴戚而或掩；良禎之績茂矣，不以兄弟之并用而見疑。稱吾子房而不名，重劉基也；賜百歲之衣而慰藉，禮宋濂也。俞忠烈病革，則曰：「平章知予問疾乎？」天性骨肉之恩，不是加也。郭靖海起避，則曰：「第坐，不汝關焉。」家人父子之愛，不是過也。覽竹帛之舊績，而六王之元祀以崇，龍蛇一章，不媿汗於茲耶？勒鼎彝之前勳，而列侯之爵以厚，弓藏
translation_en:
…the physician. When Yijian fell ill, the emperor cut off some of his own beard and personally bestowed it upon him. The honor shown to these ministers and the generous consideration accorded them could admittedly not match those of the sagely and martial rulers of Shang and Zhou. Yet compared with the harsh and ungenerous rulers of Han and Tang, these rulers were the better.
Reverently we recall how our Imperial Ancestor rose like a dragon in the Huai region and contended for the empire against the non-Han Yuan. He made loyalty and filial devotion the guiding principles of his house, and ritual propriety and righteousness the binding principles of the state. He exalted the ranks of men of founding merit and eminent virtue after “the dragon had already been prayed for” [?]; with elaborate rites and magnificent ceremonies, he further repaid their service after their deaths, when the sight of their tall trees called them to mind. When Zhongshan died, he sobbed and shed tears; when Kaiping’s coffin arrived, he wept bitterly and beat his breast. Wujing’s achievements were extraordinary: his status as an honored relative through the uncle–nephew relationship did not obscure them. Liangzhen’s accomplishments were outstanding: the simultaneous employment of brothers did not make him an object of suspicion. Calling Liu Ji “my Zifang,” rather than addressing him by his personal name, expressed his esteem for him. Bestowing a robe for a hundred years of life upon Song Lian and offering him comfort expressed his respect for him. When Yu Zhonglie became gravely ill, he said, “Does the Manager of Governmental Affairs know that I have inquired about his illness?” Even the natural affection between blood relatives could not exceed this. When Guo Jinghai rose to withdraw, he said, “Just remain seated; this does not concern you.” Even the love between father and son within a family could not surpass this. Reviewing the past achievements recorded on bamboo and silk, he exalted the principal sacrifices to the six princes. Would not the poem of the dragon and snakes blush with shame at this? Recording earlier merits upon bronze ritual vessels, he generously rewarded the marquises with noble rank—the bow put away…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
數語不報容於是耶若迺韓成之委身紀
信之誑楚也孫炎之罵賊巡遠之流亞也
忠節諸臣不一而足血食廟貌開府增光
於戲厚矣矧金書鐵券
天藻輝煌帶礪河山爵及苗裔所謂洽魚水於
一堂慶雲龍於千載我
皇祖以之矣愚也食粟而憶稷踐土而思禹於
我
皇祖君臣丕天之功自知不能摹乾坤繪日月
===
而揄揚其萬一矣謹摭拾以為明問復
第四問
黨宗正
考試官訓導穆批評隲歷代史才如指諸掌而結
末斷案歸美兩得之強學待問者也讀之終篇不覺斂衽
考試官教諭鄭批博極羣書邃於史學主司得子
可以自慶矣
事紀於儒臣之筆者可以史名事定於聖
人之筆者當以經論自有載籍以來芸編
punctuated:
數語不報容於是耶？若迺韓成之委身，紀信之誑楚也；孫炎之罵賊，巡遠之流亞也。忠節諸臣，不一而足；血食廟貌，開府增光。於戲，厚矣！矧金書鐵券，天藻輝煌，帶礪河山，爵及苗裔。所謂洽魚水於一堂，慶雲龍於千載，我皇祖以之矣。愚也，食粟而憶稷，踐土而思禹，於我皇祖君臣丕天之功，自知不能摹乾坤、繪日月，而揄揚其萬一矣。謹摭拾以為明問復。

第四問
黨宗正

考試官訓導穆批：評隲歷代史才，如指諸掌；而結末斷案、歸美，兩得之。強學待問者也。讀之終篇，不覺斂衽。

考試官教諭鄭批：博極羣書，邃於史學。主司得子，可以自慶矣。

事紀於儒臣之筆者，可以史名；事定於聖人之筆者，當以經論。自有載籍以來，芸編
translation_en:
…would those few words not find a place here [?]? As for Han Cheng’s sacrifice of himself, it was like Ji Xin’s deception of Chu; Sun Yan’s denunciation of the rebels placed him in the company of Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan. The loyal and steadfast ministers were too numerous to enumerate. They received sacrificial offerings in their temples, and the establishment of their official households added to their glory. Ah, how generous this was! Moreover, there were iron certificates inscribed in gold, resplendent with imperial composition, promising that their ranks would descend to their progeny until the rivers shrank to belts and the mountains to whetstones. What is called the harmony of fish and water within one hall, and the auspicious meeting of clouds and dragons once in a thousand years, was achieved by our Imperial Progenitor. Foolish though I am, when eating grain I remember Hou Ji, and when treading the earth I think of Yu. Concerning the Heaven-vast achievements [?] of our Imperial Progenitor and his ministers, I know that I cannot depict Heaven and Earth or portray the sun and moon so as to extol even one ten-thousandth of them. I have respectfully gathered these particulars to answer your discerning question.

Fourth Question
Dang Zongzheng

Comment by Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor: His assessment of historical talent through successive ages is as clear as pointing to something in his own palm. His concluding judgment and attribution of praise both hit the mark. Here is one who studies diligently and stands ready to answer questions. On finishing the entire essay, I involuntarily straightened my robes in respect.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: He has read widely across the whole range of books and possesses profound learning in history. The chief examiner may congratulate himself on having found you.

Events recorded by the brush of a Confucian minister may be called history; events adjudicated by the brush of a sage should be treated as a classic. Ever since written records first existed, volumes preserved with rue…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
蠹簡浩穰滿家史法相沿代有作者溫純
如左氏簡潔如子長雄健如孟堅是誠史
家之魯殿靈光而巋然者也然其才氣之
所充規模之所就要之所謂多聞習事而
猶未能離乎史也迺若朱子綱目之作發
宣尼之蘊成一家之言雖未敢擬經中之
史亦可謂史中之經矣此我
憲皇所以特命儒英法之而有續通鑑綱目之
書也請陳其槩而執事擇焉可乎蓋嘗攷
===
之書者古史也帝王之軌範政治之權輿
所從出也聖人從而定焉芟繁亂而剪浮
辭自唐虞而訖成周大經大法曉然而易
遵坦然而易行由是觀之則書非孔子莫
能定矣請米而作佳傳者豈能為其廝養
耶春秋者魯史記之名也君臣父子之大
經禮樂征伐之事所由紀也聖人從而脩
焉抑諸侯而尊王室即十二公之行事見
於二百四十二年之間而後善人勸焉淫
punctuated:
蠹簡浩穰滿家，史法相沿，代有作者。溫純如左氏，簡潔如子長，雄健如孟堅，是誠史家之魯殿靈光而巋然者也。然其才氣之所充，規模之所就，要之所謂多聞習事，而猶未能離乎史也。迺若朱子綱目之作，發宣尼之蘊，成一家之言，雖未敢擬經中之史，亦可謂史中之經矣。此我憲皇所以特命儒英法之，而有續通鑑綱目之書也。請陳其槩，而執事擇焉，可乎？
蓋嘗攷之，《書》者，古史也，帝王之軌範、政治之權輿所從出也。聖人從而定焉，芟繁亂而剪浮辭，自唐虞而訖成周，大經大法，曉然而易遵，坦然而易行。由是觀之，則《書》非孔子莫能定矣。請米而作佳傳者，豈能為其廝養耶？《春秋》者，魯史記之名也，君臣父子之大經、禮樂征伐之事所由紀也。聖人從而脩焉，抑諸侯而尊王室，即十二公之行事，見於二百四十二年之間，而後善人勸焉，淫
translation_en:
…moth-eaten bamboo slips, vast in number, fill households. The methods of historical writing have been handed down, with authors appearing in every age. Gentle and pure as Zuo shi, concise as Zichang, vigorous as Mengjian: these men indeed stand towering among historians, like the surviving Lingguang Palace of Lu. Yet, for all the fullness of their talent and spirit and the scope of their achievement, they ultimately exemplify what is called extensive learning and familiarity with affairs; they have still not transcended history.
As for Master Zhu’s Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror (Gangmu), it brings to light the profound meaning of Confucius and establishes an interpretation of its own. Though one would not venture to rank it with the histories among the Classics, it may indeed be called a classic among histories. This is why our Emperor Xian specially commanded outstanding Confucian scholars to take it as their model, producing the Continuation of the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror (Xu Tongjian Gangmu). May I set out its general purport for you, honored examiners, to consider?
I have examined the matter. The Book of Documents is an ancient history, the source of the models for emperors and kings and the beginnings of government. The Sage then established its text, cutting away what was prolix and confused and pruning empty phrases. From Tang and Yu down to the established Zhou dynasty, its great principles and laws are clear and easy to follow, straightforward and easy to put into practice. Viewed thus, none but Confucius could have established the Book of Documents. Could those who ask for grain in return for writing flattering biographies even serve as his menials?
The Spring and Autumn Annals was the name of the historical records of Lu. In it were recorded the great principles governing ruler and minister, father and son, and matters of rites, music, punitive expeditions, and warfare. The Sage then revised it, restraining the feudal lords and honoring the royal house. Through the events of the reigns of twelve dukes, presented over a span of 242 years, good people were encouraged, and the wicked…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
人懼焉執此論之則春秋非孔子莫能脩
矣受金而諛盛德者豈能望其藩籬耶於
戲尚書春秋不可及矣弗獲巳而思其次
其惟諸史乎諸史之良遷固其尤也辯而
不華質而不俚遷之得也議者謂其崇勢
利而羞貧賤特合抱之寸朽也可盡訾歟
贍而不穢詳而有體固之長也議者謂其
輕仁義而賤死節特連城之微瑕也可盡
譏歟吁自史才言之遷固又非諸史可同
===
日語矣昔之評者曰遷固之史可與左丘
明鴈行可使范曄北面可使陳壽作衙官
晉史而下可以奴僕命之何也評者之意
蓋以左氏之傳其文緩其旨遠炳然有三
代之風而班馬二史之雄深雅健似亦少
減故曰可與左丘明鴈行焉范曄之述東
漢標格卑陋文彩不足以動人嘗自擬其
傳贍不及班固則於遷可知矣故曰可使
范曄北面焉若夫陳壽之志三國義例舛
punctuated:
人懼焉。執此論之，則《春秋》非孔子莫能脩矣。受金而諛盛德者，豈能望其藩籬耶？於戲！《尚書》《春秋》不可及矣。弗獲巳而思其次，其惟諸史乎？諸史之良，遷、固其尤也。辯而不華，質而不俚，遷之得也。議者謂其崇勢利而羞貧賤，特合抱之寸朽也，可盡訾歟？贍而不穢，詳而有體，固之長也。議者謂其輕仁義而賤死節，特連城之微瑕也，可盡譏歟？吁！自史才言之，遷、固又非諸史可同日語矣。
昔之評者曰：「遷、固之史，可與左丘明鴈行，可使范曄北面，可使陳壽作衙官，晉史而下，可以奴僕命之。」何也？評者之意，蓋以左氏之傳，其文緩，其旨遠，炳然有三代之風；而班、馬二史之雄深雅健，似亦少減，故曰可與左丘明鴈行焉。范曄之述東漢，標格卑陋，文彩不足以動人，嘗自擬其傳，贍不及班固，則於遷可知矣，故曰可使范曄北面焉。若夫陳壽之志三國，義例舛
translation_en:
…the wicked are made afraid. Judging on this basis, none but Kongzi could have revised the Spring and Autumn Annals. How could those who accepted gold to lavish praise on supposedly abundant virtue even hope to approach his outer fence? Alas! The Book of Documents and the Spring and Autumn Annals are beyond reach. If, having no alternative, we consider what ranks next, would it not be the various histories? Among their finest authors, Sima Qian and Ban Gu stand foremost. Eloquent without being ornate, plain without being vulgar: these are Qian’s achievements. Critics say that he exalts power and profit and regards poverty and low station as shameful. Yet this is merely an inch of rot in a tree whose trunk takes two arms to encircle. Can one condemn him entirely for it? Ample without being cluttered, detailed yet well ordered: these are Gu’s strengths. Critics say that he makes light of benevolence and righteousness and disparages dying for one’s principles. Yet this is merely a slight flaw in a jade worth many cities. Can one disparage him entirely for it? Ah! In historical talent, Qian and Gu cannot even be spoken of in the same breath as the other historians.
A critic of former times said: “The histories of Qian and Gu may rank alongside Zuo Qiuming’s, like wild geese in formation. They could make Fan Ye face north as their pupil and Chen Shou serve as their subordinate officer. The authors of the histories of Jin and later periods may be called their servants.” Why so? The critic presumably meant that Master Zuo’s Commentary is measured in its prose and far-reaching in its purport, brilliantly displaying the spirit of the Three Dynasties. Even the grandeur, depth, elegance, and vigor of the two histories by Ban Gu and Sima Qian seem somewhat diminished beside it. Hence the statement that they may rank alongside Zuo Qiuming, like wild geese in formation. Fan Ye’s account of the Eastern Han is low and crude in its literary character, and its stylistic brilliance is insufficient to move readers. He once assessed his own biographies as falling short of Ban Gu’s in fullness; how they compare with Qian’s can therefore be inferred. Hence the statement that they could make Fan Ye face north as their pupil. As for Chen Shou’s Records of the Three Kingdoms, its principles and conventions are inconsistent…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
駁校其書而譏之者十有八九矣寧不爲
遷固之衙官耶外此若二晉所紀南北所
載朱紫不分鬼異詼諧則淫巫瞽史之流
矣寧非遷固之奴隸耶於戲遷固二子固
史之良也求其發聖人之微言邁二子之
製作吾於考亭綱目見之矣觀其自序云
表歳以首年而因年以著統大書以提要
而分註以備言歳周於上而天道明矣統
正於下而人道定矣大綱槩舉而鑒戒昭
===
矣衆物畢張而幾微著矣真自尚書春秋
以來未有也是固不可及矣然而威烈而
上未萃成編藝祖以還又自爲籍是猶未
免執卷有浩繁之歎臨文乏啓沃之資也
職此之故是以我
憲宗皇帝誕命儒臣以宋元二史之舊倣綱目
之法而成書也其書由建隆之開基至海
南之訖籙凡其中命令紀綱之詳國體安
危之係大書特書據往牒也敢爲臆說乎
punctuated:
駁，校其書而譏之者十有八九矣，寧不爲遷固之衙官耶？外此，若二晉所紀、南北所載，朱紫不分，鬼異詼諧，則淫巫瞽史之流矣，寧非遷固之奴隸耶？於戲！遷固二子固史之良也。求其發聖人之微言，邁二子之製作，吾於考亭《綱目》見之矣。觀其自序云：「表歳以首年，而因年以著統；大書以提要，而分註以備言。歳周於上，而天道明矣；統正於下，而人道定矣；大綱槩舉，而鑒戒昭矣；衆物畢張，而幾微著矣。」真自《尚書》《春秋》以來未有也，是固不可及矣。

然而威烈而上未萃成編，藝祖以還又自爲籍，是猶未免執卷有浩繁之歎，臨文乏啓沃之資也。職此之故，是以我憲宗皇帝誕命儒臣，以宋元二史之舊，倣《綱目》之法而成書也。其書由建隆之開基，至海南之訖籙，凡其中命令紀綱之詳、國體安危之係，大書特書，據往牒也，敢爲臆說乎？
translation_en:
…inconsistent; of those who examine his book, eight or nine out of ten criticize it. Could he fail to rank as a subordinate officer to Sima Qian and Ban Gu? Beyond this, the records of the two Jin dynasties and the accounts of the Northern and Southern dynasties fail to distinguish vermilion from purple—that is, the correct from the spurious—and abound in ghostly marvels and frivolous tales. They belong to the company of shamans practicing illicit rites and blind annalists. Are they not the slaves of Sima Qian and Ban Gu? Alas! Sima Qian and Ban Gu were indeed fine historians. Yet if we seek a work that elucidates the subtle words of the sages and surpasses the writings of these two, I have found it in the Outline and Details (Gangmu) of Kaoting [Zhu Xi]. Consider what he says in his own preface: “The year is displayed at the head of each annual entry, and the years serve to make the legitimate succession manifest. Prominent entries present the essentials, while subsidiary annotations supply the full account. The cycle of years appears above, making the Way of Heaven clear; the legitimate succession is set right below, establishing the human order. The main outlines are comprehensively presented, making lessons and warnings plain; the full array of affairs is laid out, revealing the subtlest beginnings of change.” Truly, nothing like it had existed since the Book of Documents and the Spring and Autumn Annals. It is indeed beyond compare.

Nevertheless, the period before King Weilie had not been gathered into a compilation, while that from Yizu [Emperor Taizu of Song] onward formed separate books. Thus, one still could not avoid sighing at the immense bulk when taking up these volumes, or finding, when consulting their text, insufficient material for enlightening and nourishing the ruler’s mind. Precisely for this reason, our Emperor Xianzong solemnly commanded his scholarly officials to draw upon the existing histories of Song and Yuan and compile a book modeled on the method of the Outline and Details. This book extends from the founding of the dynasty in the Jianlong era to the expiration of the dynastic mandate at Hainan [?]. Within it, the particulars of commands and governing institutions, and matters bearing upon the security or peril of the state, are recorded prominently and expressly, on the evidence of earlier records. Would they dare offer conjectures?

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
正例變例本成規也敢爲高論乎彼契丹
之出鮮卑女眞之起渤海亦爲采摭而附
見焉毋放失也敢闊略乎迺若胡元主華
世運極否似無足齒矣第勢成混一傳世
頗久雖則大書其年猶存外夷之意也諸
凡書法燁然華袞之褒凛然市朝之誅矣
末則紀
天兵之征討戡亂雄之割據
王師所加勢如破竹不旋踵而再闢乾坤肇脩
===
人紀眞萬代之快覩矣所謂三年鬼方之
伐六月玁狁之師豈足以爼豆於此哉於
戲訓裁斷自於
淵衷謨烈光昭乎信史與尚書春秋並觀可
也史云乎哉愚不敏謹述舊聞以對執事
以爲何如
第五問
梁佐
考試官訓導穆批深悉御將之略善談兵者也可
punctuated:
正例、變例，本成規也，敢爲高論乎？彼契丹之出鮮卑、女眞之起渤海，亦爲采摭而附見焉，毋放失也，敢闊略乎？迺若胡元主華，世運極否，似無足齒矣。第勢成混一，傳世頗久，雖則大書其年，猶存外夷之意也。諸凡書法，燁然華袞之褒，凛然市朝之誅矣。末則紀天兵之征討，戡亂雄之割據。王師所加，勢如破竹，不旋踵而再闢乾坤，肇脩人紀，眞萬代之快覩矣！所謂三年鬼方之伐、六月玁狁之師，豈足以爼豆於此哉？於戲！訓裁斷自於淵衷，謨烈光昭乎信史，與《尚書》《春秋》並觀可也，史云乎哉？愚不敏，謹述舊聞以對執事，以爲何如？
第五問
梁佐
考試官訓導穆批：深悉御將之略，善談兵者也。可
translation_en:
…Its regular and exceptional conventions follow established rules: would its compilers dare advance lofty theories of their own? They also gathered material on the Khitan’s descent from the Xianbei and the Jurchens’ rise from Bohai, appending accounts of them so that nothing would be lost: would they dare treat these matters cursorily? As for the barbarian Yuan ruling China, the fortunes of the age had reached their lowest ebb, and it might seem unworthy of mention. Yet it achieved unification and endured for many generations. Although its years are prominently recorded, the intention remains to treat it as a foreign barbarian power. Throughout, the conventions of historical writing confer praise as splendid as an ornate ceremonial robe and impose condemnation as stern as execution in the marketplace.
At the end, the work records the imperial armies’ campaigns and their suppression of the territories held by rebellious strongmen. Wherever the royal armies advanced, their momentum was like splitting bamboo. In no time they opened heaven and earth anew and began restoring the bonds of human society—a truly gratifying spectacle for all ages! How could the three-year campaign against Guifang or the expedition against the Xianyun in the sixth month deserve comparable ceremonial honor? Ah! The instructions and judgments [?] proceeded from the Emperor’s profound mind; his plans and achievements shine forth in this trustworthy history. It may rightly be viewed alongside the Book of Documents and the Spring and Autumn Annals. Could it be called merely a history? Dull-witted as I am, I have respectfully recounted what I have previously learned in reply to you, honored examiners. What do you think of it?
Fifth Question
Liang Zuo
Comment by Examiner Mu, Assistant Instructor: He thoroughly understands the strategy of controlling generals and is skilled in discussing military affairs. Worthy of…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
嘉可嘉
考試官教諭鄭批處分邊務甚當志存經濟者也
置之高等允協輿論
讀司馬附衆威敵之書則知制勝之道存
乎將誦少陵神武英雄之詠則知駕馭之
道存乎君何也疆場之事甚重兵戎之寄
匪輕矧開基逐鹿之秋重恢九縣之日食
非己之穀粟取非己之城邑於斯時而得
聖明豁達之主馭鷹揚壯猷之將則氣燄之振
===
賢於長城威名之重隱若敵國而成混一
丕天之績者無難矣萬一不知屈羣策攬
英賢焉所謂有一范增而不能用者也幾
何不敗廼翁事哉於戲商周放伐之迹遠
矣請以漢宋創復之故質之登壇一拜而
國士收於俄頃之間洗踞一見而爪牙屈
於指顧之際則繼秦而帝也在目中矣高
帝之英孰出其右歟岸幘以迎而致伏波
帝王之歎澠池以褒而激馮異巾車之恩
punctuated:
嘉，可嘉！
考試官教諭鄭批：處分邊務甚當，志存經濟者也。置之高等，允協輿論。
讀司馬附衆威敵之書，則知制勝之道存乎將；誦少陵神武英雄之詠，則知駕馭之道存乎君。何也？疆場之事甚重，兵戎之寄匪輕。矧開基逐鹿之秋，重恢九縣之日，食非己之穀粟，取非己之城邑，於斯時而得聖明豁達之主，馭鷹揚壯猷之將，則氣燄之振，賢於長城；威名之重，隱若敵國。而成混一丕天之績者，無難矣。萬一不知屈羣策、攬英賢焉，所謂有一范增而不能用者也，幾何不敗廼翁事哉！於戲！商周放伐之迹遠矣，請以漢宋創復之故質之。登壇一拜，而國士收於俄頃之間；洗踞一見，而爪牙屈於指顧之際，則繼秦而帝也在目中矣。高帝之英，孰出其右歟？岸幘以迎，而致伏波帝王之歎；澠池以褒，而激馮異巾車之恩，
translation_en:
…praiseworthy, truly praiseworthy!
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: His dispositions for frontier affairs are most appropriate; he is a man intent upon statecraft. Placing him in a high rank accords fully with the general judgment.
Reading the Sima treatise on winning the allegiance of the troops and overawing the enemy, one knows that the means of securing victory lie with the general. Reciting Shaoling’s verses on divine martial prowess and heroic men, one knows that the means of directing generals lie with the ruler. Why is this? Affairs on the frontier are exceedingly weighty, and military responsibility is no light trust. How much more so when founding a dynasty and contending for the realm, or restoring the empire, when one eats grain that is not one’s own and takes cities that are not one’s own! If at such a time an enlightened and magnanimous sovereign directs generals of soaring martial vigor and mighty strategic ability, their surging force will surpass a long wall, and their imposing renown will rival the might of an entire state. Then accomplishing the great work of unifying all under Heaven [?] will present no difficulty. Should the ruler fail to draw upon the counsel of many and gather outstanding worthies, he will be what is called a man who ‘had a Fan Zeng but could not employ him.’ How could he avoid ruining his old man’s enterprise!
Alas! The expulsions and punitive campaigns of the Shang and Zhou lie far in the past. Let us test this against the precedents of founding and restoration under the Han and Song. One appointment upon the general’s platform secured an outstanding man of the realm in an instant; one audience while sitting with feet being washed brought a stalwart servant into submission at a gesture. Succeeding Qin as emperor was then already in sight. Who could surpass Emperor Gao in heroic talent? By welcoming his visitor with his headcloth pushed back, the ruler elicited from the General Who Calms the Waves an admiring exclamation that he was a true emperor; by praising Feng Yi at Mianchi, he stirred gratitude for the kindness shown during the days of the curtained carriage…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
則祀漢配天也特掌上耳光武之賢孰能
爲之大畧乎高光之雄尚矣藝祖之略亦
有可稱郭進之在西山軍校越訴則執之
以賜進此感之以誠也曹彬之請使相官
恐太隆則寧賜之以錢此勉之以權也伐
西蜀之將至脫裘帽以衣而不惜謂非結
之以恩耶征江南之將至出匣劒以警而
無貸謂非懼之以法耶嗟夫漢之高光宋
之藝祖誠孫綽所謂馭龍馭虎者矣噫茲
特昔人謂之暗合孫吳者爾惟我
===
聖祖奮迹淮甸汛掃胡塵精神義氣感召招徠
一時猛將如雲謀臣如雨殆將擺頗牧於
禁中走穰侯於堂下矣何其盛哉嘗敬攷
之其與劉基論兵則曰克敵在兵而制兵
在將兵無節制則將不任將非其人則兵
必敗至謂因敵制勝豈必泥古闔闢竒正
在通其變容非不泥其迹而獨用其神乎
諭徐達伐張士誠則曰自大亂以來豪傑
punctuated: 則祀漢配天也，特掌上耳。光武之賢，孰能爲之大畧乎？高、光之雄尚矣，藝祖之略亦有可稱。郭進之在西山，軍校越訴，則執之以賜進，此感之以誠也。曹彬之請使相，官恐太隆，則寧賜之以錢，此勉之以權也。伐西蜀之將至，脫裘帽以衣而不惜，謂非結之以恩耶？征江南之將至，出匣劒以警而無貸，謂非懼之以法耶？嗟夫！漢之高、光，宋之藝祖，誠孫綽所謂馭龍馭虎者矣。噫！茲特昔人謂之暗合孫吳者爾。惟我聖祖奮迹淮甸，汛掃胡塵，精神義氣，感召招徠，一時猛將如雲，謀臣如雨，殆將擺頗、牧於禁中，走穰侯於堂下矣。何其盛哉！嘗敬攷之，其與劉基論兵，則曰：「克敵在兵，而制兵在將。兵無節制，則將不任；將非其人，則兵必敗。」至謂：「因敵制勝，豈必泥古？闔闢竒正，在通其變。」容非不泥其迹而獨用其神乎？諭徐達伐張士誠，則曰：「自大亂以來，豪傑
translation_en:
…then restoring the Han sacrifices and associating its imperial ancestor with Heaven was merely a matter within his grasp. Who could match Guangwu’s broad strategy and ability?
