The greatness of Gaozu and Guangwu was indeed lofty; the strategy of the Song founding emperor also deserves praise. When Guo Jin was stationed at Xishan, a military officer bypassed his superiors to lodge an accusation against him. The emperor had the officer seized and handed over to Guo Jin: this was winning his loyalty through sincerity. When Cao Bin requested appointment as military commissioner with a concurrent grand councilor’s title, the emperor feared that the rank would be too exalted and preferred to reward him with money: this was encouraging him through expedient judgment. When the commander charged with conquering Western Shu came before him, he took off his own fur robe and cap and bestowed them without reluctance. Was this not binding him through favor? When the commander charged with campaigning against Jiangnan came before him, he brought forth a sword from its case to warn him that there would be no pardon. Was this not instilling fear through law? Ah! Gaozu and Guangwu of the Han and the founding emperor of the Song were truly what Sun Chuo called men who could harness dragons and tigers. Yet these were merely men whom earlier writers described as unconsciously conforming to the teachings of Sunzi and Wu Qi.
Our sagely founding ancestor rose in the Huai region and swept away the dust of the northern invaders. His spirit and righteous ardor inspired men to answer his call and join him. At that time, fierce generals gathered like clouds and strategists like rain. It was almost as though he could marshal men like Lian Po and Li Mu within his palace and make a man like the Marquis of Rang hurry to serve below his hall. How magnificent it was! I have respectfully examined these matters. When discussing warfare with Liu Ji, he said: “Defeating the enemy depends on the troops, but controlling the troops depends on the commander. If the troops lack discipline, the commander is unequal to his responsibilities; if the commander is not the right man, the troops will certainly be defeated.” He went so far as to say: “Achieve victory by adapting to the enemy: why must one cling to antiquity? Closing and opening, unconventional and conventional operations—all depend on understanding their transformations.” Surely this was employing the animating spirit of ancient methods without being bound by their outward forms? When instructing Xu Da to attack Zhang Shicheng, he said: “Since the onset of the great disorder, heroes…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
並起江南亂雄西有陳友諒東有張士誠
聚淵寇攘數侵疆塲今姑蘇諸郡未下命
卿等討之又謂克敵者必以成功爲效樹
德者必以廣恩爲務是誠仁義之師神武
而不殺者也取中原之命則勤懇於部伍
分數之嚴虛實通變之法其決勝萬全之
師範歟捷蘭州之諭則諄切於恃功驕恣
之戒高危滿溢之憂其明哲保身之藥石
歟佩遣使諭將之勅而凛乎四失之責眞
===
===
對病之良劑也讀與李翀論武之言而確
然四善之兼眞却敵之良圖也於戲
聖謨昭乎日月
睿筭炳乎丹青方今南征之將果能書紳而儆
目莊誦而銘心又於定興指授之略西平
策應之方凡擊蛇首尾之勢逐鹿掎角之
謀悉講求其故而不泥其迹焉將見如虎
豹之在山若風雷之肅物乘月奏笳而胡
騎遠遁雪夜進旅而元濟成擒矣何也昔
punctuated: 並起，江南亂雄，西有陳友諒，東有張士誠，聚淵寇攘，數侵疆塲。今姑蘇諸郡未下，命卿等討之。」又謂：「克敵者必以成功爲效，樹德者必以廣恩爲務。」是誠仁義之師，神武而不殺者也。取中原之命，則勤懇於部伍分數之嚴、虛實通變之法，其決勝萬全之師範歟？捷蘭州之諭，則諄切於恃功驕恣之戒、高危滿溢之憂，其明哲保身之藥石歟？佩遣使諭將之勅，而凛乎四失之責，眞對病之良劑也。讀與李翀論武之言，而確然四善之兼，眞却敵之良圖也。於戲！聖謨昭乎日月，睿筭炳乎丹青！方今南征之將，果能書紳而儆目，莊誦而銘心，又於定興指授之略、西平策應之方，凡擊蛇首尾之勢、逐鹿掎角之謀，悉講求其故，而不泥其迹焉，將見如虎豹之在山，若風雷之肅物，乘月奏笳而胡騎遠遁，雪夜進旅而元濟成擒矣。何也？昔
translation_en:
…arose together. Among the powerful rebels south of the Yangzi were Chen Youliang in the west and Zhang Shicheng in the east. They gathered in deep pools [?], plundering and repeatedly invading our borders. Now, since the various prefectures around Gusu have not yet submitted, I command you to campaign against them.” He also said: “Those who overcome the enemy must measure their effectiveness by success; those who establish virtue must make extending benevolence their task.” This was truly an army of benevolence and righteousness, possessing divine martial prowess without killing. In his command to take the Central Plain, he earnestly stressed strict organization of units and their numerical divisions, and methods of adapting to weakness and strength as circumstances changed. Was this not a model for securing victory with complete assurance? In his instruction following the victory at Lanzhou, he insistently warned against relying on achievements to become arrogant and unrestrained, and expressed concern over the dangers of high position and excessive pride. Was this not salutary medicine for preserving oneself through wisdom? Reverently receiving the edict sent by an envoy to instruct the generals, one trembles at its reproach of the four failings: truly an excellent remedy precisely suited to the illness. Reading his words on military affairs addressed to Li Chong, one firmly recognizes the need to combine the four virtues: truly an excellent plan for repelling the enemy.

Ah! His sagely counsels shine like the sun and moon; his wise calculations glow in the painted record! If the generals now campaigning in the south can indeed write these words on their sashes to keep them before their eyes as a warning, solemnly recite them and engrave them upon their hearts; and if, moreover, they investigate thoroughly the reasoning behind Dingxing’s plans for directing operations and Xiping’s methods of coordinated support—all the dispositions by which a snake’s head and tail respond to an attack, and all the plans for seizing the quarry by its legs and horns—without rigidly adhering to their outward forms, then we shall see them like tigers and leopards in the mountains, like wind and thunder striking awe into all things. They will sound reed pipes beneath the moon, and the non-Chinese cavalry will flee far away; they will advance their troops on a snowy night, and Yuanji will be captured. Why is this so? In former times…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
徵側勇冠一方而竟就伏波之戮吕嘉威
行五嶺而終摧下瀨之師矧么麽逆庸特
釜中之魚机上之肉耳寧免服藁街之誅
快鯨鯢之戮哉知此則執事所謂飲富良
之馬標銅柱之勳者可坐而策也生非知
兵者然望長安而興感慨封狼居而禪姑
衍竊有志焉幸恕其狂斐而進教之
punctuated: 徵側勇冠一方，而竟就伏波之戮；吕嘉威行五嶺，而終摧下瀨之師。矧么麽逆庸，特釜中之魚、机上之肉耳，寧免服藁街之誅，快鯨鯢之戮哉？知此，則執事所謂飲富良之馬、標銅柱之勳者，可坐而策也。生非知兵者，然望長安而興感慨，封狼居而禪姑衍，竊有志焉。幸恕其狂斐而進教之。
translation_en:
…Zheng Ce’s valor surpassed all others in her region, yet she ultimately met her death at the hands of the General Who Calms the Waves; Lü Jia’s might extended throughout the Five Ranges, yet he was finally crushed by the army of the General Who Descends the Rapids. How much less could the paltry rebel Yong [?], merely a fish in a cauldron or meat on a chopping block, escape execution at Gao Street and the gratifying slaughter of such a great malefactor? Once this is understood, the achievements you speak of—watering horses in the Fuliang River and commemorating military merit with a bronze pillar—can be planned while seated at ease.

I, a mere student, am no expert in warfare. Yet gazing toward Chang’an stirs deep feelings in me, and I privately aspire to perform the feng sacrifice at Mount Langju [?] and the shan sacrifice at Mount Guyan, in celebration of victory. I hope you will forgive my rash and ill-considered words and favor me with your instruction.

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
雲南鄉試錄後序
嘉靖丁酉秋八月旺不穀以
應聘至濫竿文柄以職事當
序末簡稽之前史滇省爲古
西南夷尚矣自漢迄唐臣叛
靡一迨胡元統天始入職方
若幸也第以服左衽而言侏
===
===
儒者猶夫昔也匪滇爲然斯
時也腥氣迷天汚流漲地雖
河洛文獻之邦中土衣冠之
裔胥而爲夷者十室八九自
今攷之若許魯齋之闡明道
學郝伯常之博綜經史亦士
之魯殿靈光而巋然者顧廼
punctuated:
雲南鄉試錄後序

嘉靖丁酉秋八月，旺不穀以應聘至，濫竿文柄，以職事當序末簡。稽之前史，滇省爲古西南夷，尚矣。自漢迄唐，臣叛靡一。迨胡元統天，始入職方，若幸也。第以服左衽而言侏儒者，猶夫昔也。匪滇爲然，斯時也，腥氣迷天，汚流漲地，雖河洛文獻之邦、中土衣冠之裔，胥而爲夷者，十室八九。自今攷之，若許魯齋之闡明道學、郝伯常之博綜經史，亦士之魯殿靈光而巋然者。顧廼
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yunnan Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the dingyou year of Jiajing [1537], I, Wang, unworthy as I am, arrived in response to an invitation and undeservedly assumed authority over literary selection [?]. My official duties require me to append a postface to the closing pages. Examining earlier histories, one finds that Yunnan’s identification with the ancient Southwestern Barbarians goes far back. From the Han through the Tang, its submission and rebellion were inconstant. Only when the barbarian Yuan ruled All under Heaven was it incorporated into the imperial territorial registers—seemingly a fortunate development. Yet its people still wore robes fastening on the left and spoke in the unintelligible speech of dwarfs, just as before.

Nor was this true of Yunnan alone. At that time, a rank stench obscured the heavens and polluted currents flooded the earth. Even in the lands of the Yellow and Luo Rivers, with their literary heritage and worthy men, and among the descendants of the cultured elite of the Central Lands, eight or nine households in ten had collectively become barbarians. Looking back from the present, men such as Xu Luzhai, who elucidated the Learning of the Way, and Hao Bochang, whose learning comprehensively embraced the classics and histories, stood lofty among scholars like the surviving Lingguang Hall of Lu. Yet they …

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
俛首而拜犬豕甘心而飽胡
祿他尚何責耶間有若劉因
者居元近甸密邇朔庭而於
胡鼎不肯一染指焉可謂巨
浸懷襄而砥柱中流者矣然
降奴奔妾之言見於渡江之
賦識者恨之得非夷俗入人
===
之深雖賢者有不免歟是亦
天地之大變矣恭惟我
皇祖驅胡沙漠廓清海宇開
天一詔傳檄中原讀之使人毛髮
森灑凜然夷夏之分定律議
禮俾中國復文明之會洗左
衽之俗焉旋乾轉坤卓越千
punctuated:
俛首而拜犬豕，甘心而飽胡祿，他尚何責耶？間有若劉因者，居元近甸，密邇朔庭，而於胡鼎不肯一染指焉，可謂巨浸懷襄而砥柱中流者矣。然「降奴奔妾」之言見於《渡江》之賦，識者恨之，得非夷俗入人之深，雖賢者有不免歟？是亦天地之大變矣。
恭惟我皇祖驅胡沙漠，廓清海宇，開天一詔，傳檄中原，讀之使人毛髮森灑，凜然夷夏之分。定律議禮，俾中國復文明之會，洗左衽之俗焉。旋乾轉坤，卓越千
translation_en:
…bowed their heads and paid homage to dogs and swine, willingly feeding themselves to satiety on barbarian stipends. What could one demand of the others? Occasionally there was someone like Liu Yin, who lived in the region near the Yuan capital, close to the northern court, yet refused even once to dip a finger into the barbarians’ cauldron. He might well be called a pillar of rock standing midstream amid an overwhelming flood. Yet the words “surrendered slaves and runaway concubines” appear in his rhapsody “Crossing the River,” to the regret of discerning readers. Could it be that barbarian customs had penetrated people so deeply that even the worthy could not wholly escape them? This too was a great upheaval in Heaven and Earth.
We reverently reflect that our imperial ancestor drove the barbarians into the sandy wastes and swept clean the realm within the seas. With a single edict inaugurating a new order, he sent his proclamation throughout the Central Plain. Reading it makes one’s hair stand on end, instilling an awesome sense of the distinction between barbarians and Chinese. He established laws and deliberated upon ritual, enabling the Central Kingdom to return to an age of cultural brilliance and washing away the custom of fastening robes on the left. He turned Heaven and Earth about, surpassing a thousand…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
古
皇祖之績蔑以加巳
列聖相承化民俗俗經生學究一
變至道其弓旌之所迎科目
之所舉率皆當時豪俊而翊
賛
皇猷丕闡化理雖唐虞之際於斯
爲盛焉是以滇雲之域號稱
僻壤而士生其間往往涵泳
聖涯歌頌熈皡擢科登仕代
不乏人頃歲言者以茲土雖
遠夷荒域而
天地涵育之久人文炳蔚崇而舘
閣要而臺省胥皆沐
punctuated: 古，皇祖之績蔑以加巳。列聖相承，化民俗俗，經生學究一變至道。其弓旌之所迎、科目之所舉，率皆當時豪俊，而翊賛皇猷，丕闡化理。雖唐虞之際，於斯爲盛焉。是以滇雲之域，號稱僻壤，而士生其間，往往涵泳聖涯，歌頌熈皡，擢科登仕，代不乏人。頃歲，言者以茲土雖遠夷荒域，而天地涵育之久，人文炳蔚，崇而舘閣，要而臺省，胥皆沐
translation_en: …antiquity; nothing could surpass the achievements of our imperial progenitor. The successive sage sovereigns transformed the people's customs [?], and scholars devoted to the Classics, through a single transformation, attained the Way. Those welcomed with bows and banners of recruitment and selected through the examinations were generally the outstanding talents of their age. They assisted the imperial plans and greatly advanced moral transformation and good governance. Even compared with the age of Yao and Shun, this age was more flourishing. Thus, although the region of Dianyun, or Yunnan, is known as a remote land, scholars born there have often immersed themselves in the teachings of the sages and sung praises of radiant harmony. In every generation there have been men who succeeded in the examinations and entered official service. In recent years, those submitting proposals argued that, although this land was a distant wilderness inhabited by non-Han peoples, Heaven and Earth had nurtured it for so long that literary culture shone brilliantly. Those occupying the lofty posts of the Hanlin Academy and the important posts of the Censorate and central administration had all received…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
殊恩叨清選與中州縉紳項背相
望有鄒魯之遺焉請增解額
爲遐壤勸疏奏
皇上特賜俞允其變夷之功作人
之盛可仰窺其萬一矣是舉
也就試者殆千人鎖院如
制三試之則見摛辭脫穎談王論
===
道主六經而奴百氏啖粱肉
而茹苦茶華藻雅贍若照乗
木難媚澤奪目所謂盈前珠
璣而揀汰爲難者也豈不盛
歟諸士子之登茲選者眞千
載一時之逢亦旣幸且榮矣
尚其仰體豐芑之遺而以古
punctuated:
殊恩，叨清選，與中州縉紳項背相望，有鄒魯之遺焉。請增解額，爲遐壤勸。疏奏，皇上特賜俞允。其變夷之功、作人之盛，可仰窺其萬一矣。
是舉也，就試者殆千人，鎖院如制。三試之，則見摛辭脫穎，談王論道，主六經而奴百氏，啖粱肉而茹苦茶。華藻雅贍，若照乗、木難，媚澤奪目，所謂盈前珠璣而揀汰爲難者也。豈不盛歟！
諸士子之登茲選者，眞千載一時之逢，亦旣幸且榮矣。尚其仰體豐芑之遺，而以古
translation_en:
…special favor and are privileged to receive appointments to distinguished posts. They follow one another in close succession alongside the scholar-officials of the central provinces, preserving something of the legacy of Zou and Lu, the homelands of Mencius and Confucius. A request was made to increase the quota of provincial graduates, to encourage this distant region. When the memorial was submitted, His Majesty graciously granted special approval. From this we may reverently glimpse one ten-thousandth of his achievement in transforming non-Han peoples and his magnificent cultivation of talent.
For this examination, nearly a thousand candidates presented themselves. The examination compound was sealed in accordance with regulations. Through the three examination sessions, we saw outstanding compositions emerge, discussing kingly government and expounding the Way. They took the Six Classics as their masters and the hundred schools as their servants, feasting on fine grain and meat while also partaking of bitter tea. Their literary embellishments were elegant and abundant, like carriage-illuminating pearls and munan gems, whose enchanting luster dazzles the eye. This was truly what is meant by having pearls and jewels fill one’s view, making selection and rejection difficult. Was this not a splendid achievement!
Those candidates who have gained selection here have truly encountered an opportunity that comes but once in a thousand years; theirs is both good fortune and honor. May they reverently embrace the legacy of nurturing talent expressed in the ode on luxuriant millet, and take the ancient …

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text:
豪傑自期焉可也昔李唐之
盛閩廣之遐未聞有舉進士
者旣而於閩得歐陽詹於廣
得張九齡文章相業光昭汗
簡至今其地號詩書之府其
士挹歐張之風不衰諸君子
生長之地亦旣相若矣行將
===
===
試禮闈策
大庭服官序有日矣其亦爭自磨
濯而動念於斯否乎若夫志
伊學顏為國華彩而上不負
天子焉則又主司者之深願也寧
不為科目之光哉
江西廣信府弋陽縣儒學訓
punctuated:
豪傑自期焉可也。昔李唐之盛，閩廣之遐，未聞有舉進士者。旣而於閩得歐陽詹，於廣得張九齡，文章相業，光昭汗簡。至今其地號詩書之府，其士挹歐張之風不衰。諸君子生長之地，亦旣相若矣。行將試禮闈，策大庭，服官序有日矣。其亦爭自磨濯，而動念於斯否乎？若夫志伊學顏，為國華彩，而上不負天子焉，則又主司者之深願也，寧不為科目之光哉？

江西廣信府弋陽縣儒學訓
translation_en:
…it is fitting that you aspire to be heroes of such stature. In the flourishing days of the Tang dynasty of the Li house, no one from distant Min and Guang was yet known to have attained the jinshi degree. Subsequently, Min produced Ouyang Zhan, and Guang produced Zhang Jiuling; their literary achievements and accomplishments in the chief councillorship shone brilliantly in the historical annals. To this day, those regions are called repositories of poetry and classical learning, and their scholars continue to draw upon the example of Ouyang and Zhang. The land where you gentlemen were born and raised is comparable to theirs. Soon you will sit the Metropolitan Examination in the Ministry of Rites examination compound and answer policy questions at the Palace Examination; the day when you take your places in official service is approaching. Will you not strive to polish and purify yourselves, keeping these examples in mind? As for aspiring to be like Yi Yin and learning as Yan Hui did, bringing glory to the state and proving worthy of the Son of Heaven above—this is also the profound hope of those presiding over the examination. Would this not bring honor to the examination system?

The Instructor of the Confucian School of Yiyang County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi…

title: 嘉靖十六年雲南鄉試錄
text: 導穆旺謹序
punctuated: 導穆旺謹序。
translation_en: …Assistant Instructor Mu Wang respectfully composed this preface.
